# Cross-Plan Dependency Graph and Ownership Map

## Purpose

Define the canonical build order, shared-resource ownership, and inter-plan dependencies so that implementation agents can execute plans in the correct sequence without discovering conflicts at build time.

## How to Use This Document

1. **Before starting any plan**: check its Dependencies row in the plan header. All listed plans must be complete.
2. **Before creating a table or directory**: check the Ownership Maps below. Only the owning plan issues `CREATE`. Dependent plans `EXTEND` with an explicit dependency declaration.
3. **Build order**: follow the Canonical Build Order (Section 5). Each tier's prerequisites are the prior tier's completion.

---

## 1. Table Ownership Map

These tables are claimed by multiple plans. The table below resolves each conflict.

| Table | Owning Plan (CREATE) | Extending Plan(s) (ALTER/USE) | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `session_memberships` | Plan-001 (Shared Session Core) | Plan-002 (Invite Membership And Presence) | Plan-001 is the session foundation; Spec-002 depends on Spec-001. Plan-001 creates the table with core columns (id, session_id, participant_id, role, state, joined_at, updated_at). Plan-002 adds invite-driven membership flows but does not own the schema. |
| `branch_contexts` | Plan-010 (Worktree Lifecycle And Execution Modes) | Plan-011 (Gitflow PR And Diff Attribution) | Plan-011 already declares Plan-010 as a dependency. Plan-010 creates the table as the polymorphic writable-root carrier (id, workspace_id FK NOT NULL, worktree_id FK nullable, ephemeral_clone_id FK nullable + at-most-one CHECK, base_branch, head_branch, upstream_ref, created_at, updated_at — Tier-6 audit, Plan-010 D-010-5). Plan-011 extends it for PR and diff attribution and imports `BranchContextId` per Plan-010 CP-010-6. |
| `participant_keys` (SQLite) | Plan-001 (initial migration `0001-initial.ts`) | Plan-022 (schema origin and CRUD code paths) | **Forward-declared split per Plan-022 header.** Plan-022 authors the `participant_keys` schema but forward-declares the `CREATE TABLE` into Plan-001's Tier 1 migration so V1 session-core cannot ship without the GDPR crypto-envelope schema (per ADR-015 V1 scope). Plan-022's implementation code paths (store, rotation, wrap-codec) land at Tier 5. |
| `session_events.pii_payload` (SQLite column) | Plan-001 (initial migration `0001-initial.ts`) | Plan-022 (column origin; **codec** code path at Tier 5) | **Forward-declared split per Plan-022 header.** Plan-022 adds this BLOB column to Plan-001's `session_events` schema in the Tier 1 migration so the crypto envelope does not require a breaking schema migration after V1 ships. **Write-mechanism vs codec (Tier-5 audit).** The sole **write-path** is Plan-006's `pii-indirection.ts` (Tier 4 — structural sole-write enforcement via the branded `PiiPayloadCiphertext` type, CP-006-1); Plan-022 owns the **codec** (Tier 5 — the AES-256-GCM encrypt/decrypt that produces/consumes the ciphertext the indirection layer writes). Distinct concerns: Plan-006 gates _who may write_ the column, Plan-022 supplies _the cipher_. |
| `session_events.{monotonic_ns,prev_hash,row_hash,daemon_signature,participant_signature}` (SQLite columns) | Plan-001 (initial migration `0001-initial.ts`) | Plan-006 (column origin; integrity-protocol semantics + writer/verifier code paths at Tier 4) | **Forward-declared split per `Spec-006 §Integrity Protocol`.** Plan-001 ships the physical CREATE of these columns in the Tier 1 initial migration so the integrity protocol does not require a breaking schema migration after V1 ships. Plan-006 owns the column semantics (monotonic-clock allocation, hash-chain construction, dual-signature mechanics) and the writer/verifier code paths at Tier 4. Plan-003 emits `runtime_node.*` events into this surface at Tier 3, but the events conform to the column shape Plan-001 ships — Plan-003 does not author the integrity-protocol semantics. |
| `daemon_signing_keys` (SQLite table, Plan-006-owned, sealed-Ed25519-private-key store) | Plan-006 (additive migration at Tier 4 Phase 2 — `0005-daemon-signing-keys.ts`; new local SQLite table) | Production composition root (leg A — invokes `DaemonSigningKeyProvisioner.create(sessionId)` at the daemon's local session-establishment per CP-006-7) + Plan-006 T4.10 (leg B — registers the returned public key in the control-plane `daemon_signing_public_keys` verification-key roster at session admission per CP-003-5; post-attach 2026-07-29–2026-08-11, decoupled from attach by the 2026-08-11 admission-time registration decoupling) + Plan-008 T-008r-4-14 (leg C — the **CP-008-15 store-lineage extension**, 2026-08-12 Codex PR #323 round 3: PK widened `(session_id, node_id)` + `superseded_at_sequence` succession watermark via a Plan-008-shipped additive lineage migration, the watermark stamped by leg B's registration hook when a fresh `NodeId` takes over a carried-forward store, so the `Spec-008 §Peer History Backfill On Join (V1)` serving selector labels origin-authored rows durably; reciprocal at Plan-006 §Cross-Plan Amendments) | **Plan-006 audit F-006-2-02 resolution (hardened-mode, user-ratified 2026-05-28); revised post-Codex T4 review on PR #124.** Daemon-private signing keys are local-machine secrets and MUST live in local SQLite (per ADR-004 SQLite-Local-State boundary). They are NEVER stored in shared Postgres `sessions` (the original pre-T4-review row mis-located the column there — corrected to a new local-SQLite table here). Plan-006 Phase 2 T2.7 ships the `DaemonSigningKeySource` interface + `OsKeystoreSealedDaemonSigningKeySource` implementation, which generates the per-session Ed25519 keypair and seals the private half through an INJECTED `DaemonSigningKeySealer` boundary rather than sealing it itself; stored as ciphertext in the new local `daemon_signing_keys.sealed_private_key` BLOB column keyed by `session_id`. Plan-022 (Tier 5) ships that sealer AND specifies the column's byte format per CP-006-11 — sealing under the OS-keystore-managed master key (Keychain `kSecAttrAccessibleWhenUnlockedThisDeviceOnly` on macOS / `CRED_TYPE_GENERIC` `CRED_PERSIST_LOCAL_MACHINE` on Windows / Secret Service via libsecret + kwallet6 + keyutils fallback on Linux per [Spec-022 §Daemon Master Key](../specs/022-data-retention-and-gdpr.md#daemon-master-key)), accessed through the `@napi-rs/keyring` v1.2.0 cross-platform shim (`keytar` superseded — unmaintained). No tier inversion: the Plan-022 dependency runs through the injected interface, so Plan-006's module imports nothing from Plan-022 and pulls no native binding into the append path's consumers. (The 2026-05-28 ratification reached the same no-inversion conclusion from the stronger premise of no Plan-022 dependency at all; that premise is superseded in part 2026-07-27, PR #256 — the conclusion is not.) **Re-vehicled 2026-07-29 (the CP-006-7 two-leg correction).** The former "Plan-002 (Tier 1, closed) reopens via amendment-via-extension PR per CP-002-N" clause was a double misattribution carrying an unminted placeholder id — Plan-002 (Tier 2, invites/membership/presence) owns no session-create surface and its file never carried a reciprocal. The call-site (leg A) binds at the first production composition root that wires T3.1's durable append path, in the CP-006-1 assertion-pattern shape with T3.1's null-key fail-closed throw as backstop; the roster public-key registration (leg B) is Plan-006 T4.10 at session admission (post-attach until the 2026-08-11 decoupling) — a new idempotent control-plane procedure pair (`runtimenode.signingkeyregister` / `runtimenode.signingkeyroster`) over the new Plan-006-owned erasure-durable `daemon_signing_public_keys` table per CP-003-5, register-once with different-key refusal; no shipped attach wire shape or `runtime_node_attachments` column is touched (no master-key crypto crosses either boundary; `create` returns the public key only). `Spec-006 §Canonical Serialization Rules` (the daemon public key is resolved from the session participant roster by NodeId for signature verification) is the governing semantic for EXTERNAL verifiers; the daemon-local verifier (T4.1) checking rows it authored resolves its own `session_id`-keyed store — the NodeId = self arm. **Companion delivery table — RETIRED (registered 2026-08-01 at Codex PR #278 rounds 2–3; deleted 2026-08-11 by the admission-time registration decoupling):** the `daemon_attachment_deliveries` table existed solely to make the attach response's server-minted attachment binding restart-survivable for the T4.10 registrar's attempt precondition; the decoupling deleted that precondition outright (the register request presents no `attachmentId`), so the table, its `0NNN-attachment-deliveries.ts` migration + runner block, and its sole write path `attachment-delivery-store.ts` were removed doc-only — none ever shipped. This table stays key-material-only with T2.7's module its sole production write path. |
| `session_events.retention_class` (SQLite column, `TEXT` nullable; `'audit_stub'` discriminator) | Plan-006 (additive migration at Tier 4 Phase 3 — `0009-retention-class-and-stub-signature.ts`, shipped 2026-08-04 via PR #287) | None (Plan-006-internal: compactor T3.2 writes; replay-service T4.3 reads; verifier T4.1 keys compacted-row verification off it) | **Plan-006 audit F-006-3-02 resolution (hardened-mode, Phase 3 Design B).** Compactor (T3.2) sets `retention_class = 'audit_stub'` after compacting a row's payload to the audit-stub form per [Spec-006 §Compacted Event Format](../specs/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#compacted-event-format). A typed column (vs JSON-field probe inside `payload`) keeps hot-path replay-window construction fast and lets the compactor selector exclude already-stubbed rows via `WHERE retention_class IS NULL` for re-compaction guards. The partial index `idx_session_events_live` (`session_events(session_id, sequence) WHERE retention_class IS NULL`) ships in that same migration — creatable only there, its predicate referencing the column the migration adds — serving both compactor candidate-range queries and hot-path replay. |
| `session_events.stub_signature` (SQLite column, `BLOB` nullable; 64-byte Ed25519) | Plan-006 (additive migration at Tier 4 Phase 3 — `0009-retention-class-and-stub-signature.ts`, same migration as `retention_class`) | None (Plan-006-internal: compactor T3.2 writes; verifier T4.1 re-verifies) | **Plan-006 post-compaction stub-authenticity resolution (hardened-mode; Codex PR #124 round-2 P1, 2026-05-28).** Per-row commitment to the surviving audit-stub bytes: the compactor (T3.2) signs `canonical_bytes(audit-stub projection)` with the daemon session key and stores the 64-byte signature here; the verifier (T4.1) re-verifies it against the row's CURRENT stub bytes — tampered/replayed/missing → `failureMode: 'stub_signature_invalid'`. Closes the gap where the round-1 anchor (which commits only to the ORIGINAL `row_hash`) could not detect a post-compaction edit of the visible stub. A companion **scalar-binding check** (verifier T4.1; Codex PR #124 round-5 P1, 2026-05-28) additionally binds the surviving scalar columns (`category`/`type`/`actor`/`occurred_at`, plus `id`/`session_id`/`sequence`) to the signed `payload` projection — a scalar edited to diverge from the projection (which `stub_signature` alone cannot catch, since it signs only `payload`) → `failureMode: 'stub_scalar_mismatch'`. NULL for live (`retention_class IS NULL`) rows. See [Spec-006 §Post-Compaction Integrity](../specs/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#post-compaction-integrity). |
| `session_events.pii_participant_id` (SQLite column, `TEXT` nullable; the durable PII owner stamp) | Plan-006 (additive migration at Tier 4 Phase 3 — `0007-pii-participant-id.ts`, shipped 2026-08-04 via PR #287; T3.1's own append-path migration, distinct from the T3.2 compaction migration above) | Plan-022 (read-only consumer at Path-1 shred — `Spec-022 §Shred Fan-Out` Path 1's SQL scope selector keys off this stamp rather than the opaque ciphertext — and bound by CP-006-12 to preserve it; no ALTER, no write) | **Plan-006 PII-owner-stamp binding resolution (hardened-mode; Codex PR #256 round-4 P1, 2026-07-27).** The durable half of the owner stamp: T2.4's `pii-indirection.ts` projects the PII owner's participant id into the signed `payload` under `PII_PARTICIPANT_ID_PAYLOAD_KEY`, and T3.1's append path writes that SAME id into this column on the same write — so `daemon_signature` binds WHOSE ciphertext a row holds, not only WHICH bytes (the `pii_ciphertext_digest` half, I-006-2-11). Without the column the signed claim is its own only copy and the binding is unenforceable: T2.4's exported `isPiiOwnerStampBound` compares column against claim, and T4.1 runs it as a POSTCONDITION of a green `verifyRow` — the claim lives inside the bytes that check authenticates — reporting `failureMode: 'pii_owner_stamp_unbound'` per I-006-2-12. NULL on every row with no `pii_payload`. What the binding buys is post-shred attribution: once [Spec-022 §Shred Fan-Out](../specs/022-data-retention-and-gdpr.md#shred-fan-out) Path 1 destroys the per-participant key no decrypt can re-attribute the retained ciphertext, so the stamp is at once the sole surviving evidence of whose data the row held and Path 1's own scope selector — which is why CP-006-12 binds Plan-022 to preserve BOTH `pii_payload` and this column. Whether a COMPACTED row retains the stamp is settled as of 2026-08-04 (the signed CLAIM always retires — the stub projection replaces `payload` wholesale with a field set carrying no PII members): T3.1's migration created the column and T3.2's compactor clears it alongside `pii_payload` in the same stub-write statement, the disposition [Spec-006 §Compacted Event Format](../specs/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#compacted-event-format) now carries in its removal list. See [Spec-006 §Canonical Serialization Rules](../specs/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#canonical-serialization-rules), which assigns the column to T3.1 by name. |
| `session_events.received_from_node_id` (SQLite column, `TEXT` nullable; the received-row provenance marker) | Plan-008 (additive migration at Tier 5 R4 — `0NNN-received-row-provenance.ts`, T-008r-4-14, with its same-commit `migration-runner.ts` registration; column registered 2026-08-11 by the Plan-008/Spec-008 restoring targeted readiness-audit delta, PR #323 / §6 NS-58) | Plan-006 (semantics owner via the [Spec-006 §Canonical Serialization Rules](../specs/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#canonical-serialization-rules) 2026-08-11 amendment — the conditional `receivedFromNodeId` canonical member in receiver-signed bytes, the stub-projection carriage, and the T4.1 verifier's provenance dispatch of both PII binding modes: the compare on origin rows, a require-absent arm on received rows; reads and enforces, never ALTERs) | **Received-row provenance split (`Spec-008 §Peer History Backfill On Join (V1)` / Plan-008 CP-008-13).** NULL = origin-authored — servable on backfill, the possession-scoped serving selector `received_from_node_id IS NULL` (Plan-008 I-008-13(a)); non-NULL = the origin `NodeId` whose roster key verified the bytes at receive — a received row is re-sequenced and re-signed by its receiver and therefore unservable. Plan-008 owns the durable column because backfill is the surface that needs it; Spec-006 owns what the marker means inside the canonical bytes and the stub projection. The emission + stamping + stub-preservation seam edits inside Plan-006's `events/` module (see the §2 row) land with T-008r-4-14 under CP-008-13, the CP-003-5 per-file-crossing shape. |
| `session_events.content_payload` (SQLite column, `BLOB` nullable; the durable encrypted home for machine-authored prose) | Plan-006 (additive migration at Phase 3B — `0NNN-content-payload.ts`, T3.6, with its same-commit `migration-runner.ts` registration; ordinal deliberately unpinned because ordinals are claimed in merge order, the `received_from_node_id` placeholder idiom) | Plan-005 (**consumer only** — CP-005-13 ⇄ CP-006-15; T3.20's canonical-transcript replay reads the column and authors nothing on Plan-006's side, taking a task-scoped dispatch hold on Phase 3B instead), Plan-022 (**inventory only** — the [Spec-022 §PII Data Map](../specs/022-data-retention-and-gdpr.md#pii-data-map) durable-tier row and its export/retention disposition, on a recorded no-flip; Plan-022 owns no write path here) | **Plan-006-created, not Plan-001 forward-declared** — the `pii_participant_id` precedent, and deliberately so: this column is not part of the v1 schema Plan-001 shipped, and retrofitting it into `0001-initial.ts` would rewrite a merged migration. Sealed under a **session**-scoped key — a random DEK looked up by `session_id` in `session_content_keys` and unwrapped under the daemon master key, never derived from it (I-006-3-08) — so unlike `pii_payload` it carries **no owner-stamp sibling column** — `session_id` is already a canonical signed member — and no participant selector reaches it. Sole write path is Plan-006's `events/pii-indirection.ts`, which houses both codecs so the Encrypt-Then-Digest-Then-Sign order has one home rather than two. NULL by construction on `audit_integrity` / `event_maintenance` rows, and cleared at compaction alongside `pii_payload`. Added 2026-08-30, §6 node NS-94. |
| `session_content_keys` (SQLite table; the wrapped per-session content DEK) | Plan-006 (`CREATE` in the same additive Phase-3B migration as the column — T3.6, with `session-content-key-store.ts` as its sole reader/minter; added 2026-08-30 at the PR #383 round-1 fold, replacing a master-key derivation that rotate-on-shred would have destroyed) | Plan-022 (**inventory + rotation only** — [Spec-022](../specs/022-data-retention-and-gdpr.md)' rotate-on-shred step 2 re-wraps this table inside its **existing** `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE` alongside `participant_keys`; Plan-022 owns no write path here and took a recorded no-flip, the re-wrap entry point being Plan-006's) | Mirrors `participant_keys.encrypted_key_blob` rather than inventing a custody shape. Keyed by session because a machine-authored body is work product every member co-owns and has no participant to key on; destroying it is therefore **not** a shred. |

### Lock Ordering Across Shared Tables

Plans that touch more than one of the §1 contested or co-extended tables in a single transaction MUST acquire row locks in the order documented below to avoid cross-plan deadlocks. Adding a new caller is not sufficient grounds to deviate; reordering requires a coordinated change to all callers under the affected order. A plan that locks two of its **own** uncontested tables in one transaction registers that order here as well (2026-09-01, NS-99 Codex round 5) — the ordering discipline is worth exactly one home, and a per-plan copy is how two homes start.

| Tables Locked Together | Order | Authority | Affected Callers |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `sessions`, `session_memberships` | `sessions` → `session_memberships` | Plan-001 docstring at [`packages/control-plane/src/sessions/session-directory-service.ts`](../../packages/control-plane/src/sessions/session-directory-service.ts) (`createSession` "Lock-acquisition order" paragraph) | Plan-002 ownership-transfer, co-owner promotion, and invite-accept paths (any flow that mutates `session_memberships` while validating `sessions`) |
| `sessions`, `session_memberships`, `daemon_signing_public_keys` | `sessions` → `session_memberships` → `daemon_signing_public_keys` | Plan-006 T4.10 register transaction (registered 2026-07-31 at the CP-006-7 amendment, PR #274 round 3; `session_memberships` joined at round 4's active-membership predicate; the `runtime_node_attachments` `FOR SHARE` level — level 3 of the order as registered — was DELETED 2026-08-11 by the admission-time registration decoupling, no attachment row existing at admission time to read; lands with `signing-key-service.ts`). `sessions` is taken explicitly FIRST even though only read: the final INSERT's `session_id` FK acquires an implicit `FOR KEY SHARE` on `sessions`, and skipping a level in a total order is sound only when nothing later in the transaction acquires the skipped level implicitly — the same rule the shipped attach path applies. Modes are weakest-sufficient: `sessions` `FOR SHARE` (conflicts with a future floor raise's `FOR NO KEY UPDATE`; `FOR KEY SHARE` would be a silent no-op guard **for that floor-serialization purpose** — it is sufficient, and is the registered mode, on a surface that needs only the row's existence, per the runtime-node registrant row below), `session_memberships` `FOR SHARE` (an authorization READ — the transaction writes nothing to that table, so Plan-003 I-003-3 holds; `FOR SHARE` is the weakest mode conflicting with the `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` a `MembershipService` suspend/revoke `UPDATE` acquires, so a revocation cannot commit between the authorization read and the key INSERT; no deadlock against `updateMembership`, which serializes at level 1 on its `sessions` `FOR UPDATE`) | Plan-006 T4.10 `runtimenode.signingkeyregister` only in V1 — since round 4 it instantiates the full order (four levels as registered; three since the 2026-08-11 decoupling deleted the attachment level). The level-2 slot it reserved for the BL-141 runtime-node mutator extension is **no longer a reservation**: that extension is registered as the row below ([ADR-025](../decisions/025-runtime-node-control-plane-caller-authorization.md), ratified 2026-08-10, registered 2026-08-12), joining the same `session_memberships` `FOR SHARE` level at the same relative order with nothing re-ordered |
| `sessions`, `session_memberships`, `runtime_node_attachments` | `sessions` → `session_memberships` → `runtime_node_attachments` | [ADR-025 D8](../decisions/025-runtime-node-control-plane-caller-authorization.md) (ratified 2026-08-10, registered 2026-08-12; Plan-003 I-003-6 makes it binding; lands with `classify-caller.ts` + the `runtime-nodes/` services under Plan-003 T3.10–T3.11). A **prefix-consistent extension** of the order above, not a competing declaration — the two registrants share levels 1–2 in the same relative order, and this one continues to `runtime_node_attachments`, the level the row above occupied until the 2026-08-11 decoupling deleted it; the union across both registrants is the canonical `sessions` → `session_memberships` → `runtime_node_attachments` → `daemon_signing_public_keys` sequence, and a transaction may skip a level it does not need, which is sound only because nothing later in these transactions acquires a skipped level implicitly. Modes are weakest-sufficient per [PostgreSQL Table 13.3](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/current/explicit-locking.html): `sessions` `FOR KEY SHARE` on the `attach` path — it blocks the `DELETE` or key-changing `UPDATE` that would falsify the existence check, which is all `attach` needs, and it is the same mode the upsert's own foreign key takes implicitly, so no lock upgrade occurs; it deliberately does **not** conflict with the `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` a version-floor raise acquires, which is acceptable **only** because the read-only verdict is derived and never persisted (the attachment stores `client_version`, and every later verdict site re-derives against the then-current floor), so a lost floor race yields one stale response field and never durable corruption — a surface needing the floor verdict authoritative-at-write takes `FOR SHARE` instead, as the registration surface above does and as `runtimenode.capabilityupdate`'s version-floor write-gate does; `session_memberships` `FOR SHARE` — an authorization **read**, weakest mode conflicting with the `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` a `MembershipService` suspend/revoke `UPDATE` acquires, so a revocation cannot commit between classification and mutation, and `FOR KEY SHARE` here would be a silent no-op guard with no runtime detector; `runtime_node_attachments` `FOR NO KEY UPDATE` on mutator paths (`state` sits only in a **partial** unique index, which the `FOR UPDATE`-escalation column set excludes, so the mutating `UPDATE`s take that mode natively and matching it is sufficient), `FOR SHARE` on read-only authorization. **Two-phase resolve** is mandatory for the `nodeId`-keyed procedures, which cannot know their `session_id` before reading the attachment: unlocked pre-read → locks in canonical order → re-verify the locked row's `(session_id, participant_id)` against the pre-read snapshot, failing closed on mismatch. Locking the attachment first to learn the session would invert levels 3 and 1–2 and deadlock ABBA against `attach`. | Plan-003 `runtimenode.attach` (levels 1→2→3), `runtimenode.heartbeat` (levels 2→3 — it reads no version floor, so it skips level 1; skipping is order-consistent and creates no ABBA cycle; its level-3 acquisition is the read-only `FOR SHARE` arm, its mutation targeting `runtime_node_presence` outside this order), `runtimenode.capabilityupdate` (levels 1→2→3), `runtimenode.detach` (levels 2→3). `runtimenode.roster` takes **no lock and no transaction** — its membership predicate and projection are one `READ COMMITTED` statement, hence one snapshot, the shape `runtimenode.signingkeyroster` already ships |
| `webauthn_challenges`, `webauthn_credentials` | `webauthn_challenges` → `webauthn_credentials` | [Plan-018 I-018-19](../plans/018-identity-and-participant-state.md#invariants) (registered 2026-09-01 at the NS-99 Codex round-5 fold; lands with Plan-018 Phase 6 T6.3/T6.4). Both tables are Plan-018-uncontested, and the row is here rather than in that plan alone under the preamble's own-tables clause. The order follows the ceremony: the challenge is consumed by a `DELETE ... RETURNING` before the credential row is taken `FOR UPDATE` for the counter advance, so a caller that locked the credential first would hold it across the fence for no reason and invert the two levels against any later sibling. | Plan-018 T6.3 (verify legs; the only transaction that touches both) |

### Ownership Rule

The owning plan creates the directory structure and any shared types or base services. Extending plans add new files but must not modify files owned by the creating plan without an explicit contract (interface, type export, or extension point).

**Housekeeping Exception.** An extending plan MAY fix-in-place an owned file in the surfacing PR (rather than serializing through a precursor PR owned by the creating plan) IFF:

- (a) the defect is type-level or structural-only with zero runtime or behavioral change,
- (b) the defect was first discoverable via the extending plan's composition (the extender is the first surfacer),
- (c) the fix is sub-30-LOC + sub-day in scope,
- (d) the change is one-time correction — not an ongoing edit claim on the owned file, AND
- (e) the exception is documented inline in the extending plan's `§Cross-Plan Amendments` section, with rationale citing which of (a)–(d) apply.

The intent is to avoid cross-plan PR-coordination ceremony for sub-day, low-risk fixes that the extender's own work surfaced. Rigid serialization through a precursor PR remains the default for behavioral changes, multi-day fixes, or anything that claims ongoing edit rights on the owned file. A §6 NS-XX cross-reference entry is RECOMMENDED when the cross-plan touch is load-bearing for downstream dependency planning, but is not required for purely tactical type-fix amendments.

Behavioral changes to shipped owned code are not covered by this exception — they take the post-completion enhancement lane (CONTRIBUTING.md §How Code Lands lane 2), or a spec/plan amendment first when they alter the behavior contract (lane 4).

**Precedent.** [Plan-002 §Cross-Plan Amendments](../plans/002-invite-membership-and-presence.md#cross-plan-amendments) records PR #102's Amendment 1 (`packages/contracts/src/internal/branded.ts` extraction + `packages/contracts/src/session.ts` refactor — type-level only, surfaced during T1.1 implementation, sub-30-LOC) and Amendment 2 (`packages/control-plane/src/sessions/migration-runner.ts` per-version-loop wiring — structural-only, surfaced during Phase D code review, sub-30-LOC).

Each dependency is annotated with its type:

- **spec-declared**: the corresponding spec explicitly lists the other spec in its Depends On field
- **implementation-derived**: the plans share tables, package paths, or cross-cutting concerns that create a build-order dependency not captured in spec Depends On
- **declared in plan header**: the dependency is declared in the target plan's header Dependencies row — not in the spec's Depends On field, and not an implementation-derived table-sharing relationship

## 5. Canonical Build Order

Implementation must follow this tier sequence. Plans in a tier can generally run in parallel, but some tiers contain intra-tier ordering noted in the Prerequisites column. All plans in a tier must complete before the next tier begins. Tier sequencing governs plan-task shipment (CONTRIBUTING.md §How Code Lands lane 1); post-completion enhancements and repo tooling changes are not tier-gated.

V1 scope is 23 features per [ADR-015: V1 Feature Scope Definition](../decisions/015-v1-feature-scope-definition.md) (amended 2026-07-02 per the capability-enhancement campaign — 17 features per the earlier 2026-04-22 BL-097 workflow V1.1→V1 amendment; amended 2026-07-08 — cross-node shared artifacts pulled from V1.1 into V1 as feature-14 scope growth, landing as Plan-014 Tasks 7–10, whose readiness-audit delta landed 2026-08-12 and restored that plan and Spec-014 `approved` — the §6 NS-59 node records it, and the remaining gate is Tier-7 order; phase decomposition delivered 2026-08-15. Plan-014 and Spec-014 were flipped and restored `approved` again 2026-08-16 by the artifact-lifecycle amendment and its in-swap targeted readiness-audit delta — §6 node NS-64 — which added local Tasks 11–13 and re-specified the Task-8 fetch selector, and a third time 2026-08-17 by the ingest-protocol hardening amendment and its in-swap delta — §6 node NS-70, five Codex PR #341 round-5 findings hardened into the ingest stream protocol and the fetch-path `expired` write-back, with BL-152 minted for the flagged TTL-sweep disposition (settled and archived 2026-08-26 — §6 node NS-82); **no feature count moves** and the Tier-7 placement is unchanged). All tiers below are the V1 tier set; feature #18's governing plan ([Plan-028](../plans/028-mcp-server-configuration-and-governance.md)) landed 2026-07-22 via the campaign's B18 bundle (Task 24) and holds its Tier 7 row below — a Tier-7 leaf (every gating upstream edge resolves by Tier 6 end; the one within-Tier-7 edge — Plan-015's recovery-attach admission seam — is order-independent by its vacuous default, and nothing depends on Plan-028) whose code dispatches only after its targeted readiness audit promotes it out of `draft` per its §Preconditions. ### Plan-007 Substrate-vs-Namespace Carve-Out (Tier 1 / Tier 4)

Plan-001 Phase 5 (`packages/client-sdk/src/sessionClient.ts` `create` / `read` / `join` / `subscribe` over the daemon transport) consumes the Spec-007 wire substrate (JSON-RPC 2.0 + LSP-style Content-Length framing, 1MB max-message-size, protocol-version negotiation, error model, supervision hooks per `Spec-007 §Wire Format`) plus the `session.*` JSON-RPC method namespace. Spec-007 conflates two concerns — the cross-cutting _transport substrate_ (correctly single-owned by Plan-007) and the domain-specific _method namespaces_ (`session.*`, `run.*`, `repo.*`, `artifact.*`, `settings.*`, `daemon.*`) which cohere with their owning plans. **Resolution: Plan-007-partial** — the `Spec-007 §Wire Format` substrate (`packages/runtime-daemon/src/ipc/local-ipc-gateway.ts`, `protocol-negotiation.ts`), the bind-time Spec-027 substrate (`packages/runtime-daemon/src/bootstrap/secure-defaults.ts`, `packages/runtime-daemon/src/bootstrap/secure-defaults-events.ts` — validation scope limited to the loopback OS-local socket bind path Tier 1 exposes), the `session.*` method namespace only, and the SDK Zod layer (~500–1000 LOC per `Spec-007 §Wire Format`) — lands at Tier 1 alongside Plan-001 to unblock Phase 5. **Plan-007-remainder** (the `settings.*` + `daemon.*` JSON-RPC namespaces, the Spec-027 surfaces that widen alongside additional bind paths — `tls-surface.ts`, `first-run-keys.ts`, `update-notify.ts`, and the CLI `self-update` dual-verification command — and the CLI + desktop-shell supervision surfaces) ships at the original Tier 4 slot. The `run.*` / `repo.*` / `artifact.*` namespaces are owned by their downstream plans — Plan-004 (Tier 5) / Plan-009 (Tier 6) / Plan-014 (Tier 7) — and register their handlers under Plan-007's namespace registry at the consuming plan's tier per the Plan-002 `presence.*` precedent (NS-26), exactly as Plan-005's `driver.*` and Plan-006's `event.*` do (§3): Plan-007 owns the registry surface, not these namespaces' handlers. The `session.*` namespace is not duplicated at Tier 4; Plan-007-remainder extends the registry with its `settings.*` + `daemon.*` namespaces.

This establishes the **substrate-vs-namespace decomposition pattern** as a reusable methodology rule — see `Plan-007 §Execution Windows (V1 Carve-Out)`. The rule: cross-cutting infrastructure plans MAY be split into a Tier-N substrate-deliverable + a Tier-M namespace-deliverable when (a) the substrate is single-owned and load-bearing for an earlier-tier consumer, AND (b) the namespaces have natural cohesion with their owning plans. Substrate ships first; namespaces ship with their owning plans.

Operational admission for substrate phases routes through the `audit_status: substrate_exempt` phase-level precondition per [runbook §Per-Phase Audit Semantics](../operations/plan-implementation-readiness-audit-runbook.md#per-phase-audit-semantics). A substrate phase qualifies only when (1) it is covered by a §5 carve-out, (2) it ships substrate-only files, AND (3) it covers no Spec-NNN acceptance criteria (criterion (3) is the mechanically-checked operative filter — preflight rejects substrate claims that ship `Spec coverage:` cites in their Tasks block). The plan-level audit checkbox stays unchecked until the plan's later-tier remainder audit completes; until then the plan stays in `approved` status with the checkbox deferred via the `substrate_exempt` declaration on the affected phases.

### Plan-008 Bootstrap-vs-Remainder Carve-Out (Tier 1 / Tier 5)

Plan-001 Phase 5's `sessionClient.subscribe` over the control-plane transport requires the tRPC v11 server skeleton plus an SSE transport for `SessionSubscribe` (the contract is request-only on the wire — the response is an `AsyncIterable<EventEnvelope>` SSE stream per `packages/contracts/src/session.ts#SessionSubscribeRequest`). Plan-001 Phase 4 already shipped the underlying `packages/control-plane/src/sessions/session-directory-service.ts` at Tier 1; what's missing is the HTTP transport that exposes it. **Resolution: Plan-008-bootstrap** — the tRPC v11 server skeleton (Cloudflare Workers via `@trpc/server/adapters/fetch` per [ADR-014](../decisions/014-trpc-control-plane-api.md) and BL-104 resolution 2026-04-30; local dev uses workerd via `wrangler dev`), the `sessionRouter` HTTP handlers wrapping the existing `session-directory-service.ts`, and the SSE substrate for `SessionSubscribe` (produced natively by tRPC's shared `resolveResponse.ts` substrate when invoked through `fetchRequestHandler`) — lands at Tier 1 alongside Plan-001 to unblock Phase 5. **Plan-008-remainder** (relay broker, presence register, invite-acceptance handoff, reconnect association, `session_directory` + `relay_connections` + `relay_seen_ephemeral_keys` Postgres tables) ships at the original Tier 5 slot once Plan-002 (invite/presence) is complete. Tier 5 placement of Plan-008-remainder is unchanged because relay coordination depends on Plan-002.

This carve-out follows the same substrate-vs-namespace decomposition rule as Plan-007 above (cross-reference `Plan-007 §Execution Windows (V1 Carve-Out)`): the _transport substrate_ (tRPC server + sessionRouter + SSE plumbing) is what Plan-001 Phase 5 consumes; the _relay/presence behavior_ is what Plan-008 owns canonically. Substrate ships first.

### Plan-023 Substrate-vs-Namespace Carve-Out (Tier 1 / Tier 8)

Plan-001 Phase 5 (`apps/desktop/src/main/sidecar-lifecycle.ts` per CP-001-1 + `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/session-bootstrap/` per T5.2) and Plan-024 Phase 3 (I-024-4 satisfaction integration test at `apps/desktop/src/main/__tests__/sidecar-lifecycle.integration.test.ts`) both extend file content into the `apps/desktop/` directory tree. Plan-023 (Tier 8 canonical) owns that tree — but the tree's bare existence (workspace package + electron-vite toolchain + minimal main/preload/renderer entrypoints) is what Plan-001 Phase 5 + Plan-024 Phase 3 actually consume; the heavy main-process behavior (daemon supervisor, keystore, WebAuthn, auto-updater, deep-link, crash reporter) is what Plan-023 owns canonically and depends on Plan-007 / Plan-018 / Plan-008 / Plan-024 — none of which are at Tier 1. Spec-023 conflates two concerns the same way Spec-007 / Spec-008 did: the cross-cutting _package skeleton substrate_ (correctly single-owned by Plan-023 but standalone — no upstream plan deps) and the domain-specific _shell behavior surface_ which depends on Tier 4–7 plans. **Resolution: Plan-023-partial** — the Tier 1 Partial PR Sequence per [Plan-023 §Tier 1 Partial PR Sequence](../plans/023-desktop-shell-and-renderer.md#tier-1-partial-pr-sequence): `apps/desktop/package.json` + `electron.vite.config.ts` + `apps/desktop/src/main/{index,window}.ts` (minimal entrypoint + `webPreferences`-locked window factory) + `apps/desktop/src/preload/index.ts` (single `contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('sidekicks', bridge)` with stub method bodies) + `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/{main,App}.tsx` (placeholder React mount) + `packages/contracts/src/desktop-bridge.ts` (`SidekicksBridge` interface stub re-exporting Plan-007 daemon types) + `apps/desktop/eslint.config.mjs` (renderer-untrusted import bans) + the `apps/desktop/test/launch.smoke.test.ts` Vitest smoke — lands at Tier 1 alongside Plan-001 to unblock Phase 5 + Plan-024 Phase 3. **Widened 2026-09-01 (§6 node NS-97) by two explicit-label supplements that stay inside the same no-upstream-deps rule:** Phase 1B — `apps/desktop/src/main/protocol.ts` (privileged scheme registration + bundle handler), `apps/desktop/src/main/menu.ts`, the `window.ts` load and auxiliary-window factory, the `main-unit` Vitest project, and the Electron-44 / `better-sqlite3`-13.0.3 pin move (T-023p-1B-1..4, gated only on Phase 1 merged) — and Phase 1C — the `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/console/` tree, the whole Meridian console built over the fixture bridge (T-023p-1C-1..8, gated only on Phase 1B merged). Both sit at Tier 1 precisely because none of their legs consumes a Plan-007 / Plan-018 / Plan-008 / Plan-024 contract: the console's live wires wait on `Plan-023 §Console growth slate` rows and on the Tier-8 phases, and the pin move consumes ADR-016 / ADR-022 alone. Resolves [BL-101](../archive/backlog-archive.md#bl-101-c-3--plan-023-tier-1-partial-substrate-carve-out-mirrors-plan-007-partial--plan-008-bootstrap) (option (a); BL-101 closed 2026-04-30 and archived). **Plan-023-remainder** (full main-process behavior — daemon supervisor, keystore, WebAuthn, auto-updater, DAG fallback, deep-link, crash reporter, build pipeline + fuses + signing + notarization + ASAR digest, full Playwright `_electron` E2E suite, CI gate, release runbook) ships at the original Tier 8 slot. Tier 8 placement of Plan-023-remainder is unchanged because the heavy main-process behavior depends on Plan-007 (daemon contract) + Plan-018 (PASETO tokens) + Plan-008 (control-plane tRPC client) + Plan-024 (PtyHost contract for the supervised daemon). The Plan-001 Phase 1 placeholder `apps/desktop/src/index.ts` (shipped 2026-04-26 in PR #6) is repositioned to the substrate split during Plan-023-partial per its forward-declaration comment ("split into `apps/desktop/src/{main,preload,renderer}/` per the electron-vite zero-config convention" — comment amended in this PR for path-convention consistency with the new architecture-canonical authority).

This carve-out follows the same substrate-vs-namespace decomposition rule as Plan-007 + Plan-008 above: the _package skeleton substrate_ (workspace package + toolchain + minimal entrypoints + bridge stub) is what Plan-001 Phase 5 + Plan-024 Phase 3 consume; the _shell behavior surface_ is what Plan-023 owns canonically. Substrate ships first; behavior ships at the owning plan's tier when its upstream dependencies (Plan-007 / Plan-018 / Plan-008 / Plan-024) are in place. **Architecture-canonical paths — orchestrated 5-axis research synthesis.** The carve-out adopts the electron-vite zero-config convention `apps/desktop/src/{main,preload,renderer}/` per [container-architecture.md §Canonical Implementation Topology](./container-architecture.md#canonical-implementation-topology) and [component-architecture-desktop-app.md §Implementation Home](./component-architecture-desktop-app.md#implementation-home). This canonicalization is grounded in an orchestrated 5-axis primary-source research synthesis (60+ sources surveyed by parallel Opus 4.7 subagents, 2026-04-30): **(A)** electron-vite official Development guide ([electron-vite.org/guide/dev](https://electron-vite.org/guide/dev)) explicitly prescribes `src/{main,preload,renderer}/` as the zero-config-detection layout; **(B)** production OSS app survey (17 apps including Cherry Studio, Chatbox, DeepChat, Feishin, PicGo, Deskreen, LobeChat, Marktext-rewrite) finds 9–10 of 14 verified apps using this layout; **(C)** 22 articles + talks 2024–2026 unanimously back this layout from maintainer-grade sources (alex8088, Spatie Ray, daltonmenezes, Tuui, Forge docs); **(D)** none of the seven major monorepo tools (Turborepo, Nx, pnpm, Yarn, Lerna, Bun, Rush) publish official Electron templates that would override this; **(E)** layout is orthogonal to security posture (Electron security docs, Electronegativity SAST, and security-conscious app layouts impose no constraint). The pivot supersedes (a) Plan-023's earlier `apps/desktop/electron/{main,preload}/` naming, (b) the BL-101 description's `apps/desktop/main/src/...` self-reference, and (c) an interim `apps/desktop/{shell,renderer}/` architecture-canonical that this PR amends in lockstep. The full research artifact set lives transiently under `.agents/tmp/research/electron-app-layout/{A-toolchain-docs,B-production-apps,C-articles-talks,D-monorepo-tooling,E-security-hardening}.md` (gitignored, surface-forward to the [BL-101 archive entry](../archive/backlog-archive.md#bl-101-c-3--plan-023-tier-1-partial-substrate-carve-out-mirrors-plan-007-partial--plan-008-bootstrap) per AGENTS.md transient-research convention).

### Plan-025 Substrate-vs-Namespace Carve-Out (Tier 1 / Tier 7)

Plan-025's `Dependencies` header declares Plan-018 as a dependency (PASETO issuer key publication), but Plan-018 cannot compile without `packages/crypto-paseto/` which Plan-025 owns (`Plan-025 §Risks And Blockers`). Plan-002 Phase 2 has the same problem for invite-token issuance per CP-002-4 (BL-119). **Resolution: Plan-025 Tier 1 Partial** — create `packages/crypto-paseto/` exporting the PASETO v4.public `signV4Public`/`verifyV4Public`/`generateV4PublicKeyPair` AND v4.local `encryptV4Local`/`decryptV4Local` primitives (no symmetric-key generator ships — v4.local callers supply 32 random key bytes; built on `@noble/curves` Ed25519 + `@noble/ciphers` XChaCha20 stream — v4.local is encrypt-then-MAC with BLAKE2b-MAC, **not** XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD — + `@noble/hashes` BLAKE2b-MAC + BLAKE2b-KDF per [ADR-010 §PASETO v4 Implementation Library](../decisions/010-paseto-webauthn-mls-auth.md#paseto-v4-implementation-library)), `KeyRing` rotation surface, and the PASETO RFC conformance vector suites for both primitives — lands at Tier 1 alongside Plan-007-partial / Plan-008-bootstrap / Plan-023-partial. **Plan-025 remainder** (Fastify relay server, `@fastify/websocket` frame handling, PASETO verification middleware, Plan-021 rate-limiter wiring, operator HTTP surface, graceful shutdown, structured logging, config loader, Dockerfile, `docker-compose.yml`, Caddyfile, CI release workflow, operator runbook, and all eight Spec-027 secure-defaults rows) waits for Tier 7 after Plan-008-remainder + Plan-018 + Plan-021 are ready to instantiate. This carve-out follows the same substrate-vs-namespace decomposition rule as Plan-007 + Plan-008 + Plan-023 above: the _crypto primitive substrate_ is what Plan-002 Phase 2 + Plan-018 consume; the _relay deployment surface_ is what Plan-025 owns canonically and ships at Tier 7. BL-119 (option (a), substrate-vs-namespace) resolved 2026-05-20; Plan-002 + Plan-018 dep headers cite "Plan-025 Tier 1 Partial" — header-alignment propagation completed inline with the BL-119 PR.

When that primitive ships, this extension unblocks. | [ADR-017 §Node-Scope Anchor Witnessing](../decisions/017-shared-event-sourcing-scope.md#node-scope-anchor-witnessing-v1-local-only-v11-control-plane-upload); [Spec-006 §Daemon-Scope Event Binding](../specs/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#daemon-scope-event-binding-and-node-scope-anchoring) |
| **Independently verifiable trust path for `signing_key_slot_conflict`** — an authentication channel for the T4.10 registrar's conflict alarm that does not rest on the very key the roster refused. In V1 the alarm row is signed with the refused daemon's local key, so a roster-resolving external verifier sees it only as one more `signature_mismatch` — the wholesale mismatch IS the external signal, and the durable row serves local diagnosis plus the anchor-covered post-repair forensic record. | Plan-006 (the T4.10 registrar conflict-append; the `audit_integrity_failed` sixteenth mode) | **Plan-018 / Plan-003** — the same non-forgeable node-identity key + control-plane resolution surface the row above waits on: a node-scoped attestation key independent of the refused session-scoped signing slot is the trust root that authenticates the conflict record without trusting the refused key. | Adjudicated 2026-08-01 by the Plan-006 T4.10 targeted readiness-audit delta, carried from the PR #274 round-6 review; [Spec-006 §Audit Integrity (`audit_integrity`)](../specs/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#audit-integrity-audit_integrity) (the sixteenth-mode prose records the V1 scoping + this deferral) |
| **Cross-session `key_reuse_detected` observation beyond the daemon-local horizon** — a control-plane-side detector over the full `daemon_signing_public_keys` roster, closing the structural blindness Plan-006 I-006-4-03 records: a daemon-local observer detects a collision only where at least one colliding identity is locally resolvable, so a collision spanning two sessions with no common member is invisible to every V1 observer. V1 deliberately REJECTS control-plane uniqueness enforcement — under global uniqueness an attacker registering a victim's readable public roster key into an attacker-owned slot would permanently lock the victim out (no V1 rotation ceremony exists), and the probe reintroduces the key-existence oracle the register path's refusal collapse prevents — so the V1.1 shape is attributable observation, never registration-time refusal. | Plan-006 (`key_reuse_detected` taxonomy + the I-006-4-03 observable-scope invariant) | **Plan-018 / Plan-003** — the same node-identity + control-plane resolution primitive: an authenticated node-identity roster is what turns a control-plane-side observation into attributable, non-oracle testimony rather than an anonymous key-presence lookup surface. | Adjudicated 2026-08-01 by the Plan-006 T4.10 targeted readiness-audit delta; [Plan-006 §Invariants](../plans/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#invariants) I-006-4-03 (the observable scope, the rejection rationale, and the fail-closed both-identities halt) |
| **Node-granular artifact fetch authorization, attestation binding, and delivery integrity** — three V1 residuals that close on one primitive, all scoped to a compromised node inside a participant's own trust domain, and all **availability- or attribution-class** — none is a confidentiality residual. Restoring it buys: **(a) node-scoped fetch authorization** — `ArtifactFetchAuthorize` mints at participant granularity in V1 because its access token carries `sub` + `cnf` and no node claim, so the issuer cannot tell which of a participant's attached nodes is calling (the multi-node authorize path's selector is **no longer owed** — it was specified 2026-08-16 as the caller's key-thumbprint set, which disambiguates among a participant's own nodes and is **explicitly not a closure for this row**: a compromised same-participant sibling holds its own durable key and resolves its own row exactly as designed, so participant-granular minting is untouched and this residual stands as written); **(b) attestation integrity** — V1 artifact-key attestations verify only as signed by _some_ identity key registered to that participant (each workstation holds its own, separately registered), and nothing binds the signing identity to the `node_id` it attests, so any participant-authorized registered identity can bind an attacker-held X25519 key to a victim node's `node_id`. The harm is **victim-node lockout plus corrupted attestation and delivery attribution — not confidentiality** (reclassified 2026-08-08 at PR #301 round 3): an attached sibling is already an intended recipient holding that CEK under its own attested key, so the spoof widens no plaintext reach, and plaintext reach by an authorized node is participant-granularity sharing working as designed. What the primitive restores is binding the **signer** to the attested `node_id` — deliberately **not** node-level content exclusion, which no named V1.1 primitive defines; **(c) delivery-attribution integrity** — the `ArtifactFetchComplete` ack proves no CEK unwrap, so a compromised sibling can forge it, drive refcount-zero GC, and destroy the blob with no remedy while the publisher is offline (an **availability** residual against the ADR-015 offline-availability property). | Plan-014 (`ArtifactFetchAuthorize` / `ArtifactFetchComplete`, the artifact-key attestation path, `artifact_relay_recipients` delivery state) | **Plan-018 / Plan-003** — the same non-forgeable node-identity key + control-plane resolution surface the three rows above wait on. It is the single primitive all three legs need: an issuer-resolvable node identity to scope the mint to, a node-held signing key to bind attestations to instead of the shared participant key, and an ack authenticated as the node whose row it clears. | Adjudicated 2026-08-08 by the I-014-10 node-attach-context re-scope, from the PR #301 round-1 review; [Spec-014 §Cross-Node Artifact Relay (V1)](../specs/014-artifacts-files-and-attachments.md#cross-node-artifact-relay-v1) (§Required Behavior threat-model scope, Publish step 3, Fetch steps 5–6, and the two scoped §Acceptance Criteria rows); [Plan-014 §Invariants](../plans/014-artifacts-files-and-attachments.md#invariants) I-014-10 |

### Spec-024 Implementation Plan

[Plan-027: Cross-Node Dispatch And Approval](../plans/027-cross-node-dispatch-and-approval.md) owns the V1 implementation of [Spec-024](../specs/024-cross-node-dispatch-and-approval.md). Earlier Session H-interim dependency headers on Plans 002/003/008/012 remain historical context for surfaces governed by Spec-024, but those plans do not absorb cross-node dispatch implementation work.

Plan-027 owns the `cross_node_dispatch_approvals` and `cross_node_pending_dispatch` Local SQLite tables, the `cross_node_dispatch_coordination` Shared Postgres table, the daemon/control-plane dispatch modules, and the typed dispatch contract. Its Tier 9 placement keeps it after the relay, identity, approval, replay, crypto, and desktop approval surfaces it composes.

### Optimization Notes

- Plan-003 (Tier 3) has Plan-001 as its only hard plan-level upstream — Plan-008-bootstrap is already at Tier 1 (already in place at Tier 1) and the Plan-006 taxonomy edge is a Tier 4 additive follow-up (Plan-003 Tier 3 ships event-shape stubs only for the integrity envelope; the per-event payload-shape schemas are Plan-003 Phase 2, and the Tier-4 follow-up is union-registration + `EventEnvelope` + `CapabilityDetails` binding). Plan-003 could move to Tier 2 alongside Plan-002 if parallelism is desired.
- Plan-014 (Tier 7) depends only on earlier-tier substrate — Plan-006 (Tier 4 — `EventLogService.append` + the T1.2 type registry) + Plan-007-partial (Tier 1 — the `artifact.*` IPC `MethodRegistry`), both complete before Tier 7 (see the §3 Plan-014 row) — and had no within-Tier-7 upstream, so before the 2026-07-08 relay amendment it could have moved as early as Tier 5. That is no longer true: the amendment added Plan-008-remainder (Tier 5 — the R4 pairwise channels the artifact-key attestation rides) and Plan-021 (Tier 6 — the six Spec-021 relay registry rows Tasks 7–9 self-wire), and the 2026-08-12 relay-scope targeted readiness-audit delta added Plan-018 (Tier 5 — the fetch-token issuer key) and Plan-003 (Tier 3 — the fetch-mint's attach-state corroboration; that edge was the `attachmentId` node selector when added, re-specified 2026-08-16 to the key-thumbprint selector, which **narrows the edge to corroboration but does not remove it**, so the tier floor is unaffected). Plan-021 at Tier 6 sets the floor, so Tier 7 is now Plan-014's earliest tier, not a conservative placement. Plan-012 (Tier 6) cannot move earlier: its Phase-2 trust-envelope evaluation reads Plan-009/Plan-010 envelope roots, and its event/wire surfaces ride Plan-006 (Tier 4) + Plan-004 (Tier 5) (Tier-6 audit; see the §3 row).
- Within Tier 6, Plan-010 depends on Plan-009. If Plan-009 finishes before Plan-012, Plan-010 can start immediately without waiting for Plan-012.
- Plan-024 (Tier 1) has no upstream-as-blocker inter-plan deps for Phases 1–3 and could land at any point before Plan-005 begins; placed at Tier 1 to document the standalone status explicitly. Phase 3B (campaign B16) is the scoped exception: consume-only extension seams per CP-024-4 plus the CP-024-5 credential-seam `plan_phase` precondition gating Phase 3B on Plan-006 Phase 3 merged (2026-08-02, PR #279; Phase 3B holds its own Tier-4 row per the same remainder split).

## 6. Active Next Steps DAG

This section tracks the actionable next steps the [plan-readiness-audit Tier 1](../operations/plan-implementation-readiness-audit-runbook.md) PR #15 left for the Tier 1 code track and the Tiers 2-9 audit track. Each `NS-NN` node is one actionable step — code, governance, audit, or cleanup. Edges are hard preconditions; a node moves from `blocked` to `todo` when all incoming edges are satisfied. Existing [`BL-NNN`](../backlog.md) entries are cross-referenced where they gate downstream `NS-NN` nodes. Static plan-level dependencies live in §3; static tier ordering lives in §5; this section is the dynamic "we are here" pointer that complements both — it never overrides them. In particular, an audit node reaching `completed` clears only the **audit gate**: the code lanes it unblocks are not thereby code-ready — they dispatch only once §5 tier order is satisfied (all prior-tier code complete — excepting the procurement-blocked Plan-024 Phase 4-5 tail at NS-09/NS-10, a standalone Tier-1 leaf that per §5's Optimization Notes has no inter-plan deps and so gates no later tier) **and** their own plan §Preconditions are met. Audit clearance is necessary, not sufficient. All of this gates plan-task dispatch; the enhancement and tooling lanes (CONTRIBUTING.md §How Code Lands) sit outside it. Status values follow [`backlog.md`](../backlog.md) conventions (`todo` / `in_progress` / `blocked` / `completed`).

- **2026-08-25 amendment (NS-79 auto-create — the CLI executable-name canonicalization):** NS-79 (Plan-007 CLI executable-name targeted readiness-audit delta — the restoring re-audit) is added to the DAG as born-`completed`, the restoring delta riding the same diff (the NS-63 / NS-65..NS-74 / NS-78 in-swap shape). The corpus spelled the CLI executable two ways; the split traced back to the npm package name (`@ai-sidekicks/cli`) and the repository name leaking into invocation text, with this plan's own `bin` map the outlier against **130** already-canonical invocation sites including README, CLAUDE.md, and every runbook. **The classification is the substance of the entry, and it corrects a first reading.** The 52 rewrites divide into two classes: 48 are CITING prose — a plan restating how a command is invoked — which is the runbook's citation-fix row and carries no flip, exactly the class the 2026-04-30 BL-101 precedent governs (`8c838d4a`: 32 files across 22 plan bodies canonicalizing executable-form strings, zero header Status flips); four are the `bin` map at T-007r-3-1 and its restatements (§Target Areas, §Files, §Done Checklist), which DEFINE the executables npm installs. Rewriting that key — and registering a second entry beside it — is a behavior change in the plan body, the runbook's behavior-change row, and it is amendment-class whether or not code has shipped, since the surface being amended is the definition rather than a citation of it. The two `bin`-map restatements outside Plan-007 (`Plan-016 §Phase 3 — Wire namespace + SDK`, `Plan-028 §Target Areas`) sit in the citing class and already write the map with an ellipsis, so neither claims to enumerate its entries. Plan-007 alone therefore flips `approved → review → approved` in-swap, its §Preconditions audit box taking a second 2026-08-25 Re-opened/Delivered record pair; the five other plans and the five other specs the sweep touches take citing rewrites only and stay `approved` unflipped, and Plan-026 takes only the paired-spec box record its sibling's flip obliges. `Spec-007` is among those five rather than untouched: it takes one citing rewrite — an invocation restated in §Interfaces And Contracts — and stays `approved`, because it sets no `bin` map, so that sentence cites a name Plan-007 defines rather than defining one. **Spec-026 takes two touches, and the review round corrected how they were classified.** Its §CLI Surface gains one descriptive sentence on the alias and its `PATH` collision, matched by one in the README's §CLI-First introduction — a note rather than a requirement, outside §Required Behavior, and citing-class. But its §Three-Way Choice Semantics Option-3 sentence sits **inside normative §Required Behavior**, and it carried the `ai-` prefix on a URL scheme `Spec-023 §Deep-Link Invite Flow` owns and that same sentence cites. The repair to `sidekicks://` restores what the authority always said and moves the scheme's canonical value not at all — which is exactly why the first reading filed it as citing-class and left the spec unflipped. The runbook's [§Spec-Status Promotion Gate](../operations/plan-implementation-readiness-audit-runbook.md#spec-status-promotion-gate) does not read that way: it flips a spec on an amendment to §Required Behavior, without an exemption for a correction, and the reason survives the obviousness — a reader implementing from this spec alone would have registered the wrong handler. **Spec-026 therefore flips `approved → review → approved` in-swap**, with Plan-026 recording a **no-flip** (no plan-side surface, invariant, task, or obligation moves) on the NS-72 precedent, its paired-spec box taking the scoped Re-opened/Delivered record. The alias obligation itself is normative only in Plan-007's T-007r-3-1, the task that authors the manifest and its install documentation. **The `sk` short alias is registered in this same pass, and an earlier draft of this entry got that wrong.** That draft deferred the alias to a follow-on Plan-007 amendment, reasoning that registering a second installed executable is the same amendment class as renaming the first and strictly larger. The class reading was right and the conclusion did not follow: the naming is one user-ratified decision pairing `sidekicks` with `sk`, so deferring half of it would have left the plan describing half a settled contract, and the flip this vehicle already pays covers both. The map therefore declares **two** entries at all four sites, both resolving to `./dist/main.js`, with the long form never replaced — every doc, runbook, help string, and error message spells `sidekicks`, and `sk` is named once in the `--help` header. The accepted risk is recorded rather than mitigated away, and **the review round corrected its mechanism twice**. Homebrew ships an unrelated `sk` (skim). Where its prefix and the npm/pnpm global bin directory differ, two distinct files exist, both directories sit on `PATH`, POSIX command search takes the first match scanning from beginning to end, and `PATH` order alone silently decides the winner. But the prefixes are **not guaranteed to differ**, and an earlier draft of this entry asserted that they always do: Homebrew documents `/usr/local` as its supported Intel-macOS prefix, npm links into `{prefix}/bin` with `/usr/local` its Unix default, and on that layout both target `/usr/local/bin/sk` — so the install meets the existing entry before `PATH` order is ever consulted, surfacing as a package-manager refusal or a replaced link rather than as silent shadowing. Whether the collision is loud or silent is therefore a property of the machine's layout, and the ratification accepts **either**; the plan deliberately predicts neither tool's reaction, because no cited source fixes it. The plan's §References carries the npm `bin` and npm `folders` sources, pnpm `globalBinDir`, POSIX `PATH`, and Homebrew's installation prefix — replacing, in two successive rounds, first an unsourced claim that the installers detect nothing and then an over-strong claim that they never can. Documentation is the mitigation and it is an obligation — T-007r-3-1's install documentation MUST cover **both** outcomes: the `which -a sk` check for the silent case, and, for the shared-prefix case, that an install error or a replaced `sk` is this accepted collision rather than a defect. **The regression gate required the shared engine to grow.** `canonical-paths.json` entries gain an opt-in `matcher` field (`"literal"`, today's `git grep -F` behavior and the default, vs `"regex"`, `git grep -E`), because a fixed-string needle for a multi-token command invocation is imprecise in BOTH directions — it misses whitespace variants (space runs, tabs) and, having no trailing boundary, fires on legitimate project-name prose. Both directions were observed rather than theorized: the over-match half failed CI on this very PR, where a hyphen-suffixed fixed-string needle matched `--repository <owner>/ai-sidekicks --environment production` in `docs/backlog.md`. The field is **opt-in, never a global flip** — the founding `apps/desktop/` entry's unbounded substring semantics are what catch the executable/CLI shape PR #24 missed, so boundary-wrapping every entry would silently narrow this registry's own founding instance. Two regex entries land: **six** needles for the CLI invocation surface (verb-anchored and whitespace-tolerant, global-flag, the bin-map key matched independently of JSON colon spacing and required to carry a string value — since JSON permits whitespace between a property name and its colon and a manifest written that way would otherwise install the deprecated executable past a green gate, while key position alone would fire on any object merely KEYED by the deliberately-unchanged project name — the prose `bin` shorthand, the deep-link scheme, and the shell line-continuation signature, which exists because `git grep` is line-oriented and no `[[:space:]]+` can consume a newline) and one source-scoped needle covering all three string-literal delimiters of the Electron protocol call. **Path-qualified invocations are covered by the prefix guard rather than by a needle of their own, and that is the shape the last review round forced.** They were first added as a seventh needle carrying its own copy of the verb alternation, which covered `<path>/ai-sidekicks <verb>` and silently left `<path>/ai-sidekicks --help` and `<path>/ai-sidekicks \\` uncovered — the path anchor lived on one signature and the other two had never been given it. The guard is now a **single shared two-arm alternation** every invocation needle carries: a plain arm rejecting `/`, `@`, and word characters, and a path arm readmitting the slash only behind a filesystem anchor (`/`, `./`, `../`, `~/`). That arm's own leading boundary is an ENUMERATION of what may precede a path — start of line, whitespace, quote, backtick, open paren, `=`, `[` — rather than an exclusion of what may not, which is a third counterexample-driven correction: the subtractive spelling admitted the `>` closing a `<owner>/` placeholder and so re-flagged `--repository <owner>/ai-sidekicks --environment production` in `docs/backlog.md`, the same prose that failed CI on this PR's first round, plus the `<path>/…` placeholders this very entry uses to describe the gate. The enumeration excludes `:` as a side effect, keeping `https://github.com/<owner>/ai-sidekicks run` out of the arm through a URL's own `//`. Coverage is then a property of the guard rather than of whoever remembered to copy it. Four of the six needles were sharpened by review rather than shipped as first written, each against a demonstrated counterexample: the key needle over-matched an object keyed by the project name, the continuation needle over-matched a Windows configuration directory ending the line, the guard under-matched every path-qualified command form, and its first path-arm draft then under-matched two of the three signatures it was added for. Seven new tests in `tools/docs-corpus/__tests__/path-canonical-ripple.test.ts` — plus one in `tools/docs-corpus/__tests__/inbound-cite-discovery.test.ts` for the unbounded-buffer crash this vehicle hit on pristine `develop`; NS-83 independently bounded the `git show :` site underneath this branch and shipped no test, so this diff bounds the two calls it left unbounded (the corpus `ls-files` and the `git grep`), names the overflow in the error, and carries the only regression test — drive the SHIPPED needles against planted fixtures rather than restating patterns inline, covering both directions plus opt-in-ness, mode divergence, registry validation, and fail-closed behavior on an uncompilable and on an unrecognized matcher; each was confirmed to FAIL under a targeted perturbation of what it guards, and the registry's slash allowlist is now DERIVED from the registry so the test file is not the one place a dead executable form survives in-tree. The PR's own Codex round folded five contract corrections into the text rather than deferring them, one of which was a defect in this amendment's first draft: the intervention landing had promised the caller a wire error **alongside** the settlement, which the shipped `JsonRpcResponseEnvelope` union makes unrepresentable and which inverted the very precedent it cited, so round 1 moved the cause onto the `degraded` response and left the error branch on the `startRun` landing alone — a two-landings split round 2 then discarded outright (below), so nothing in this clause describes the settled design; the command-shaped predicate, previously named but undefined, is now one shared byte-level rule (first non-whitespace byte is `/`) with its earlier path-like carve-out withdrawn as a fail-open hole; `every driver must neutralize` is narrowed to a universal boundary and tripwire with a **grade-scoped** transform, resolving its contradiction with the plan's own byte-preservation test; the tripwire is wired into **both** provider normalizers rather than only the leg that command-dispatches today; and the Codex `native` grade — which rested on `codex exec` rather than the app-server `turn/start` path the driver uses — was held **provisional** until T3.18's currency step probes that path. A round-2 pass then found those last two corrections jointly fail-open: grade-scoping makes the parity row the behavioral input, and a row reading `native` for a leg the same round had called unverified instructed that leg to skip the transform on evidence the spec itself discounted. The structural fix is that **a behavioral row states the grade governing today** — the Codex cell is graded **`emulated`**, its `codex exec` basis and unprobed `turn/start` transport recorded in the cell, and a confirming probe re-grades it `native` by ordinary amendment, a success branch the provisional wording never named. The same pass corrected `Spec-017`'s standing composer-escape refusal, which this amendment's own predicate had made unjustifiable as stated. Round 2 then **redesigned the landing** rather than patching it a third time: `startRun` has no registered JSON-RPC method behind it, and the shipped `.strict()` `DriverInterventionResultSchema` was read as unable to carry a cause without re-opening a merged Phase-1 task — so the two-landings split named one branch that does not exist and one surface then believed closed. **Round 3 reversed that second half** (below): the plan's own Phase 3B is the counterexample, additive-optional widening of a merged contract surface being exactly what it exists to do, and `.strict()` rejects only _unknown_ keys. The refusal moved off the driver's return value onto the run's own `run.failed` terminal — one landing for both paths, on CP-005-5's resolved handoff shape, touching no Plan-004 file — and a tripped intervention now **fails the run**, reversing round 1's reading: a frame the provider dispatched as its own command may have mutated the session state that run depends on, so continuing was the fail-open branch and the terminal state is the quarantine, costing no `runtime_bindings` column. The tripwire's detector was inverted in the same pass, from recognizing an open set of command-dispatch shapes the pinned references document nowhere to requiring positive typed turn evidence, an unrecognized response envelope tripping rather than passing. **Round 3 (the final round) settled four dispositions on top of that.** The intervention cause gets a **typed carrier** after all: `DriverInterventionResult` takes one additive-optional closed-literal `refusalCode`, a Phase-3 EXTEND of the Plan-005-owned `packages/contracts/src/provider-driver.ts` on the same additive-optional footing Phase 3B already uses, consumed by Plan-004 **T2.6** under the already-registered **CP-004-1** — whose row widens by one clause, Plan-004 taking that mirror on a **recorded no-flip** (no obligation, task, or invariant minted there). A closed literal union rather than a string is load-bearing: the envelope parses untrusted provider output, so a daemon-selected code from a fixed set adds no free-form surface and needs no `wireFreeFormString` bound, and `.strict()` is retained because it rejects only _unknown_ keys. The **run-start** landing is restated as what it structurally was — an asynchronous run outcome on the existing `run.failed` kind, no new kind registered — with the reason made explicit: a queued or orchestration-started run has no caller waiting, so a synchronous refusal would have had nobody to refuse to. The **binding is quarantined** by disposal rather than by a flag, closing the hole a terminal run state alone left open (the process holding possibly-mutated client-side state outlives the run, and the next run binds back to it), which keeps this plan's prohibition on `runtime_bindings` recovery columns intact. And the **zero-turn synthetic shape** is named normatively as the detector's conformance instance with the recorded transcript as T3.18's fixture — deliberately the rule's instance and not its definition, so the fail-closed positive-evidence burden is unchanged. The one census consequence is stated where it lands: **one wire member is minted**, and it is the only one. [BL-148](../archive/backlog-archive.md) is completed and archived, and its gate is re-homed off the archived item onto the landed contract at [Spec-017 §Command interception — the reserved `/` prefix (C-18)](../specs/017-workflow-authoring-and-execution.md#command-interception--the-reserved--prefix-c-18), Plan-017 I-017-17, and ADR-027 — an erratum-class cite repoint carrying no Status flip, with the escape follow-up's downstream-consumer record moved into Spec-017's own text because an archived item records nothing forward. NS-76 carries no §6 edges (a born-`completed` docs-only leaf, the NS-42..NS-74 shape). Node census re-derived by direct count over the §Graph nodes (a pattern admitting the `NS13a` / `NS13b` split ids): **80** NS nodes / **78** completed at this diff's HEAD, the blocked set **{NS-09, NS-10}** unchanged and nothing promoted. This entry adds exactly **one** born-`completed` node; sibling vehicles of the same sprint land their own NS nodes in their own PRs, so the absolute figures move with merge order while that delta does not.

### NS-41: Plan-006 Phase 2 — Crypto Protocol Core

- Status: `completed` (resolved 2026-07-27 via PR #256 — squash commit `faff8cc`: shipped Plan-006 Phase 2 (Crypto protocol core, Tier 4), tasks T2.1–T2.5 + T2.7, opening the Plan-006-owned `packages/runtime-daemon/src/events/` subtree; 29 files, +11985/−142. T2.1 CREATEd `canonicalizer.ts` — RFC 8785 JCS canonical bytes behind the phantom-branded `CanonicalBytes` type, over an **exact** `canonicalize@3.0.0` pin rather than a caret range: the canonical bytes are the input to a hash chain, so a patch-level serialization change is a silent chain break across every previously-signed row, not a bug fix — and EXTENDed the Plan-006-owned `packages/contracts/src/event.ts` in place with `EVENT_ENVELOPE_SEQUENCE_MAX`, bound on `EventEnvelopeSchema.sequence` via `.max()`: above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` distinct sequences collapse onto one IEEE-754 double and the canonical bytes stop being injective, so two different events could canonicalize identically and collide in the `row_hash` chain — a hash-collision guard, not an arbitrary limit, and not raisable. T2.2 CREATEd `signer.ts` — the BLAKE3 hash chain rooted at `GENESIS_PREV_HASH` (32 zero bytes) plus Ed25519 sign/verify pinned to strict RFC 8032 semantics via `{ zip215: false }`, so a signature that ZIP-215's looser cofactored equation would admit is refused. T2.3 shipped the golden-vector suite binding the canonicalizer to **RFC 8785 Appendix B Table 1** (Appendix A is the ECMAScript sample canonicalizer and carries no vectors), alongside the NUL / lone-surrogate / callable-`toJSON` refusal fixtures. T2.4 CREATEd `pii-indirection.ts` — the injected `PiiEncryptor` seam and the `PiiPayloadCiphertext` brand, and the **sole** PII write path: cleartext never reaches `payload`, and both the ciphertext's BLAKE3 digest and the PII owner's participant id are projected into the signed bytes. T2.5 shipped the post-shred signature-verification property suite — a row whose per-participant key has been destroyed still verifies, because the signature commits to the ciphertext and never to the plaintext, which is what makes [Spec-022 §Shred Fan-Out](../specs/022-data-retention-and-gdpr.md#shred-fan-out) Path 1 chain-safe. ### NS-48: Plan-010 Phase 2 — Daemon Git Services (Worktrees, Clones, Execution Roots)

- Status: `completed` (resolved 2026-08-08 via PR #297 — squash commit `3e98412`: shipped Plan-010 Phase 2 (Daemon git services — worktrees, clones, execution roots; Tier 6), tasks T2.1–T2.6 — the `git/` service layer that turns Phase 1's contracts and four tables into live worktrees, ephemeral clones and bound execution roots, with the five registered `worktree.*` transitions observable as Spec-006 lifecycle events (`-> failed` is deliberately non-evented per D-010-11, and the `-> dirty` / `-> merged` producers are a recorded Phase-3 obligation — both carve-outs detailed below) and every provisioning git invocation structurally incapable of firing repository-controlled hooks (hooks-scoped per the codex round-1 I-010-10 true-up: checkout-time filter drivers named by content-carried `.gitattributes` still run, though their commands come from the user's own git config — git-lfs the canonical case — never from repo content; the residual is recorded in both services' I-010-10 sections). **T2.1** CREATEd `packages/runtime-daemon/src/git/worktree-event-emitter.ts` as the SINGLE emission seam for the five `worktree.*` `session_lifecycle` events, sitting OVER Plan-006 T3.1's `EventLogService.append` rather than beside it — the Plan-009 T2.2 precedent applied to the sibling domain, so the halt gate, the PII split gate and the integrity columns govern worktree events by construction. It exposes exactly five emit surfaces and no `emitFailed`: D-010-11's deliberate carve-out is closed by the ABSENCE of a method rather than by a convention a later caller could forget, and the `-> failed` no-emit path is pinned by regression — the registration-is-not-an-emission-license rule NS-37 states, now read from the producer side. **T2.2** CREATEd `worktree-service.ts` + `worktree-errors.ts`: create / validateReuse / retire / cleanupPass over the D-010-7 provenance-split collision policy (a caller-supplied name colliding refuses `worktree.branch_collision` because user intent is never adapted; a daemon-derived name takes the first-free ordinal suffix through an index-arbitrated insert-retry, the partial-unique `idx_worktrees_active_branch` arbitrating the race rather than a lock — I-010-4 treating its violation as the typed retry signal, never a crash), the D-010-8 base-ref policy, and D-010-15 explicit-reuse-only binding. `worktree-errors.ts` carries every Plan-010 typed error class, and the review's sharpest structural finding lands here: `workspace.busy` is a Plan-010-INTRODUCED registry row whose CARRIER is Plan-009's live `WorkspaceBusyError` per CP-009-7 — minting a second class for the same code would fork `instanceof` discrimination at exactly the seam T2.3 adjudicates on, so the row is Plan-010's and the carrier stays Plan-009's. **T2.3** CREATEd `ephemeral-clone-service.ts` — prepare / dispose / retireRunClone / cleanupTick, TTL bookkeeping as daemon config rather than wire.
