### NS-50: Plan-010 Phase 5 — Turn-Snapshot Service (Capture, Restore, Retention Prune)

- Status: `completed` (resolved 2026-08-09 via PR #303 — squash commit `5bcf40c`: shipped Plan-010 Phase 5 (Turn-snapshot service; Tier 6, campaign B23 / Task 26), tasks T5.1–T5.3 — the daemon-side file-restore leg the run time-travel feature (#19) requires, and the last enumerated remainder in the §2 `packages/runtime-daemon/src/git/` row. The phase authors a **pure callee** per CP-010-12: execution root, run id, epoch, turn ordinal, execution mode and the restore `epochLineage` all arrive as caller-supplied parameters, so the service never reads `run_execution_contexts` outside its retention leg and takes no build edge on the B9-owned Plan-004 call site — the reading its own `preconditions:` block ratifies, since a Phase-3 gate here would deadlock the Phases 1/2 → Phase 5 → Plan-004 Phase 3 → Plan-010 Phase 3 order. **T5.1** CREATEd `packages/runtime-daemon/src/git/turn-snapshot-service.ts` and its test file: capture stages a scratch index outside the worktree and is pinned to `git add -A` **tree** equivalence rather than to a hand-described recipe — non-ignored untracked embedded repositories normalized to `160000` gitlinks recording their own `HEAD`, commitless ones skipped and enumerated instead of fatal (porcelain fabricates or hard-fails there, so the skip is degrade-honestly, not a gap) — with one base OID resolved at entry for BOTH the tree and the recorded parent so a mid-capture `HEAD` move cannot record an old tree under a new parent, the six-var ident/date env stamp that keeps the OID host-independent, and the create-only `update-ref --no-deref refs/sidekicks/runs/<runId>/epoch-<E>/turn-<N>` write whose idempotence is per-epoch (a retried capture returns the recorded OID; a post-rollback re-execution's identical ordinal mints a fresh ref under its own epoch segment and never resolves to the superseded one). Two properties are structural rather than asserted: capture failure emits to an injected diagnostics sink and **never blocks the turn**, and every host git-config knob that can move the recorded bytes or the captured path set carries exactly one recorded ruling in a closed disposition table on the service header — pinned, deliberately honored, measured-irrelevant with the measurement stated, or recorded residual. **T5.2** EXTENDed the file with the restore leg, split so that `Spec-004 §Required Behavior`'s whole-rollback rejection runs before the conversation leg: the non-mutating `resolveRestoreTarget` walks the caller-supplied lineage to the newest epoch whose `rewindBase` sits below the target and **refuses rather than falls through** when that epoch's ref is absent (a failed epoch-1 capture must never resolve epoch-0's same-ordinal tree), checks the fail-closed `HEAD` precondition, and mints a sealed, frozen, `WeakSet`-registered target that `restoreToTurn` binds and re-verifies against TOCTOU before mutating. The destructive `read-tree --reset -u` names the **verified OID**, not the mutable ref, so the enumeration derivation and the checkout can no longer name different commits; the untracked-delete pass runs to a fixpoint (a turn-created untracked `.gitignore` shields what it ignores through the single pass that deletes it) while exempting the embedded repositories capture recorded on the snapshot commit's `Skipped-Embedded-Repositories` trailer, an omission that measurement — not review reading — caught destroying them; and the typed result unions carry collision-overwrite, divergent-gitlink and partial-restore enumerations whose field names are pinned identical to Plan-004's wire arms so the T3.13 mapping stays an identity rather than a rename. **T5.3** EXTENDed it with retention: `sweepPrunableRuns` deletes every run whose `released_at` plus the daemon-config window has closed, driven by a startup reconcile (for windows that elapsed while the daemon was down) plus a periodic cadence, with every ref op running through `git --git-dir=<git_common_dir>` and never through `execution_root`, because a `worktree`-mode root can be physically retired long before its refs leave the shared object store; unprunable runs take a typed skip taxonomy in which an absent git dir warns and a disposed ephemeral clone stays quiet, matching what the plan row asks of each. Its one edit outside Plan-010's own namespace is the sanctioned `wireTurnSnapshotRetentionSweep` call in Plan-007-owned `bootstrap/index.ts`; the sweeper DRIVER had first been written into that file on a corpus-false ownership rationale and was relocated into the service file under CP-010-7 during review, the dead rationale recorded at the relocation site. **The review arc ran eight rounds — three internal per task, four external codex rounds, and a CI follow-up — and each closed a defect CLASS rather than an instance.** The `--no-deref` hardening is the shape of the whole phase: an unflagged `update-ref -d <ref> <oid>` against a planted in-namespace symref resolves its own compare-and-swap oid THROUGH the symref and deletes the referent branch at exit 0, invisible to both existing defenses, and the create side transfers its must-not-exist check to a dangling symref the same way — both measured, both flagged, and the CI follow-up then found the flagged create's outcome to be git-version-dependent (2.50.1 succeeds at the validated name, ≥2.54 refuses), so the test now asserts the I-010-21 claims unbranched before branching on the outcome tag rather than pinning one version's shape as universal. ### NS-52: Plan-010 Phase 6 — Sparse-Root Capture Closure (Sparse-Aware Capture Staging)

- Status: `completed` (resolved 2026-08-10 via PR #309 — squash commit `d83ae0e`: shipped Plan-010 Phase 6 (Sparse-root capture closure; Tier 6), task T6.1, an in-place EXTEND of `packages/runtime-daemon/src/git/turn-snapshot-service.ts` and its test file. The phase closes NS-50's recorded residual (2) — sparse-checkout capture loss, measured there to its root cause at CAPTURE rather than at the checkout leg and deliberately left unpinned so its two candidate closures could be adjudicated as the contract-surface product decision they are — along the disposition the 2026-08-09 sparse-root capture-closure amendment (PR #307) ratified and NS-51's restoring targeted readiness-audit delta (PR #308) carried back into `approved`: **sparse-aware staging**, not a typed capture refusal. **What shipped.** Sparse detection reads the config bit alone and fails closed when the bit is set but the rules have vanished, so a half-configured root refuses rather than silently capturing the truncated tree the not-sparse pipeline would mint. The sparsity oracle is git's own — `git sparse-checkout check-rules`, floored at git 2.41, fail-closed on both legs, behind a single spelling shared by its three callers rather than one predicate per call site. Scratch staging seeds from the LIVE index rather than the base tree (the base tree is what dropped out-of-cone paths in the first place, and a `git add --sparse`-staged modification surviving a cone shrink reaches porcelain's tree while a `<base>`-seeded tree reverts it), serialized under the per-root resolved `<index>.lock` — an `open` with `wx`, four 25 ms retries on `EEXIST`, released without ever writing through the lock — so the daemon contends with a concurrent git the way git itself does instead of reading a pre-write index at exit 0. The recorded boundary set rides an unconditional kind-preserving `Sparse-Boundary-Paths:` sorted-JSON trailer: directory entries keep their trailing slash, `[]` spells the empty set as a format marker rather than an absence, the subtraction deriving it is byte-exact through the latin1 listing-key bijection, and a trailer-absent snapshot restored into a detected sparse root draws a typed vintage refusal ahead of every write instead of a silently truncated restore. Restore gains a kind-scoped delete-exemption (exact-path for file entries, segment-boundary subtree for non-descended directory entries) and a membership-scoped index pre-drop of the recorded boundary set — one atomic `update-index` under the `derive-enumerations` step cursor, applied after the TOCTOU second `HEAD` read — plus a pre-mutation boundary-obstruction refusal covering all three shapes of the measured collision taxonomy: a blob beneath a boundary file, a blob at a boundary directory, and a blob at a proper ancestor of either kind, with gitlinks exempt from the cone oracle because git never marks a gitlink `skip-worktree` (measured, not reasoned), and the refusal detail bounded. **Three of those legs were repaired 2026-08-10 by PR #312 (`develop` squash `9d3b93b`), ahead of the naming amendment below, which therefore names a repaired contract rather than recording destructive residuals in the aliasing class those legs govern:** the trailer's JSON strings re-encoded from `utf8` to `latin1`, making the trailer itself a byte record — the subtraction was already byte-exact at this merge, but a `utf8` trailer collapses every invalid sequence onto `U+FFFD`, and the destructive direction of that collapse is the restore-side pre-drop's snapshot-tree exclusion firing spuriously; the pre-drop's predicate widened from the recorded set's FILE half to its full recorded width, directory subtrees included, the exclusion retained and both halves byte-keyed; and the untracked-delete pass gained a whole-pass pre-mutation round-trip guard, refusing the entire pass rather than removing any path through a decode alias. The shipped `commit-tree` call site converts from `-m` argv to `-F -` stdin transport, and the success tail gains an observed-subset materialized-out-of-cone diagnostic re-fingerprinted at emission. **The frozen surfaces stayed frozen, which is the phase's other deliverable:** restore gains no new worktree-mutating pipeline step, restore-step vocabulary stays at five members, both result unions stay three arms so Plan-004's T3.13 wire mapping remains an identity, and the daemon-local capture-step vocabulary — not wire-pinned — grew by exactly two members, `detect-sparse-root` and `check-sparse-rules`. PR #309's record closes the scoped suite at **189 file-scoped arms** (176 → 189 in that PR, the external-round fixes included) inside 2,026 package-wide, with three mutation matrices carrying per-arm kill attribution. **That record carries three internal review rounds and one external codex round, and both internal ceremony escalations were one-way and are recorded as such:** S → M on round 1's actionables, then M → L on round 2's — the membership-scoped versus root-gated pre-drop — with the round-trip cap spent. Codex round 1 raised three findings, each verified real before repair rather than fixed on assertion: byte-exact subtraction (F1), the kind-preserving trailer plus the subtree exemption (F2), and the obstruction refusal (F3/P1); the follow-up sweep then surfaced the third obstruction shape, measured destructive on git 2.50.1 BEFORE implementation, and a self-surfaced fix bounded the refusal detail. Codex round 2 is recorded there as reaching its 20-minute session cap with CI green, zero unresolved threads and a `CLEAN` merge state at merge. **One design gap is open, and it is this entry's follow-on obligation.** The pre-mutation obstruction refusal is behavior [I-010-24](../plans/010-worktree-lifecycle-and-execution-modes.md#invariants) does not yet name — that invariant names the trailer-absent vintage refusal only — and `Spec-010`'s nearest precedent, the ignored-path ruling, chose restore-wins-with-enumeration for paths OUTSIDE the snapshot contract, which recorded boundary paths are not. The disposition PR #309's review record settles is the typed refusal (rollback never destroys user-authored content sitting at a recorded boundary path; a force-override is deferred as a possible enhancement rather than shipped), and the amendment naming that behavior on I-010-24 and the `Spec-010 §Turn-Boundary Snapshots` capture bullet is **owed** as the next docs PR on the same targeted-amendment channel PR #307 → PR #308 established. [I-010-24](../plans/010-worktree-lifecycle-and-execution-modes.md#invariants)'s restore half now names the pre-mutation refusal — typed at `derive-enumerations`, all three measured destructive shapes, both deliberately admitted non-shapes, oracle-scored materialization with gitlink displacers exempt, bounded detail, frozen unions — beside the rescoped kind-width delete-exemption and the byte-exact boundary subtraction, and the `Spec-010 §Turn-Boundary Snapshots` capture bullet carries all three legs with the disposition rationale and the deliberately-unscheduled force-override. A **third** non-shape sits outside that admitted pair and is structurally unreachable rather than tolerated: a snapshot **tree** path standing at a recorded boundary FILE path never arises, because capture derives the boundary set by subtracting the whole `ls-tree -r` listing — blobs and gitlinks alike — from its candidates, so a recorded boundary FILE path is by construction absent from that snapshot's tree. That unreachability is exactly as strong as the subtraction's byte-exactness and depends on nothing else: were the subtraction decoded rather than byte-keyed, two distinct on-disk paths that decode alike could leave a tree path and a boundary FILE path co-recorded and the shape would go live, which is why the end-to-end byte-keying PR #312 completed is what holds it closed rather than merely unobserved. The `Plan-010's plan-level status stays approved` and no-census-consequence readings below stay true **of PR #309's own merge**, which is what they describe, and are overtaken as current state by that amendment.) **Six residuals were recorded at this merge rather than closed; one has since closed, leaving five open.** (1) A `SIGKILL` inside the lock window strands `<index>.lock` — git's own lockfile property, not a defect this seam can remove. ### NS-53: Plan-010/Spec-010 Boundary-Obstruction Naming Targeted Readiness-Audit Delta — Restoring Re-Audit

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-08-10 via PR #313, squash `165923b` — the restoring re-audit the 2026-08-10 boundary-obstruction refusal + kind-scoped exemption naming amendment (PR #311) obligated when it named three Required Behavior legs on I-010-24's restore half and the `Spec-010 §Turn-Boundary Snapshots` capture bullet — the pre-mutation typed refusal at `derive-enumerations` over the three measured destructive shapes, the kind-preserving trailer with its kind-scoped delete-exemption widths, and the byte-exact boundary subtraction — flipping Plan-010 under the runbook's Status Flip Rule row 4 and Spec-010 under its spec-amendment rule. That amendment is the docs PR NS-52 above recorded as **owed**, so this delta closes the second half of that obligation: the naming landed, and this is what carries it back into `approved`. **Scope: the amendment's growth, read against the code truth.** The audit target is the merged amendment diff; the oracle is `packages/runtime-daemon/src/git/turn-snapshot-service.ts#TurnSnapshotService` (its restore pipeline and the exported result unions `TurnSnapshotCaptureResult` / `TurnSnapshotRestoreResult`) and its suite at `develop` (`9d3b93b` — PR #312's repair round, which is the state the naming describes), since a naming amendment's only real failure mode is naming something the code does not do. Six axes: claim-vs-code over every mechanism sentence in I-010-24, the T6.1 contract, the capture bullet and its banner (the three width predicates and the one they share, the directory arm's equality case both over-protection residuals rest on, the `160000` displacer carve landing at the oracle rather than at the refusal, the refusal's position ahead of the index pre-drop, the single atomic `update-index --force-remove` drop under the `derive-enumerations` cursor, the frozen three-arm result unions and five-member restore-step vocabulary against the two added capture-step members, the unconditional `latin1` byte-record trailer and the subtraction taken against the whole `ls-tree -r` listing on listing bytes); internal coherence across the six surfaces the amendment touched; quoted-title fidelity (all twelve `it` titles the spec quotes byte-compared against the merged suite — twelve exact matches, the comparator negative-controlled on a perturbed title); citation-anchor fidelity (both added `git-ls-files` anchors resolve against the published page's own ids); census arithmetic re-derived from the per-file `Status` headers, closing to 28 plans and 28 specs in both directions; and Gate-4 marker-line integrity. Every prior disposition was fed as input and verified landed rather than relitigated — the amendment PR's eight review threads (three of them closed in code by PR #312 ahead of the naming) and the parallel audit's findings. The mandatory **seeded-refutation negative control** was run on the gitlink carve: the true form is exemption from the _oracle scoring_ (scoring a gitlink would fail open exactly on the destructive case), and the plausible-but-wrong twin — exemption from the _refusal_ — predicts the opposite code at the shape-1 displacer map and the materialization predicate, both of which take the true form, so the method discriminates. **Zero critical, zero major, zero actionable; one polish finding, amended in the same swap:** I-010-24's obstruction clause read as though the frozen `partial_restore` arm carried the refusal detail — the arm carries `failedStep` and the two enumerations and has no detail field, the obstruction detail riding the restore diagnostic channel — now scoped to that, matching the T6.1 row and the spec bullet, which were already exact. One near-miss is recorded rather than dropped: this entry's sibling NS-52 records `189 file-scoped arms` at the Phase-6 merge, which disagrees with a plain count of `it(` call sites and reconciles exactly once the suite's `it.skipIf` alias arms are counted with them — the figure is correct and correctly scoped to that PR's own merge. Status restored `review → approved` on both files in the same swap, the two re-opened Preconditions boxes re-checked with Delivered records, the corpus's forward-looking restoring-delta clauses discharged across all six surfaces, and NS-52's sink-quantifier sentence and `pending` References parenthetical corrected in place with dated records.)

- Summary: Close the gap where a fresh install completes onboarding with no provider account registered and discovers it only when the first provider run refuses. Two halves, split along the plane each belongs to. **Daemon side (Spec-029 / Plan-029):** a per-provider **readiness projection** on the existing `providerAccount.list` reply — a _derivation_ of the registry and never a second source of truth, computed by the same resolution the spawn path performs, expressed in the same vocabulary (two registry-shape arms, otherwise the resolved account's health verbatim), served from the account row's **stored** last-probe result so a registry read spawns no provider process, and **advisory only**: I-029-3 re-validates unconditionally at spawn. Detection is credential-free and never runs a sign-in command; the surface discloses the remedy — provider, account, the provider's own first-party sign-in invocation, and the credential home — **operator-facing only**, on the `mcp.oauth_unsupported` / `mcp.config_scope_unsupported` disclosure discipline, carried since the round-1 fold on the readiness entry's schema-optional `remedy` member, the rule binding the reader rather than the encoding: never an event payload, a relayed payload, a refusal envelope, or a log line. `Spec-029 §Vendor authentication-policy constraints` records at **Documented** trust grade the four published vendor rules that make this a handoff rather than a login form, the decisive one being that a developer may not collect, store, or intermediate provider credentials. New: I-029-9, I-029-10, CP-029-7, T2.5, AC-11..AC-14. **Codex round-1 fold:** the remedy gained the transport it lacked — a schema-optional, producer-obligated `remedy` member on the readiness entry (`ProviderSignInRemedy`), composed at read time and stored nowhere, because a surface obliged to display four values no wire member carried could not implement the handoff at all; the message-text-only disclosure rule is unchanged and re-scoped to the **reader** rather than the encoding. The stored reading also gained its persisted home — `health_state` + `health_observed_at` on the unshipped `provider_accounts` CREATE — so a restart cannot convert a stored read into a fresh probe. **Onboarding side (Spec-026 / Plan-026):** §Required Behavior is restated as two independently-triggered step groups, and `Spec-026 §Provider Authentication (Group B)` is added — offered on exactly three triggers (inside a running flow after the choice resolves, **after** an account-plane refusal, or on explicit activation), never ahead of a run that would otherwise have been admitted, **offered and never demanded** (onboarding completes with zero accounts, with the completion summary naming which providers are not ready and what the first run will do), reporting a provider set up only on the authenticated arm, and offering no field, flag, or environment variable anywhere for a provider token. New: I-026-11..13, CP-026-6, Implementation Steps 23-25, and a terminal **Phase 7** carrying all four Group-B tasks behind an `external_plan_phase_merged` entry on Plan-029 Phase 3 (raised from Phase 2 at the Codex round-1 fold, because T7.4 asserts a provider run **starts** and the spawn path is Phase-3 machinery; Phase 3's own gate names Phase 2) — mechanical enforcement rather than a born-unchecked carrier box (the NS-64 "check the box by making the carrier unnecessary" outcome), and homed as a supplement phase so no shipped phase's gate moves. The round-3 fold closed four more: the readiness read takes the **node-operator gate** its own disclosure boundary assumed (a remedy naming a daemon-owned credential home must not ride an ordinarily-gated read); the read became **account-scopable** so an override-bound refusal yields the failed account's remedy rather than the healthy default's; `observedAt` absence was re-scoped to _this resolution_ rather than the node's probe history; and the `choose_default` arm gained the control that resolves it, since a remedy a client can render and cannot act on is not a remedy. The round-2 fold supplied Group B's two missing consumers: the post-refusal trigger is **routed** (the CLI error path recognizes the five typed account-plane refusal codes and prints an invitation, never auto-launching; the shell's run-failure surface calls the desktop activation entry point on the same codes), and the desktop step gained an **action path** — the renderer's controls post credential-free step-action messages over the walkthrough's existing main-process channel and the host calls the registry verb, so the step can act while adding no preload method. Group B deliberately **persists nothing**: a drafted seen-and-settled config marker was removed rather than shipped, because writing it would have required a sixth `onboarding.*` verb whose only job is recording a UI dismissal and would have created a second record of a step whose truth lives in the registry.
- Exit Criteria: Spec-026, Plan-026, Spec-029, and Plan-029 all present at `approved` with each pair's two governance boxes carrying the scoped Re-opened / Delivered record and no born-unchecked box minted; `Spec-026 §Provider Authentication (Group B)`, `Spec-029 §Node provider readiness and the sign-in handoff`, and `Spec-029 §Vendor authentication-policy constraints` present as normative headings with the anchors this node cites; `ProviderReadinessState`, `ProviderReadiness`, and `ProviderSignInRemedy` registered in `api-payload-contracts.md §Plan-029` with `readiness` on `ProviderAccountListResponse` and the schema-optional, producer-obligated `remedy` on each readiness entry; Plan-026's two closed-set quantifiers re-derived by counting the post-edit body (7 phases, 25 Implementation Steps, 26 tasks, and §Touched But Not Owned 8 → 10 — this bundle's one moved quantifier, for the Plan-007-owned `apps/cli/src/exit-codes.ts` call that routes an account-plane refusal into Group B and the Plan-001-owned `packages/client-sdk/src/index.ts` barrel line that exports the relocated Group-B coordinator); and **no census moves** — the `providerAccount` namespace unmoved at seven verbs, the five `onboarding.*` methods unmoved, no event type, no error code, and no table minted, and the one minted column pair (the stored health reading and its observation timestamp, on the unshipped `provider_accounts` CREATE statement) consuming no migration ordinal (SQLite 56, Postgres 26, plans 29, specs 29 all unchanged); the Gate-4 invariant-census pin moves on the bold channel alone for the ten resolved id references the five new tasks add (Plan-026 T7.1-T7.4, Plan-029 T2.5), the none-arm and legacy channels unmoved, and the value is read off a live `preflight.mjs --survey` run on the rebased tree rather than reconciled by arithmetic against any predecessor. [BL-154](../archive/backlog-archive.md) `completed` and archived, and all four of its named flag sites restated as resolved. Node census re-derived by direct count over the §Graph nodes: **79** NS nodes / **77** completed, counted over the §Graph block in this merge's own rebased tree (`develop` 9791e268, counted at 78 / 76 before this node); this sprint lands several node-minting vehicles concurrently, so a later reader recounts rather than carrying this figure forward. Every inbound line-keyed cite into each touched file content-compared against its pre-edit target rather than trusted to the corpus cite gate, which is a truncation floor: a stale number that still lands on neighbouring prose passes it silently, and the two frozen-tree citers it cannot see at all were swept by hand — one repaired to a line-free descriptor, the dated 2026-04-22 provenance records deliberately left unrenumbered.
- Named residual, recorded rather than closed: a credential-free probe cannot distinguish a healthy first-party login from one whose stored credential has since been destroyed, so the authenticated arm is **necessary and not sufficient**. Bounded by the unchanged I-029-3 spawn gate and the per-account re-authentication runbook, and deliberately not closed by reading credential bytes — that would reverse the no-token-custody posture, which `Spec-029 §ADR Triggers` already classifies as an ADR-level reversal rather than an amendment.

### NS-83: Provider-Account Sign-In, Health Observation, And Per-Limit Quota — With ADR-028 Bounded Custody

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-08-26 via the provider-account sign-in amendment PR — the restoring targeted readiness-audit delta riding the same diff, the NS-63 / NS-65..NS-77 in-swap flip-and-restore shape. **The swap is unusual in one respect and it is called out rather than buried: it lands a new `accepted` ADR that reverses an absolute the corpus stated on five surfaces.** [ADR-028](../decisions/028-provider-credential-custody-posture.md) is not optional garnish — `Spec-029 §ADR Triggers` named this exact change as requiring an ADR _and not an amendment_, so the amendment is only legitimate because the ADR rides with it. It lands `accepted` in the same diff, the same-PR-accepted shape [ADR-025](../decisions/025-runtime-node-control-plane-caller-authorization.md) established at NS-60, which keeps Plan-029's "Required ADRs are accepted" box true at merge rather than pending a follow-on promotion.)
- Type: governance
- Priority: `P2`
- Upstream: none as a §6 edge. The obligating events are two gaps the corpus already recorded and neither of which had an owner: [Provider Failure Runbook §Provider Re-Authentication (Per Account)](../operations/provider-failure-runbook.md#provider-re-authentication-per-account) step 7 instructed an operator to re-authenticate into an account's own credential home and **named no command and no surface, because none existed** — unexecutable on every node, not only headless ones — and `Spec-029 §Fallback Behavior`'s headless arm terminated in a refusal with no path to a working node. Sequenced after NS-77 (PR #358), which landed the `provider_accounts` health columns this amendment extends rather than re-adds. **ID note:** NS-82 was held by a sibling vehicle of this sprint and merged ahead of this node — this branch is rebased onto it, so the ID is settled rather than contested. The siblings still open at this node's landing are NS-79 and NS-84, and the ADR number is the one remaining contested resource: a sibling vehicle claims ADR-029, this vehicle takes ADR-028, and any collision is resolved by the lead at merge.
- References: [ADR-028](../decisions/028-provider-credential-custody-posture.md) (`accepted`, Type 2 — D1 brokered sign-in, D2 bounded token custody; antithesis points 1, 3, and 5 accepted as recorded residuals rather than rebutted), [Spec-029 §Brokered interactive sign-in](../specs/029-provider-accounts-and-credential-homes.md#brokered-interactive-sign-in), [§Non-interactive token registration](../specs/029-provider-accounts-and-credential-homes.md#non-interactive-token-registration), [§Credential-home health observation](../specs/029-provider-accounts-and-credential-homes.md#credential-home-health-observation), [§Per-limit provider quota](../specs/029-provider-accounts-and-credential-homes.md#per-limit-provider-quota), [Plan-029 §Invariants](../plans/029-provider-accounts-and-credential-homes.md#invariants) (I-029-11, I-029-12, I-029-13), [Plan-029 §Cross-Plan Obligations](../plans/029-provider-accounts-and-credential-homes.md#cross-plan-obligations) (CP-029-8..CP-029-11), [Spec-006 §Usage Telemetry](../specs/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#usage-telemetry-usage_telemetry), [Spec-013 §Rate-Limit Display](../specs/013-live-timeline-visibility-and-reasoning-surfaces.md#rate-limit-display), [Spec-022 §PII Data Map](../specs/022-data-retention-and-gdpr.md#pii-data-map), [Spec-023 §Provider Accounts And Cost View](../specs/023-desktop-shell-and-renderer.md#provider-accounts-and-cost-view--plan-029-provider-accounts-and-credential-homes), [Local SQLite Schema §Provider Account Tables (Plan-029)](./schemas/local-sqlite-schema.md#provider-account-tables-plan-029).
- Summary: Close the two recorded gaps and the quota-key defect behind them. **(a) Brokered sign-in** (ADR-028 D1, _not_ custody): two verbs plus a read-shaped subscription; the daemon constructs the invocation, spawns the provider's **unmodified** binary with the account's home pinned, surfaces the provider's own verification URL or device code, and has **no read path into the home at all**. Completion rides a wire-only notification, never an `EventEnvelope`, so the registry stays un-evented and **no Spec-006 event type is minted** — the 156-type / 20-category taxonomy census does not move. **(b) Bounded token custody** (ADR-028 D2, the actual reversal): one write-only input on `register`, five conjunctive admission conditions, sealed through the ADR-021 ladder **outside** the credential home, injected only into the two enumerated invocations an admitting leg allows, and destroyed with the account registration. The replaced absolute is restated in the same mechanically-checkable register it had — _exactly one credential-accepting input, zero credential-bearing outputs_ (I-029-11) — so a reviewer keeps the grep and only the grepped string changes. **(c) A health observer that never refreshes** (I-029-12): both pinned providers rotate refresh tokens single-use with no grace window, so a refreshing poll burns a rotation per tick and a lost rotation **ends the operator's login** — the observed failure mode of the one surveyed tool that does it. The observer reads local state only; the honest residual (a server-side revocation reads as authenticated until real traffic or a deliberate probe finds otherwise) is stated in the spec rather than papered over. It joins the stored pair's writer set as the third writer while the generation-bump authority is deliberately **not** widened, so a transient fault cannot end a parked-work `(accountId, credentialGeneration)` attention epoch. **(d) Per-limit quota re-key** (I-029-13, CP-029-8): the pinned Claude surface publishes five limit identifiers of which **three share a 10080-minute window**, so the 2026-08-18 `(providerAccountId, windowMins)` key retained one of the three by arrival order — an operator shown one weekly limit as their weekly standing with two silently gone, and the survivor changing between restarts. The axis re-keys to `(providerAccountId, limitId)`, additive-optional and absent meaning `default`. Three errata are corrected in the same sweep (two stale `usage.rate_limit_update` payload restatements predating the 2026-08-18 account re-key, in `Spec-017` and the provider-failure runbook), and the **missing §2 ownership row** for `apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/provider-accounts/` is registered — the same defect class NS-78 closed for this plan's own CLI files. **(h) Coherence closure on the inherited absolute.** ADR-028 D2 contradicts the sentence [Spec-028 §Non-Goals](../specs/028-mcp-server-configuration-and-governance.md#non-goals) states — a daemon holding a sealed token is neither the provider storing it nor a daemon that never persists credential material — and [Spec-029](../specs/029-provider-accounts-and-credential-homes.md) had inherited that sentence **verbatim onto a different plane**, which is itself the proof the corpus read it daemon-generally rather than as an MCP-plane rule. That spec's own [Plan-028 I-028-1](../plans/028-mcp-server-configuration-and-governance.md#i-028-1--no-credential-custody) already scopes the identical rule to material `belonging to an MCP server`, so the bullet is corrected **erratum-class** to carry the scope its plan-side twin never lost: it adds nothing, changes no MCP-plane behavior, and bounds no approved content — the provider-account plane's single bounded custody claim is registered on that plane, not as an exception here. **(i) Round-1 Codex fold (2026-08-26).** Seventeen findings, eleven P1, all accepted and folded rather than cataloged. Seven of them were **D2 token-custody** defects, which is the redesign signal rather than a patch queue: the class as first written could not be admitted at all (its mode gates admission, but the token reached a child only on a run admission had already refused), so a **registration-time status invocation** now breaks that cycle, and ADR-028 gains a **fifth conjunctive condition** — the consuming process runs no model-directed code, or the provider is _observed_ to strip the variable from the tool, shell, and subagent subprocesses it spawns. That condition is fail-closed and is not a residual: a run child executes model-directed tools, so an `env` dump the model itself issues reads the bearer token, which is a risk the daemon **creates** rather than one it inherits from the vendor's documented posture, where no untrusted code runs inside that environment. Its refusal lands at **registration**, not at run start: a leg with no recorded strip observation does not admit the class at all, since admitting it would register an account that stores `authenticated`, reports **ready**, and then refuses every run — the exact surface-versus-admission divergence the readiness section exists to prevent. Until the strip is observed on a leg, run-bound injection is refused there and the operator is routed to D1. Also folded: re-supply keyed to the existing `accountId` (deregister-then-register would have discarded the identity and detached its spend history) with the credential-accepting input census unmoved at one; a seal-first/intent-marked-removal reconciliation protocol, because the registry and the secret store are two durability domains and "the same operation" does not make them atomic; an account-keyed tier-2 file layout, ADR-021's fallback being a single fixed-path ciphertext; the same-window quota high-water guard, without which one erroneous low reading overwrites a durable row and shows a 90%-consumed account as 20%; the durable windows served on `providerAccount.list`, carrying the provenance they were **observed** under rather than the transport's; and the five ADR claims that the nightly provider-CLI check detects token renewability — it inspects no token shape, so detection is re-homed onto an **enforced** version pin refused at spawn. **(j) Codex round 2 — eleven findings, all accepted, all downstream-propagation defects from round 1's own folds.** Round 1 corrected the spec and ADR layer; round 2 found the implementing plan tasks, the canonical contract, and the DDL still carrying the pre-fold shape, which is the sweep-completeness class rather than eleven independent defects. Folded: run-bound token injection gated on condition 5 in `api-payload` and AC-18, with the condition's refusal re-homed to **registration** — a leg with no recorded strip observation does not admit the class at all, because admitting it would register an account that stores `authenticated`, reports **ready**, and then refuses every run; the provider version floor moved from Plan-029 T3.2 to **T2.2** as a reusable precondition of every account-pinned invocation, since T2.6's login and T2.7's registration observation both spawn against a pinned home in Phase 2 and an older binary would write the operator's shared home before any Phase-3 check ran; the registration-time status invocation and the daemon-start cross-store reconciliation sweep assigned to T2.7 with fault-injected crash-window tests, and `provider_accounts.removal_intent` added as the durable half of that intent protocol; `logged_in_at` re-anchored in the DDL to the token's **issuance** time and null where no anchor exists; the same-window high-water guard and the three provider-reported identity columns assigned to T3.6 with tests; `accountId` added to `ProviderAccountUsageWindow`, without which a flat multi-account snapshot cannot be attributed; Plan-013 T4.5 re-derived to accept both provenance values and to render **three** absence causes; and the brokered-output whitelist widened three → **four** for the attempt expiry under the same parse-and-validate rule, an operator handed a device code with no visible bound being an operator who types a dead one.
- Exit Criteria: ADR-028 `accepted` with all five §Pre-Implementation Checklist boxes resolved (ADR census 26 → 27 accepted, none `proposed`); Spec-029 / Plan-029, Spec-006 / Plan-006, Spec-013 / Plan-013, Spec-022, and Spec-023 each `approved → review → approved` within the diff, with Plan-029's §Preconditions paired-spec and plan-readiness-audit boxes carrying the literal `- [x]` marker and 2026-08-26 Re-opened/Delivered records; **no born-unchecked box minted** (CP-029-11's CLI run-start option gates a capability, not a correctness property — the default-account path without it is correct and safe — so it holds no task and needs no box); the `providerAccount` wire census seven → ten verbs and six → eight mutating, re-derived by direct count at all four claim sites (`api-payload-contracts.md` §Plan-029, `Plan-029 §API And Transport Changes`, `Plan-029` T2.4's enumerated gate test, and the dated `Plan-029 §Notes` record, which keeps its provenance and takes a superseding pointer); four refusal codes registered (plane census seven → eleven); local SQLite **56 → 57** (`provider_account_usage_windows`) re-derived by direct `CREATE TABLE` count on the merged tree and mirrored in `README.md` + `CLAUDE.md` in the same PR; Postgres unmoved at 26; the Spec-006 taxonomy censuses unmoved at 156 / 20; `Spec-026` deliberately **not** flipped and taking nothing, so its "no field, flag, or environment variable anywhere in this flow" statement stays true as written. Four repairs carried by this diff are **ripple-check findings rather than bundle scope**, recorded here so the diff's width is legible: the `Spec-006 §Usage Telemetry (usage_telemetry)` preamble and the `Spec-013 §Rate-Limit Display` update-mechanism bullet each still restated a superseded payload/key and were swept (both stale since the 2026-08-18 re-key, so this diff is the second widening to reach them); eleven inbound line cites into `Spec-006` from `Plan-003` and `Plan-009` — already drifted before this diff and pushed two further by its blockquote insertion — were converted to the durable unbackticked marker-line `§Heading` form, which is **audit-layer rather than gate-verified** in that namespace (a fabricated heading was confirmed to pass, so the byte-match was performed by hand); two governance line cites in `.github/workflows/ci.yml` were converted after this diff pushed one onto a blank line, with the lane gap that hid them recorded as a CAT-06 Known Gap; and `tools/docs-corpus/lib/inbound-cite-discovery.ts` gained the `maxBuffer` its sibling call already carried — the governance corpus's largest doc has been past `spawnSync`'s 1 MB default since before this branch, so the runner was crashing with an empty message on any staged set that read that file from the index rather than the working tree.; [Spec-028 §Non-Goals](../specs/028-mcp-server-configuration-and-governance.md#non-goals)'s token-custody bullet carrying the MCP-plane scope [Plan-028 I-028-1](../plans/028-mcp-server-configuration-and-governance.md#i-028-1--no-credential-custody) already states, recorded as a dated erratum in that spec and **cited** from ADR-028's §Related Specs And Plans rather than characterized there, with Spec-028's Status unmoved at `approved` and the specs census unmoved at 29; and one corpus-integrity repair carried by the same diff — `lang_altertable` backticked at all twelve bare-prose sites across five docs, after a single added emphasis pair on this repo's 44k-character CLAUDE.md line silently re-parsed that identifier thousands of characters away into `lang*altertable`, a non-local failure mode that Prettier surfaces as a format error rather than as the content corruption it is; and the round-1 Codex fold's own census effects re-derived by direct count — `provideraccount.*` refusal codes eleven → **twelve** (`provider_version_below_floor`, which T3.4's version floor required and no code represented), the `providerAccount` namespace unmoved at **ten** verbs (the opt-out rides `update`, re-supply rides `register`), and local SQLite unmoved at **57** (the three provider-reported identity columns and the four token-lifecycle columns all land on the unshipped `provider_accounts` CREATE, consuming no migration ordinal) Round 2's eleven findings folded in one pass with no census move: SQLite **57** unmoved (`removal_intent` and the three identity columns land on the unshipped `provider_accounts` CREATE and consume no migration ordinal), Postgres **26**, `providerAccount` verbs **10**, `provideraccount.*` error codes **12**, plans **29**, specs **29**, accepted ADRs **27** — the one count that moves is the brokered-output field whitelist, three → four, re-derived across `Spec-029 §Brokered interactive sign-in` and the `ProviderAccountLoginResponse` contract.

### NS-80: Rate-Limit Wiring — The Three Unowned `Spec-021` Enforcement Legs Given Owners

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-08-25 via the rate-limit wiring amendment — the restoring targeted readiness-audit delta rides the amendment's own diff, the NS-63 / NS-65..NS-74 in-swap flip-and-restore shape, so Spec-021, Plan-021, Plan-008, Plan-014, and Plan-002 all return to `approved` within the same swap)
- Type: governance
- Priority: `P1`
- Upstream: none as a §6 edge — the obligating condition is a standing corpus gap plus a set of user-ratified product decisions (2026-08-25) on the live-connection cap value, the dormant-row posture for `artifact.publish`, and the invite-cap refusal wording. `Spec-021`'s Tier-6 audit priced twenty-five endpoint groups and its D-021-6 wiring-ownership table assigned each one an owner, but three assignments named a plan without naming a task, so the obligations lived only in backlog sentinels (BL-120, BL-144, BL-146) and no plan-side dispatch could ever reach them.
- References: [Spec-021 §Canonical Endpoint Group Registry](../specs/021-rate-limiting-policy.md#canonical-endpoint-group-registry), [Spec-021 §Overflow Response](../specs/021-rate-limiting-policy.md#overflow-response), [Spec-021 §ADR Triggers](../specs/021-rate-limiting-policy.md#adr-triggers), [Plan-021 §Cross-Plan Obligations](../plans/021-rate-limiting-policy.md#cross-plan-obligations) (CP-021-6) + §Endpoint wiring ownership (D-021-6), [Plan-008 §Preconditions](../plans/008-control-plane-relay-and-session-join.md#preconditions) (Phase R5, I-008-15, CP-008-17), [Plan-014 §Preconditions](../plans/014-artifacts-files-and-attachments.md#preconditions) (T14.14, T14.15, I-014-14, CP-014-9), [Plan-002 §Preconditions](../plans/002-invite-membership-and-presence.md#preconditions) (T4.3), [Spec-002 §Rate Limiting](../specs/002-invite-membership-and-presence.md#rate-limiting) (the `concurrency_cap` refusal envelope), [BL-120](../archive/backlog-archive.md#bl-120-plan-002-phase-4-invite-endpoint-rate-limit-wiring-tier-6-deferral) / [BL-144](../archive/backlog-archive.md#bl-144-eventsubscribe-sse-concurrency-cap-enforcement-5-concurrentparticipant) / [BL-146](../archive/backlog-archive.md#bl-146-artifactpublish-rate-limit-wiring-plan-014-tier-7) (archived in the same PR)
- Summary: Give the three unowned `Spec-021` enforcement legs named owners in the plans that own their surfaces, and close the three sentinels into those tasks. **(1) `event.subscribe` → Plan-008 Phase R5.** The row is a `concurrency_cap`, and the finding that shaped the phase is that it **cannot** ride `rateLimitProcedure`: read first-hand in the pinned `@trpc/server@11.17.0` distribution, a subscription procedure's middleware runs, but a thrown `TRPCError` is emitted through `errorToAsyncIterable` as an in-stream SSE error under an already-`200` `text/event-stream` response, with `initResponse` called on `errors: []` so `responseMeta` cannot observe it either — an HTTP `429` is unreachable from middleware. The refusal therefore lands in `buildControlPlaneFetchHandler` before `fetchRequestHandler` (the D-021-10 raw-route precedent), and `I-008-15` additionally forbids anything in front of it rewriting the status into a `5xx`: a conforming WHATWG `EventSource` fails the connection on **every** non-`200` and reconnects on none, so the hazard a rewrite creates is not a retry storm but a misdescribed refusal — `429` names a caller-side limit the caller clears by closing a subscription, while `5xx` names a server fault and licenses the client's and the operator's outage handling. Slot release ships in three parts (generator `finally`, `signal` abort with `enable_request_signal` declared, and a TTL backstop expressed as a declared multiple of `SSE_HEARTBEAT_INTERVAL_MS`) because [workerd #6832](https://github.com/cloudflare/workerd/issues/6832) is open: a stream's `cancel()` no longer fires on client disconnect, and a leaked slot fails **closed against an honest participant**. `I-008-15` closes the third property the pair implies — what a cap does when its own lease store is down — by applying `Spec-021 §Fallback Behavior` **unmodified**: grace-period `degraded` admission, then `503` `ratelimit.backend_unavailable`, with the outage-versus-cap-trip distinction carried by `rate_limit_backend_error_total` rather than by the status. A draft status deviation (refuse `429`, never `503`) was **withdrawn** at Codex round 2 once its premise — that a conforming `EventSource` reconnects on 5xx — was checked against the processing model, which fails the connection on every non-`200`. One acceptance criterion appended **last** (so the existing AC1–AC8 keep the positional identity Plan-021's `Spec-021 AC8` cite depends on) covers all three properties. The cap is re-priced 5 → 10 concurrent (user-ratified: a browser alone allows six connections per site, and desktop + CLI + tabs share one participant budget). **(2) The six `artifact.*` relay rows → Plan-014 T14.14 / T14.15**, split by landing phase because the upload surfaces ship in Phase 4 and the fetch surfaces in Phase 5 — different PRs, so one task spanning both would have been unbuildable. The upload transport is deliberately **not** invented (api-payload-contracts states the relay method shapes are "deliberately not typed here yet"); the obligation is written transport-invariantly instead as `I-014-14` — admission resolves before any request-body byte is consumed — with `artifact.fetch.chunk` settled independently by Spec-014 as a raw GET, consuming `checkAdmission` on the standing Plan-025 Fastify-hook precedent. `I-014-14`'s second clause repairs a pre-existing conflation in T14.9, which had claimed the six rows as its own backpressure: a request-rate `429` and a byte-quota `429` are different advice, and a caller that reads one as the other retries futilely or gives up prematurely. **(3) `invite.pending_cap` → Plan-002 T4.3**, enforced store-side inside the shipped `InviteService.createInvite` transaction after the parent-session `FOR UPDATE` lock and the owner probe — a placement that inherits the existing serialization, adds no lock-order edge, and refuses a non-owner before revealing invite volume — counting only pending-and-unexpired rows so a session's own history cannot exhaust its own cap. `Spec-002 §Rate Limiting`'s response snippet, which typed `retryAfter` as required for every invite row, is narrowed in the same swap to the enforcement-class-conditional shape `error-contracts.md` already types — the divergence was inert while nothing enforced the cap, and T4.3 makes it live. **(4) `artifact.publish` gets no owner, deliberately**: no control-plane method string or tRPC procedure for artifact publication is registered anywhere in the corpus, so the row joins the dormant class on the `approval.resolve` template with a new §ADR Triggers re-arm bullet and **no backlog item**. One further finding is recorded rather than acted on: no maintained JS rate-limiting library implements a concurrency cap — `rate-limiter-flexible` (this corpus's own sliding-window backend, latest `11.2.0`, 2026-06-08) offers points/duration consumption and a FIFO queue, and Cloudflare's `rate_limit` binding is window-based — so the cap is hand-rolled on a Durable Object whose whole prune → count → insert runs inside one `state.storage.transaction()` (hosted — single-threading is necessary and not sufficient, since the runtime's input gate re-opens across any non-storage await) or in-process (single-process self-host, which refuses to construct against a declared multi-process deployment), and no dependency is added. **Codex round 2 added four further legs to that store and its host**: the lease is owned by the host until dispatch takes it through a single-shot context accessor, so a request refused before the subscription resolver returns releases its slot instead of holding it for a TTL; an alarm armed at the earliest expiry deletes expired rows and re-arms only while live leases remain, since pruning-on-read reclaims a slot but never a row; the max-renewals branch **closes** the stream in the same act as relinquishing the lease, because a released lease beside a live stream is an uncounted subscription; and `CP-021-6` gains a fourth part, `checkCapAdmission` + `recordCapViolation`, because the shipped `check` fuses block lookup with counter consumption and `recordViolation` is internal — without the pair a cap owner must either double-price its row or bypass the escalation ladder.
- Exit Criteria: all six Statuses `review → approved` within the same swap (Spec-021, Plan-021, Plan-008, Plan-014, Plan-002, and Spec-002 — the last for its one-part `concurrency_cap` refusal-envelope narrowing), each plan's audit box re-checked with a scoped Re-opened/Delivered record; `Spec-021`'s registry at 25 rows with `event.subscribe` at 10 concurrent and `artifact.publish` marked dormant; CP-021-6 ⇄ CP-008-17 and CP-014-9 ⇄ the D-021-6 relay row registered bidirectionally; Plan-008's Tier-5 test census re-derived 117 → 135 and Plan-014's task count thirteen → fifteen, both by direct count; the preflight Gate-4 corpus pin re-derived in the same PR by direct count over the rebased tree (bold 914/158 → 917/159 against the baseline the NS-81 and NS-78 landings left, legacy 61 → 64, legacy-marker population 49 → 52); BL-120, BL-144, and BL-146 moved whole to the backlog archive with dated closure lines that state what did **and did not** land; no interface, wire member, method string, error code, table, or column minted, so the SQLite (56) and Postgres (26) censuses and the README plan/spec censuses are unmoved.

The audit of the pinned build surfaced four behaviors the plan had not accounted for, each adjudicated into task text rather than cataloged: parse refusals and errors escaping a command body both reach the run context's **stdout** (the latter with a full stack trace under a hardcoded exit `1`, bypassing I-007-14); a command's static `schema` typanion cascade is applied inside `validateAndExecute()` and throws from there **before** `execute()` runs, so the base class's error boundary must override `validateAndExecute()` — an `execute()`-only boundary leaks a schema-validation failure to stdout on the same hardcoded `1`; `enableCapture: true` throws under a pure-ESM bundle whenever the context streams are injected, so the defect is latent in production and fires exactly in the test configuration; and the parse-error classes are exported through neither the package root nor any subpath, so classification must be by `error.name` and the library's own `error.clipanion` discriminator. ### NS-76: Spec-005/Plan-005 Provider-Bound Text Neutrality Targeted Readiness-Audit Delta — Restoring Re-Audit

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-08-25 via the provider-bound text-neutrality amendment — the restoring targeted readiness-audit delta rides the amendment's own diff, the NS-63/NS-65..NS-74 in-swap flip-and-restore shape, so Spec-005 and Plan-005 return to `approved` within the same swap. **Scope: the driver's outbound text boundary only** — no capability flag, driver operation, event kind, table, or column is minted, and the driver-result vocabulary is restated unwidened.)
- Priority: `P1`
- Upstream: none as a §6 edge — the obligating event is the closure of [BL-148](../archive/backlog-archive.md), whose exit criteria named `Spec-005` as the settling surface (the NS-42..NS-74 amendment-node shape). ID note: the NS ids adjacent to this one are held by sibling vehicles of the same sprint landing in their own PRs, so this diff moves the §6 census by exactly one node.
- References: [Spec-005 §Required Behavior](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md#required-behavior), [Spec-005 §Parity Capability Mechanism Grades](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md#parity-capability-mechanism-grades), [Plan-005 §Preconditions](../plans/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md#preconditions), [Plan-005 §Phase 3 — Codex + Claude driver implementations](../plans/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md#phase-3--codex--claude-driver-implementations) (T3.18), [error-contracts.md §Driver](contracts/error-contracts.md#driver), [Queue And Intervention Model §Driver Result To Lifecycle Mapping](../domain/queue-and-intervention-model.md#driver-result-to-lifecycle-mapping) (the intervention-path landing), [Spec-017 §Command interception — the reserved `/` prefix (C-18)](../specs/017-workflow-authoring-and-execution.md#command-interception--the-reserved--prefix-c-18) (the residual this settles, and the downstream `//`-escape consumer it gates), [ADR-027](../decisions/027-chat-invoked-workflow-start.md), [BL-148](../archive/backlog-archive.md).
- Summary: Make it normative that participant-authored text bound for a provider reaches the model as prose, or the turn fails visibly. The hazard is delivery, not authorization: a provider CLI that command-parses its programmatic input swallows a message whose first word is command-shaped and answers with a zero-turn success, which every layer above this system reads as a completed turn — verified first-party at authoring against Claude Code `2.1.245` and codex-cli `0.149.1` rather than inherited from a prior record. The settlement is three rules, not one transform, because a transform alone is a claim about a parser this repo neither owns nor pins: a **transport-only** neutralization at the driver's outbound frame boundary that never mutates the text the repo persists, events, replays, rewinds to, or shows a participant; a closed **frame-origin** discriminator whose absent or unrecognized arm neutralizes, so the seam fails closed and a future driver-composed command surface (`model_mutation` the plausible first — V1 emits no such frame) has a declared route rather than an exemption cut in later; and a **runtime tripwire** that fails the turn when a provider dispatches a frame as a command anyway. Coverage is **structural**: the child process's writable handle is encapsulated by the shared frame writer, so a later provider-bound path cannot bypass neutralization by forgetting to call it, where an audited call-site list decays on its first addition. Plan-005 T3.18 builds it across all three provider-bound paths — a run's opening content, a steer directive's content, and admitted queue content re-entering through `startRun` — under I-005-7. The refusal's landing is **one** landing for both provider-bound paths, and it is on the run rather than on either caller's response: the daemon emits the run's ordinary `run.failed` terminal carrying `failureCategory: 'provider failure'`, `recoveryCondition: 'recovery-needed'`, and a `providerFailureDetail` led by the registered code and naming the frame's origin — CP-005-5's already-resolved handoff shape, minting no driver event, no new result **status**, and no persisted column. Neither path can raise a JSON-RPC error, and the run-start path could take no synchronous refusal at all — `startRun` is daemon-internal with no wire method behind it, and a queued or orchestration-started run has no caller waiting, so the existing `run.failed` kind is the **asynchronous run outcome** that path surfaces through. An intervention does have a caller, so it also settles `degraded` on the existing zero-effect arm (the frame was dispatched, so pre-dispatch `rejected` is out of reach) with no `fallbackAction` and with the cause on one additive-optional closed-literal `refusalCode` member the driver result envelope gains here — best-effort, set only when the trip is classified before the call resolves, the run terminal staying the guarantee on both paths — consumed by Plan-004 T2.6 under the already-registered CP-004-1, whose row widens by one clause on a recorded no-flip. A tripped intervention **fails the run and disposes its provider binding**: the terminal state alone would leave the process holding possibly-mutated client-side state alive for the next run to bind to, so the quarantine is disposal — costing no `runtime_bindings` column, which this plan prohibits. The boundary and the tripwire are universal while the **transform is grade-scoped**, which makes `Spec-005 §Parity Capability Mechanism Grades` a behavioral input rather than a bare record — so that row states the grade governing today: the Codex leg's only verbatim-delivery evidence is `codex exec`, a different frontend from the app-server transport the driver drives, so it is graded **`emulated`** and neutralizes until T3.18's currency step probes that transport, the confirming re-grade being an ordinary amendment. The default is the transform rather than its absence. Non-delivery, not no-effect, is what gets recorded; the run halts rather than continuing and its binding is retired: a provider that dispatched the frame as a command may have run an unrecognized client-side action against the session state that run depends on, so `recovery-needed` asks a human to reconcile and a fresh spawn — not a re-attach — is how work resumes.
- Exit Criteria: Spec-005 and Plan-005 Statuses `approved → review → approved` within the diff, with both Plan-005 §Preconditions boxes carrying scoped Re-opened/re-checked records; T3.18 present in **Phase 3** (not Phase 3B) with the full marker set, `Spec coverage:` markers byte-compared against the real Spec-005 headings in the unbackticked spec-plus-heading form, and an explicit statement that it dispatches with Phase 3 on that phase's met gates; I-005-7 grounded in a named Spec-005 clause; **no** CP minted and **no** carrier box minted, the Spec-017 escape gate recorded as task-scoped reviewer-checkable prose on the NS-73 precedent; `driver.text_neutralization_failed` registered reserved against T3.18 at 409 with its status choice justified against the 502/503 alternative; every count claim whose set moved re-derived from the files — `Plan-005 §Done Checklist` invariants 5 → 7 plus the missing Phase 3B row and the AC8 extension, this document's §2 `provider/drivers/` Phase-3 file count 12 → 13, and the §API And Transport Changes driver-code enumeration completed and extended to seven — while SQLite 56, Postgres 26, plans 29, specs 29, and ADR 26-accepted stay unmoved and the README plan-status census reads unchanged because both flips restore in-diff; the Gate-4 marker pin moved to the live figures with the delta matching the new markers one-for-one; all inbound `Spec-005:NNN` cites re-swept before the header blockquote's line shift landed and split on the live-versus-provenance rule (all seventeen that remain are immutable §Shipment Manifest merge-time provenance, deliberately untouched; no live inbound line cite into Spec-005 exists elsewhere in the repo); BL-148 archived `completed` with its gate re-homed onto the landed contract across Spec-017, Plan-017 I-017-17, and ADR-027 as an erratum-class repoint carrying no Status flip, dated provenance cells left frozen.
- Landing-time note: the composer-side `//`-escape activation on provider-bound paths — a Plan-017 / Plan-023 change — is deliberately **not** in this diff and remains unassigned. It can only activate once T3.18's **code** merges, not once this doc amendment does, so it properly sequences behind a code lane; activating it here would flip Spec-017 and author tasks outside this node's scope.

### NS-82: Spec-014/Plan-014 Relay TTL-Sweep Disposition Targeted Readiness-Audit Delta — Restoring Re-Audit

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-08-26 via the relay TTL-sweep disposition amendment PR — the restoring targeted readiness-audit delta riding the same diff, the NS-63/NS-65..NS-74 in-swap shape. **Scope: the relay blob lifecycle only** — no interface, wire member, method string, error code, or table is minted; the sole schema growth is one additive nullable column and one partial index, both on a table Plan-014 already owns.)
- Priority: `P2`
- Upstream: none as a §6 edge — the obligating event is the disposition [BL-152](../archive/backlog-archive.md) recorded, which the 2026-08-17 ingest-protocol hardening amendment (NS-70) deliberately flagged rather than settled because its own fact-keyed write-back rule was correct under either candidate reading. ID note: **NS-79 and NS-83 are held by sibling vehicles of the same sprint landing in their own PRs** (NS-75, NS-76, NS-77, NS-78, NS-80, and NS-81 are already in-tree — NS-76 merged as `develop` 6a0998d0 before this branch's final rebase), so this node claims its ID out of order. Node census re-derived by direct count over the §Graph nodes of this diff’s merged tree (the same `NS13a` / `NS13b` split-id pattern admitted; the heading-only `### NS-27` entry carries no graph node and is not counted) — the §6 census at this node's merge was **81 nodes, 79 `completed`, 2 `blocked` (NS-09, NS-10)** — 80 / 78 on `develop` 6a0998d0 plus this node — with the `NS-15..NS-21` heading covering seven of them and five further nodes declared in the graph without a `###` entry of their own, which is why the heading count is lower.
- References: [Spec-014 §TTL sweep disposition (V1)](../specs/014-artifacts-files-and-attachments.md#ttl-sweep-disposition-v1) (the settled rule), [Spec-014 §Delete (refcount + TTL + crypto-shred)](../specs/014-artifacts-files-and-attachments.md#delete-refcount--ttl--crypto-shred) (step 8's per-path row disposition), [Spec-014 §Fetch (authenticated; relay-served in V1)](../specs/014-artifacts-files-and-attachments.md#fetch-authenticated-relay-served-in-v1) (the retired BL-152 flag; the unchanged fact-keyed write-back), [Plan-014 §Preconditions](../plans/014-artifacts-files-and-attachments.md#preconditions) (both boxes' 2026-08-26 Re-opened/Delivered records), [Plan-014 §Invariants](../plans/014-artifacts-files-and-attachments.md#invariants) (I-014-15 new; I-014-5 extended), [Plan-014 §Implementation Phase Sequence](../plans/014-artifacts-files-and-attachments.md#implementation-phase-sequence) (T14.8 Phase 5, T14.9 Phase 6), [Shared Postgres Schema §Artifact Relay Blob Store](schemas/shared-postgres-schema.md#artifact-relay-blob-store-plan-014) (`bytes_reclaimed_at` and the `idx_artifact_relay_blobs_unreclaimed` partial index), [Spec-022 §PII Data Map](../specs/022-data-retention-and-gdpr.md#pii-data-map) and [§Shred Fan-Out](../specs/022-data-retention-and-gdpr.md#shred-fan-out) (the narrowing clauses), [error-contracts.md](contracts/error-contracts.md) (§Artifact producer pinning).
- Summary: Settle what the relay's hourly TTL sweep does with an expired blob's coordination row. **Decision: retain** — the sweep leaves a payload-free tombstone at `state = 'expired'`, having hard-DELETEd every recipient row for the digest (the wrapped-CEK crypto-shred) and set `state` in one intent transaction, then reclaims the object-store bytes and, in a second transaction, stamps the new `bytes_reclaimed_at` and `NULL`s `publisher_participant_id` together. Retain wins because only a surviving row can separate _was pinned, retention elapsed, re-publish restores_ (410) from _you hold no grant_ (zero-row 404), and because three commitments already in the corpus are false under the delete reading: `'expired'` exists in the blob-state set as the value a swept row carries, the §Failure modes mid-fetch row promises a resume gets 410 and "never a bare 404", and RFC 9110 §15.5.11 licenses a bounded gone-marker outright. **Refcount-gated delete was rejected on a factual ground** — the relay holds no content reference count (`ciphertext_digest` is the primary key and per-artifact CEKs preclude cross-publication dedup), so I-014-12's derived-CAS-refcount rule has no relay analogue and the reclaim is a plain idempotent object-store delete. **Retain-forever was rejected** as an unbounded metadata ledger inside a deliberately transient buffer; the bound is the new `relay_tombstone_grace` (30 d default, 24 h – 90 d), derived rather than picked — it equals both the `extended`-tier TTL ceiling and the erasure-SLA backup ceiling Spec-014 already carries. Two ordering rules carry the correctness: shred-then-reclaim-then-confirm, because the coordination row is the only index into the stored object and row-first deletion orphans bytes on a crash; and read-time liveness (`state = 'pinned' AND expires_at > now()`) checked **before** the thumbprint selector at the mint, so the 410 is correct in the up-to-an-hour gap before the sweep runs and gives the same answer on both sides of it. Leg placement follows buildability: the read-time and mint-ordering legs land on T14.8 in Phase 5 because they are correct with no sweep in existence, the sweep/purge/metrics on T14.9 in Phase 6 — the T14.14/T14.15 split precedent and Plan-014's gate-cannot-precede-its-call-site rule. **Spec-022 takes narrowing clauses on a recorded no-flip** (the CP-016-7 / B13 one-clause reciprocal-mirror precedent): the sweep applies dispositions that spec already assigns, under a second lifecycle-driven trigger, and the tombstone names no participant once its reclaim confirms — its one pre-reclaim reference being the anonymize-class `publisher_participant_id` FK Spec-022 already enumerates — so no §PII Data Map row is owed and no CP-022-6 leg is added at either stage. **Round-1 Codex fold (six findings, all accepted, riding this same in-swap flip** — no second flip and no second audit delta, on the NS-67 round-2-fold precedent): Publish is fenced against an in-flight reclaim (`state = 'expired' AND bytes_reclaimed_at IS NULL` refuses `429` + `Retry-After`, because the `SKIP LOCKED` claim's transaction commits before the external object-store delete and cannot serialize across it); the publisher identity is held to the reclaim confirmation so stored-but-unreclaimed bytes stay charged to their publisher instead of only to the node-wide cap; the cost of liveness-first is stated — the check subsumes the grant check, so a grantless session member meets the 410, with the 404's three producers re-scoped to live pins across Spec-014, the failure-mode table, and the error registry; one partial index (`(expires_at) WHERE state = 'expired' AND bytes_reclaimed_at IS NULL`) keeps the reclaim-retry pass off the ever-growing reclaimed population; the `SKIP LOCKED` claim gains its PostgreSQL primary source in a new Spec-014 §References subsection; and the unobtainable-payload write-back is re-homed from T14.9 to T14.8, since T14.8 now makes both refusals reachable and the 2026-08-17 buildability rule that placed it selects the earlier task once that is true. **Round-2 Codex fold (four findings, all accepted, riding the same in-swap flip):** two were residuals of the round-1 fold itself, repaired where they stood — T14.9's deliverable paragraph still claimed the write-back and still said "no second index is added", both contradicting the round-1 text elsewhere in the same task — and two were new. The reclaim's exclusion is extended past the publish fence to cover **sweep against sweep**: because `SKIP LOCKED`'s transaction commits before the external delete, two passes can hold one tombstone at `state = 'expired' AND bytes_reclaimed_at IS NULL`, the first confirming and lifting the fence while the second's delete is still in flight to destroy a re-pinned blob's fresh bytes, so stages (2) and (3) run under a session-level advisory lock keyed on the digest — chosen because a session-level advisory lock is held "until explicitly released or the session ends" and therefore spans an external call no transaction can, with its own PostgreSQL primary source added. And the two **removing** GC paths are ordered explicitly for the first time: they reclaim the object **before** removing the row, the mirror of the TTL path's order, safe because their trigger already establishes that no fetch is owed — the asymmetry the round-1 text asserted for the TTL path without saying what the other two do. No new interface, wire member, error code, table, or column: the advisory lock is a runtime primitive, not schema.
- Exit Criteria: Spec-014 and Plan-014 Statuses `approved → review → approved` within the diff, with both Plan-014 §Preconditions boxes carrying the literal `- [x]` marker plus 2026-08-26 Re-opened and Delivered records and no born-unchecked box minted; `Spec-014 §TTL sweep disposition (V1)` present and normative with the lifecycle/fetch-result table; I-014-15 minted and I-014-5 extended with the relay-side liveness predicate, with the same restatement carried into the `shared-postgres-schema.md` blob-state comment so the two surfaces do not disagree; T14.9's "presumes the retained-row reading" hedge struck and its quota-defaults count re-derived seven → eight; `artifact_relay_blobs.bytes_reclaimed_at` and the `idx_artifact_relay_blobs_unreclaimed` partial index added to the schema's first `CREATE TABLE` shape with no migration owed (no `artifact_relay_*` DDL has shipped — verified by `rg artifact_relay packages/ apps/` returning nothing); census unmoved — Postgres 26, SQLite 56, plans 29, specs 29, ADRs 26 accepted, error-contracts §Artifact reserved rows ten (the round-1 fold adds one partial index and one acceptance criterion, neither of which is a counted table, code, or wire member); [BL-152](../archive/backlog-archive.md) archived with a dated closure line, `docs/backlog.md` left equal to `develop` minus that one entry — and the headless three-field residue PR #358's BL-154 archival left behind it removed under the §Housekeeping Exception, since a stub naming no item is not an active backlog entry; and the §6 census at 81 nodes / 79 `completed` / 2 `blocked`. **Coherence sweep carried in the same diff** — the guarantee this disposition bounds in time is restated on surfaces the 2026-08-08 threat-model scoping had already enumerated, so each takes the matching bound: `README.md` feature-14 row, [v1-feature-scope.md](v1-feature-scope.md) row 14, [data-architecture.md](data-architecture.md) §Artifact Storage, [ADR-015](../decisions/015-v1-feature-scope-definition.md) (§Decision row 14, the C4 rationale, and a dated §Decision Log row on the 2026-08-08 precedent — not an amendment, ADR stays `accepted`, no feature-count census moves), and the **recipient-side** twin in [Local SQLite Schema §Artifact Tables (Plan-014)](schemas/local-sqlite-schema.md#artifact-tables-plan-014), which I-014-5 now names beside the relay-side Postgres comment.
