### NS-84: ADR-029 Canonical Transcript Authority, Same-Agent Provider Switch, And The Turn-Scoped Effective-Principal Carrier

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-08-26 via the canonical-transcript-authority and same-agent-provider-switch amendment PR — the restoring targeted readiness-audit deltas ride the same diff, the NS-63/NS-65..NS-82 in-swap shape, across all five flipped pairs. **Scope: the provider-continuity boundary** — one ADR minted `accepted`, two event types, one error code, three `agents` columns on an unshipped `CREATE`, one capability flag (a second was drafted and withdrawn), and no wire method, no Cedar action, and no table.)
- Priority: `P1`
- Upstream: none as a §6 edge. Three obligating facts, all already in-tree: [ADR-017](../decisions/017-shared-event-sourcing-scope.md)'s 2026-07-02 row settled the log's authority over a provider's reported session _position_ but never over its _content_; `Spec-016 §Interfaces And Contracts` (A-016-2) required `driverName` at attach and omitted it from `AgentConfigUpdate`; and NS-71 gave every intervention a durable admitting principal without giving any metering surface a way to read it. ID note: **NS-83 and NS-79 both landed ahead of this node** — NS-83 the provider-accounts bundle, which also took the `028` ADR ordinal, so this node's ADR is `029`, renumbered at rebase rather than re-argued; NS-79 the `sidekicks` CLI executable-name canonicalization (Plan-007), merged while this branch was open and taken by rebase. No sibling vehicle of this sprint is still open behind it, so this node's `84 nodes / 82 completed / 2 blocked` graph census is the direct count over **this** diff's rebased tree and is not expected to move again before merge. NS-75..NS-78 and NS-80..NS-82 are already in-tree.
- References: [ADR-029](../decisions/029-canonical-transcript-is-authoritative.md) (the ruling and its enumerated gate/fallback table), [Spec-005 §Canonical Transcript Export And Replay](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md#canonical-transcript-export-and-replay) (the driver-boundary contract), [Spec-016 §Same-Agent Provider Switch](../specs/016-multi-agent-channels-and-orchestration.md#same-agent-provider-switch) (the mutation surface), [Spec-006 §Channel and Agent Lifecycle](../specs/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#channel-and-agent-lifecycle-session_lifecycle) and [§Usage Telemetry](../specs/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#usage-telemetry-usage_telemetry) (the minted event and the effective-principal member), [Spec-004 §Required Behavior](../specs/004-queue-steer-pause-resume.md#required-behavior) (the publication clause), [Spec-013 §Timeline Entry Types](../specs/013-live-timeline-visibility-and-reasoning-surfaces.md#timeline-entry-types) (the one-line status row), [api-payload-contracts.md §Authenticated Principal And Authorization Model](contracts/api-payload-contracts.md#authenticated-principal-and-authorization-model) (instance (4) and its two stated shape deviations).
- Summary: Three settlements in one swap. **(1) ADR-029 lands `accepted`** (ADR census 27 → 28): the daemon's canonical transcript — a projection rebuilt from `session_events`, never a store — is the authority for the content of a provider session, and every provider session is a replay target. Provider-native continuity verbs stay the hot path but become capability-gated optimizations, each with a named daemon-side fallback, enumerated in a five-row table so the synthesis is checkable by count rather than by assurance. The strongest antithesis — that sufficiency cannot be proved for provider-private state — is answered by **narrowing the claim** to visibility sufficiency, declared loss, and named non-portability rather than by rebuttal. Option E records why no off-the-shelf format was adopted: ACP replays agent→client only and accepts no history at session creation, OTel GenAI is `stability: development` with plaintext reasoning, and the two organizations best placed to define a portable transcript each built adapters for both of this project's CLIs and declined to. **(2) The same-agent provider switch**: `agent.configUpdate` gains `driverName?` / `providerAccountId?` / `effort?` / `interruptAndSwitch?`, applying at the next boundary the target axis permits — a **turn** boundary for an axis the target driver accepts as a per-turn override (Codex `turn/start` takes per-turn `model` / `effort`), a **run** boundary for a spawn-bound one, which `driverName` and `providerAccountId` are on every driver because Spec-029 binds a run's account for the run's lifetime and a different vendor is a different binary. The split is read from the driver's declared vocabulary rather than assumed, it preserves Spec-029's run-binding rule instead of carving it out, and it is what keeps the receipt's per-paying-account key exact. Mutation and application are two moments, and the response shape says so: it is a **discriminated union**, a `pending` arm naming the resolved boundary, the daemon-minted `switchId`, and any intent it superseded, and an `applied` arm reachable only through `interruptAndSwitch` — the one path that collapses the two moments. The pending intent is **durable and singular** on a third `agents` column, so a restart re-arms it instead of breaking a promise already acknowledged, and a second provider-axis update supersedes rather than queues (queueing would apply a participant's abandoned first choice, run a turn on it, and then replace it). Every non-superseded pending switch reaches exactly **one** terminal: `agent.provider_switched` at application — `continuity` closed at three arms, `in_place` for a per-turn override carried on the running process, `replayed`, and `memo`, with the declared-loss list arm-scoped so an empty list keeps meaning "nothing was dropped" — or `agent.provider_switch_failed`, the second minted type, because a caller acknowledged and since disconnected is reachable only through an event and an event named `switched` is the wrong record of a switch that did not happen. The immediate arm dispatches the **existing** `interrupt` intervention, so Spec-004's V1 control set stays closed on the NS-73 edit-affordance precedent, and no Cedar action is minted because the two authorizations the switch needs both already exist. **(3) The turn-scoped effective-principal carrier**: `usage.cost_update` carries the turn's daemon-resolved `effectivePrincipal`, resolved by Plan-004 T3.19 from the NS-71 `interventions` rows and stamped by Plan-005's usage normalizer. ### NS-86: Spec-030/Plan-030 Sidekick Definitions, Peer Invocation, And The Plan-028 Effective-Binding Discharge

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-08-26 via the sidekick-definitions and peer-invocation amendment PR — the new pair's first-time targeted readiness audit and every restoring delta ride the same diff, the NS-74 in-swap mint shape extended across the documents it flips — eight after the round-1 review fold added the Spec-006/Plan-006 pair)
- Type: `governance`
- Priority: `P1`
- Upstream: none as a §6 edge. Three obligating facts, all already in-tree. (1) A sidekick's configuration — provider, model, effort, posture mode, instructions, goal, tool allowlist, paying account — was expressible **only** inline on `agent.attach`, so the same collaborator had to be re-described on every attach and could not be named, versioned, or corrected in one place. (2) `Spec-016 §Default Behavior` admitted child runs only "by user request or workflow definition", which left a sidekick no way to consult another sidekick even where the orchestration pipeline, the `spawn` / `delegate` link types, and the depth rule already supported it. (3) [Plan-028](../plans/028-mcp-server-configuration-and-governance.md)'s §Preconditions carried a born-unchecked effective-binding box holding **T28.4.9**, minted when the Tier-7 audit found no registered carrier for the binding a tool actually resolved from.
- References: [Spec-030](../specs/030-sidekick-definitions-and-peer-invocation.md) + [Plan-030](../plans/030-sidekick-definitions-and-peer-invocation.md) (the new pair), [Spec-028 §Trust Governance](../specs/028-mcp-server-configuration-and-governance.md#trust-governance) + [Plan-028 §Cross-Plan Obligations](../plans/028-mcp-server-configuration-and-governance.md#cross-plan-obligations) (I-028-6, CP-028-7, T28.4.11), [Spec-012 §Implementation Notes](../specs/012-approvals-permissions-and-trust-boundaries.md#implementation-notes) (the named-action enumeration, five → seven), [Spec-016 §Default Behavior](../specs/016-multi-agent-channels-and-orchestration.md#default-behavior) (the third child-run-origin arm), [Plan-016 §Cross-Plan Obligations](../plans/016-multi-agent-channels-and-orchestration.md#cross-plan-obligations) (CP-016-18 + the Phase 3B supplement), [Plan-023 §Cross-Plan Obligations](../plans/023-desktop-shell-and-renderer.md#cross-plan-obligations) (CP-023-6), [Spec-006 §Session Lifecycle](../specs/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#session-lifecycle-session_lifecycle) + [Plan-006 §Event Taxonomy Coverage](../plans/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#event-taxonomy-coverage) (the `session.peer_invocation_set` registration, taxonomy 158 → 159), [error-contracts.md §Sidekick Definitions](contracts/error-contracts.md#sidekick-definitions), [api-payload-contracts.md §Plan-030 — Sidekick Definitions And Peer Invocation](contracts/api-payload-contracts.md#plan-030--sidekick-definitions-and-peer-invocation), [local-sqlite-schema.md](schemas/local-sqlite-schema.md).
- Summary: Three settlements in one swap. **(1) The definition registry.** `sidekick_definitions` (SQLite, census 57 → 58) makes a sidekick a saved, named, node-local record, and `agent.attach` gains an additive-optional `definitionId` resolved daemon-side. Identity is a daemon-minted opaque immutable `definitionId` and never the mutable `name`, on the `ProviderAccountId` discipline NS-74 established. The attached agent is a **snapshot**: editing or deleting a definition reaches no running agent, because a live reference would let an edit widen an already-attached agent's allowlist, posture, or paying account without that widening ever passing the attach-time authorization that admitted it. Explicitly-present request members merge **per field** over the definition's values with the effective resolved configuration echoed back — a precedence-refusal was considered and rejected, since it would force every caller to know a definition's contents before composing a request. Resolution fails closed and substitutes nothing; a pinned account that has left the registry refuses rather than silently becoming "whichever account is default now". Definitions are node-local and are never relayed, published, or joined. **(2) Peer invocation.** `ask_sidekick` (link `spawn`) and `delegate_to_sidekick` (link `delegate`) are served into a session's existing callback-tool registry, reaching Codex as function-form dynamic tools and Claude through the daemon-hosted ephemeral MCP server. Both target a **sidekick** — a session agent or a saved definition — never a provider or a model. Both are registered into that registry **unconditionally** at spawn — filtered only by the resolved agent's tool allowlist (I-030-10) — and every invocation is adjudicated per call as `Action::"sidekick::invoke"` with the session's projected enablement flag supplied as Cedar context, so a session that has not opted in answers `denied` on a tool that is nonetheless present. The single opt-in act is the user request `Spec-016 §Default Behavior` requires, so `Spec-016 §Default Behavior` gains a third child-run-origin arm and `Spec-012 §Implementation Notes` gains the two named actions `Action::"sidekick::manage"` / `Action::"sidekick::invoke"` (enumeration five → seven). The created run is admitted through the ordinary pipeline, so the one-layer nesting rule and `orchestration.depth_exceeded` apply without restatement, and spend lands on the child's **own** cost-receipt row under the target's paying account — an ordinary value of an existing axis, so `aggregationScope` stays REQUIRED and closed at `"run-only"` and no receipt **contract** growth is owed. `Spec-016 §Session Cost Receipt` does take one added rule — a peer-invoked run's spend attributes, on the per-caused-by axis, to the effective principal of the **turn that issued the call**, never to the `system` arm — but that is a resolution narrowing on an existing axis rather than a fold change: it settles which participant an already-present arm names, and mints no member, axis, or scope. **(3) The Plan-028 box, discharged the NS-64 way — by making the carrier unnecessary rather than registering one.** On the invocation side T28.4.6 already builds the composed snapshot **from** the post-drift read, so the session's effective binding is a pure function of state Plan-028 already holds: new **T28.4.11** derives it in-plan and Plan-005's `driver_tools` seam is never touched. On the durable side a carrier could not have helped — recovery runs with no session, and re-resolution is exactly what `Spec-015` forbids — so the binding **identity** is stamped as one additive-nullable `command_receipts.mcp_binding_digest` (CP-028-7), a `"b3:"`-prefixed keyed BLAKE3 over the RFC 8785 JCS canonicalization of the `McpServerBindingRef` tuple, deliberately **excluding** the config hash so a drift-triggered revocation still matches receipts stamped before the drift, and carrying no filesystem path into a durable row. New **I-028-6** makes revocation neutralize the durable surface as well as the live one, and the neutralization is placed in **T28.4.4** — the single revocation writer both the operator and drift entries funnel through — so a future third entry inherits it by construction. No lock-ordering row is owed: every `§1 Lock Ordering` registrant locks control-plane Postgres rows, while `command_receipts` and the `mcp_*` tables are local SQLite under a single writer. **Round-1 review fold (Codex, PR #368 — twelve findings, all adjudicated into normative content).** Three of them collapsed into one redesign of the peer-invocation seam. Grant-gated tool registration was withdrawn: `callbackTools` rides only the session-creation and resume parameter shapes and the corpus has no live-registry mutation seam, so a registry filtered by enablement is frozen at spawn — enabling mid-session would change nothing observable, and withdrawal would leave a live leg holding a revoked capability. Both tools are now registered unconditionally and adjudicated per call on the landed `workflow_start` precedent, which makes both directions effective on the next invocation. That in turn re-homed the opt-in: a remembered approval rule is **unrepresentable** for a named-operation action (`remembered_approval_rules` closes its category enum over the approval-pipeline categories and requires an `approval_resolutions` reference), and this corpus projects no session-configuration table, so enablement became the minted `session.peer_invocation_set` event — the session-goal shape — read by Cedar as **context**. A definition's `toolAllowlist` now filters the daemon's own curated tools too (**I-030-10**), closing a hole where an allowlist bound provider-native tools while admitting the two that start runs. **I-030-11** closes two more: a peer-invoked child run resolves no effective principal under either existing arm, so the invoking turn's principal is stamped at creation on `run_links.invoking_principal_id` (**CP-030-4** ⇄ **CP-016-19**, refusing before admission when unresolvable), and every terminal state of an `ask_sidekick` child now settles the waiting call rather than leaving it blocked. **I-030-7** was re-specified: the two-layer split of full-Unicode folding in the service over an ASCII `COLLATE NOCASE` index does not hold, because the layer doing the real comparison is the one that cannot be atomic — the index now arbitrates a stored `name_folded` key. On the Plan-028 side, **T28.4.12** was added to own the binding-digest migration and the receipt-write argument (the column had a DDL and an invariant reading it but no creator or writer, which would have made the neutralization sweep silently vacuous), and **I-028-6** gained its key-loss arm: the digest is keyed, so an unavailable binding-identity subkey means a revocation cannot recompute what it covers — unmatchable is now treated as revoked rather than untouched. Contract-shape corrections in the same fold: the attach members were moved onto `AgentAttachRequest`/`AgentAttachResponse` (two standalone helper interfaces composed with nothing), `SidekickDefinitionListRequest` was declared, and the `sidekick.definition_not_found` row stopped naming a peer-invocation origin its own section forbids. `Action::"sidekick::manage"` now names two resource descriptors — node-scoped for the node-global definition CRUD, the named session for enablement — rather than one `Session` resource the CRUD operations carry no id for; Spec-012's enumeration stays at the two registered actions.
- Exit Criteria: Spec-030 and Plan-030 present at `approved` with every template section complete, Plan-030's §Preconditions plan-readiness-audit box ending in the literal `- [x]` marker and recording a first-time in-swap audit; Spec-006, Plan-006, Spec-012, Spec-016, Plan-016, Plan-023, Spec-028, and Plan-028 Statuses `approved → review → approved` within the diff, each with its restoring targeted readiness-audit delta on the same diff and its §Preconditions box re-opened and re-checked; Plan-028's born-unchecked effective-binding box ending in `- [x]` with T28.4.9 released; Plan-004 and Plan-007 recorded as **no-flip** (a `command_receipts` additive-nullable EXTEND on the Plan-005 `mcp_task_id` precedent, a seventh consuming-plan registration CP-007-15's own text admits without the obligation changing, and — added at the round-2 fold — a second Plan-007-partial-owned touch, the CP-030-8 `peerInvocationEnabled` population line in `handlers/session-read.ts`, which likewise moves no Status because it is a **sanctioned field-population edit rather than ownership**, the exact class the §2 map already records for Plan-006 T4.3's `timelineCursors.earliest` line in that same file); §1 / §2 / §3 / §5 rows present for Plan-030 and this node present in the §6 graph and node list; local SQLite 57 → 58, plans 29 → 30, and specs 29 → 30 re-derived by direct count in README.md and CLAUDE.md in the same PR, with Postgres 26 and accepted ADRs 28 unmoved.
- Landing-time note: the sibling `docs/provider-version-tolerance` vehicle (NS-85) landed first, as `27687c61`. This node was **rebased** onto it rather than merge-resolved, per the rule this line carried while that vehicle was in flight: the §6 census was re-derived by counting on the rebased tree, the `- [x]` marker flips were re-grepped, and the two §3 `Plan-028` dependency-row edits — that vehicle's `CP-005-11` probe-artifact clause and this swap's effective-binding discharge — were merged into one row rather than either side being taken whole.

- Summary: Two verified provider behaviors that Spec-005 and Plan-005 had left ownerless, both landing on **T3.11** — the task that already owns the normalize boundary's reorder-and-diagnostics band. **(1) Usage counters are cumulative.** Both pinned surfaces report a running total for the provider session that resets at no turn boundary, no compaction, and no resume, and both fold cache-read tokens **inside** their input figure rather than beside it. T3.11's unshipped telemetry producers would have emitted those totals per turn, overstating session spend by the conversation's length — measured **22×** on a long thread — straight into the `Spec-016 §Session Cost Receipt` committed-spend fold, so the defect would have landed on money rather than on a display. The new `provider/usage-delta-accountant.ts` emits per-axis deltas from **one base register per provider thread and axis, advanced in stream order**, attributing each interval to **the turn the metered frame itself names** — never a base snapshot copied at turn dispatch, which double-counts interleaved turns, and never whichever turn is open at arrival, since a usage frame for one turn routinely lands after the next has opened (the bind-at-dispatch discipline the turn-scoped `effectivePrincipal` already imposes on these same rows). Four edges are settled rather than left implicit: a **fresh** session — replay-seeded included — bases at zero, its first reading metering in full (seeding spends nothing; the first turn's spend is real); a **provider-native resume** bases at the daemon's own prior-emitted cumulative sum for that thread, never the first post-resume reading, so pre-resume spend is never re-metered; a compaction does **not** re-base (the provider's counter is unaffected, and re-basing would forgive every pre-boundary token); and a decrease on a declared-cumulative axis is a **falsified declaration**, floored at zero with a recorded diagnostic rather than emitted as negative spend. A wire-declared per-turn figure (the Codex breakdown's `last`) corroborates the derived interval and never substitutes for it, and the cached-input subtraction is gated on the breakdown's own arithmetic identity. **(2) A connection carries more than one thread.** Both providers multiplex subagent, review, and compaction child threads over the session's own connection, so a normalizer that projects what it receives writes a child's words into the parent's transcript and either double-counts or loses the child's spend. The new `provider/thread-frame-router.ts` classifies every frame by **family** against the pinned stream-surface census — thread-scoped families route by explicit thread identity, censused connection- and account-scoped families route without one, an unrecognized family with no identity still quarantines — registers the session's own thread at establishment and child identities from the provider's parent-linked announcements, holds a present-but-unregistered identity in a bounded pending-registration buffer (released on registration, shed with a diagnostic on timeout), **quarantines** an absent or unrecognized identity under a bounded oldest-first buffer rather than projecting or guessing it, and carves **both** usage and child-raised interactive requests out **ahead of** suppression — the requests routed through the same approval pipeline as the parent's per `Spec-016 §Provider-Native Subagents` and answered on the child's own correlation — so child content is dropped while child spend and child tool calls are not — provider-attributed subagent spend riding the already-registered (`runId`, `provider`, `subagentId`) triple, and provider-internal child spend (compaction, memory ### NS-93: Desktop-Console Parity — Compaction, Provider Commands, Output Speed, The Input-Ask Card, And The MCP Operator Page

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-08-29 — the in-swap flip-and-restore shape: twelve documents `approved → review → approved` within this diff, each restored by its own targeted readiness-audit delta riding the same diff, the runbook [§Status Flip Rule](../operations/plan-implementation-readiness-audit-runbook.md#status-flip-rule) path the NS-83 / NS-84 / NS-86 cohort established)

- References: [Spec-005 §Desktop Console Parity Surfaces](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md#desktop-console-parity-surfaces), [Plan-005 §Phase 4](../plans/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md) (decision #2's client-facing enumeration, T3.26, T4.9), [Spec-013 §Timeline Entry Types](../specs/013-live-timeline-visibility-and-reasoning-surfaces.md#timeline-entry-types) and [§Context Window and Usage Meters](../specs/013-live-timeline-visibility-and-reasoning-surfaces.md#context-window-and-usage-meters), [Spec-016 §Same-Agent Provider Switch](../specs/016-multi-agent-channels-and-orchestration.md#same-agent-provider-switch), [Spec-023 §Signature Feature Composition Sketches](../specs/023-desktop-shell-and-renderer.md#signature-feature-composition-sketches), [Spec-028 §The operator surface](../specs/028-mcp-server-configuration-and-governance.md), [Spec-006 §Driver Ask Events](../specs/006-session-event-taxonomy-and-audit-log.md#driver-ask-events), [api-payload-contracts.md](contracts/api-payload-contracts.md), [local-sqlite-schema.md](schemas/local-sqlite-schema.md), [security-architecture.md §Permission Matrix (Task 5.4)](security-architecture.md#permission-matrix-task-54)
- Summary: Four provider-console capabilities the pinned CLIs expose and this corpus had no home for, plus one operator page it had named only in passing. **(1) Participant-triggered context compaction.** `Spec-013 §Context Window and Usage Meters` has told a participant since it was written that their context is nearly full and that the system will not act on it, while offering them no way to act either. `compactContext` is that way: a capability-gated driver operation, `native` on Codex through `thread/compact/start` and `emulated` on Claude through a `driver_command` frame carrying the provider's own `/compact`. The hint is **reconciled explicitly rather than revised** — it stays informational and automatic compaction stays prohibited; a participant-initiated trigger is a different act by a different actor and is stated as such. The operation settles on the provider's typed compaction evidence and **never** on the request being accepted, because both mechanisms answer before the work is done. The Claude leg is the **first V1 producer of a `driver_command` frame**, which falsified `Spec-005 §Required Behavior`'s standing negative claim — that claim is **re-derived by count** against its two nearest candidates rather than restated, and because the arm is exempt from the neutralization tripwire the amendment supplies its **substitute guard**: pre-dispatch presence in the provider's own enumerated command set, post-dispatch typed evidence. **(2) The provider command and skill surface.** `listProviderCommands` reads both providers' own enumerations over the transport the driver already establishes. It is a **live read held as driver-session state, never a stored registry** — a deliberate decision, and the reason this capability adds no table and no column: a stored copy would need invalidation, staleness, and reconciliation machinery whose only purpose would be to re-derive what one read gives. Every entry carries the `(driverName, providerAccountId)` it was read under as a **routing invariant** enforced at the daemon, not trusted to the renderer: a Claude-enumerated command is never offered to, nor sent through, a Codex agent. **(3) The output-speed axis.** One pinned provider declares a fast-output state and the other publishes no speed axis at all, so this is a **single-provider** flag rather than a corpus-wide one, and the Codex `false` is a complete declaration whose analog is the `model` / `effort` axis `agent.configUpdate` already carries — nothing is emulated onto it. The axis is declared **`static`** rather than `probed` because reading the provider's declared state costs a user-message request and `Spec-005 §Capability discovery`'s admissibility test is conjunctive: **zero-turn** is the conjunct that fails. It reaches participants as `outputSpeed?`, a fifth provider axis on the existing `agent.configUpdate`, **spawn-bound and therefore resolving to a `run` boundary** — stated rather than left to the reader because it is the minority case on that mutation. **(4) The input-ask card.** The `driver_ask.*` family has been fully specified daemon-side since campaign B1 and named in no renderer surface anywhere; permission-kind asks already ride the approvals surface, but an **input**-kind ask had no home at all, so a provider blocking on a structured question produced a run that stopped with nothing on screen to answer. The card mints **no wire method** — the answer ingress is the already-registered client-facing `driver.respondToRequest`, whose `response` is unknown-typed — and one additive-optional payload member, `options?`, is registered so the card's structured-options arm is reachable rather than dead text; the free-text arm is **unconditional** precisely because exactly one of the two pinned mechanisms can supply a choice set. **(5) The MCP operator page.** `Spec-028` has carried eleven IPC operations, five event types, and ten error codes since it was written and named its own operator surface once, in passing, inside a bullet about a subscription. `Spec-028 §The operator surface` and a Spec-023 sub-sketch say what it renders, what it may not render, and which rules it is forbidden to re-derive — it composes the existing surface, takes `mcp.subscribe` as its update channel rather than reintroducing above the daemon the polling that spec forbids below it, and derives no eligibility of its own, because a renderer that recomputed effective idempotency class would be a second source of truth for a decision [Spec-015](../specs/015-persistence-recovery-and-replay.md) recovery depends on. **Two client-facing verbs are minted** — `driver.compactContext` and `driver.listProviderCommands`, taking that set seven → nine — and they are admitted by `Plan-005 §Phase 4 — Client SDK exposure + degraded-fallback` decision #2's own governing principle rather than in spite of it: both operate on an already-existing session, and neither establishes, restores, starts, nor tears one down. They differ from the R8 parity operations that decision kept daemon-internal in the one respect that decided those: those had existing client routes and these have none — and inventing a sixth intervention for compaction would widen `Spec-004`'s deliberately closed V1 control set, the NS-73 / NS-84 precedent. **One residual is recorded rather than filed as a backlog item:** the [provider-wire reference](../reference/provider-wire/README.md) family does not yet carry the `skills/list`, session-handshake-enumeration, or output-speed shapes this amendment verified at that family's own current pins (`codex-cli 0.150.1`, Claude Code `2.1.251`) — folding them in is an ordinary regeneration entry owed to that family's next pass, and it changes nothing any governance document here states. **Review fold.** The round's findings are adjudicated into the contract text of the same twelve documents rather than cataloged, and four of them narrow first-round claims. **The compaction wait is bounded and twice-terminated** — a per-driver declared bound and the run's provider binding ceasing to be live — settling `failed` on expiry, and the split it forces is stated rather than glossed: bounding the **operation** never bounds the **boundary's record**, so a compaction frame arriving after settlement still normalizes into `usage.context_compacted` exactly as an unsolicited one would, no boundary escapes Spec-004's rewind classifier, and the Spec-013 control's in-progress state clears on the **call's** settlement rather than on the boundary row, which is what keeps a settled-`failed` compaction from leaving a control spinning forever. `DriverCompactionResult` becomes a **discriminated union** whose `applied` arm requires `boundaryPosition` and whose `capability_undeclared` reason is **dropped** — an undeclared flag refuses at the static capability gate before the driver is reached, so keeping the arm would be a second, contradictory encoding of one refusal. **The command surface is settled as enumeration and discovery**, and the settlement is a contract consequence rather than a scope cut: C-18 refuses leading-`/` input outright on provider-bound composer paths, so an insert-then-send autocomplete would compose text the send path rejects; and the `driver_command` origin — the one origin exempt from the neutralization tripwire — is admitted only against post-dispatch typed evidence, which no arbitrary provider command supplies. V1 therefore sends exactly one enumerated entry, the compaction command through its own control, the "exactly one `driver_command` producer" count stays exact by construction rather than by promise, and a dispatch route is **named and gated** on C-18's escape plus a per-command evidence contract instead of left implicit. **The output-speed axis publishes its value set** as `outputSpeedLevels` — statically declared like the flag it accompanies (a vocabulary obtained by reading the provider would contradict the very conjunct that makes that flag `static`) and client-visible unlike `detectionSource`, because the control that offers the choice lives in the renderer — and it travels the **durable** switch record end to end rather than only the mutation, since a spawn-bound axis is the axis most likely to be pending across a restart and one the slot could not hold would be acknowledged and then silently dropped. **Authorization is stated rather than assumed, and mints nothing:** a non-participant is refused the already-registered `session.not_found` on both verbs — one byte-identical refusal for a non-member and an unknown session, so neither verb is an existence oracle — the enumeration needs only active membership, and compaction runs the identical `Action::"intervene"` evaluation `run.pause` / `run.resume` already share, its non-local hosting-node leg unreachable by construction because a binding this daemon holds is hosted on this node. Reuse of a row is recorded **on that row**, not only beside it: the [Security Architecture §Permission Matrix](security-architecture.md#permission-matrix-task-54) run-control row's subject now names compaction, and the `Action::"intervene"` coverage enumeration in [api-payload-contracts.md](contracts/api-payload-contracts.md) widens with it, so a reader who follows the citation lands on a row that names the operation instead of one they would have to extend by inference — the matrix gains no row and the enumeration no action. **The Spec-028 operator surface is corrected on three counts it overstated**: mutation is uniformly Cedar-gated but **not** uniformly trusted-server-only (a first observation upserts an untrusted binding, `mcp.setTrust` is reachable only on one, and safety-**tightening** overrides are admitted regardless of trust) nor uniformly audited (`mcp.reconnect` carries no dedicated governance event and `mcp.oauthLogin` is receipted and deliberately not evented); **state** is projected fail-closed while **eligibility is not projected at all** — no field on that plane reports it, so every control is offered and the daemon's typed refusal renders, which resolves the contradiction between the old availability sentence and the no-pre-filtering rule; and configuration content **splits three ways** rather than being uniformly withheld — operator-authored input the declaration form collects (credential-bearing values write-only in the renderer as well as on the wire), read-back that is exactly `McpServerConfigView`, and values the daemon does not serve, which are rendered nowhere — because a page that could render and collect none of it could not register a server at all. **Round-2 fold.** Eleven further findings are adjudicated into the same documents' contract text, and the core of them is one axis carried end to end rather than eleven separate patches: `outputSpeed` now **declares** (the driver's static flag plus its published `outputSpeedLevels`, served identically on the live and the cache-reconstructed capability read because the vocabulary is a property of the driver and is re-derived rather than stored, so the durable cache gains no column and `CapabilityDetails` is not widened), **spawns** (`CreateSessionParams.outputSpeed` with `ResumeSessionParams` re-realizing it from the durable `spawn_config` record, the posture precedent — without which an accepted switch would commit the column, settle its terminal, and start a process that was never told), **switches** (the coordinator supplies the committed value to the spawn in the same act that writes the column), **events** (`pendingAxes` at five axes, `from`/`toOutputSpeed` on `agent.provider_switched`, `attemptedOutputSpeed` and `output_speed_unavailable` on `agent.provider_switch_failed`, so the effective column is rebuildable from the log after the terminal clears the slot), and **reads back** (`AgentListResponse.observedOutputSpeed`, the provider's own declared state and its reason, projected live-scoped from the held session handle and stored in no column). That last member is the one the round demanded and the corpus lacked: a request is not a grant, and a provider that accepts the settings opt-in while its account gate leaves the mode off was previously indistinguishable from one that honoured it. The declared value is carried **verbatim** rather than narrowed to the published vocabulary — that vocabulary bounds what may be **requested**, and coercing an unlisted report to `off` would fabricate the very reading the member exists to prevent — and the disagreement is deliberately **not** a switch failure, since the switch applied and the provider then declared something else. Beside the axis: both console-parity verbs become **client-addressable**, taking `{sessionId, runId}` and `{sessionId, agentId}` rather than the daemon-internal `bindingId` no client-facing read publishes, each the identifier its own authorization and its own consumer already use, with resolution refusing in a fixed order on already-registered codes so a cross-binding request is **unrepresentable** rather than merely refused; the enumeration is **bounded at the normalize boundary** and returns the `ProviderCommandListResult` envelope whose `complete` flag keeps a cap-truncated read distinguishable from a small one, while `compactContext`'s presence check reads the driver's own held enumeration so a truncated read can never manufacture a `command_absent` refusal; the `driver_ask` `options` set is **bounded before append** — cardinality and per-option strings — so an over-large ask is dropped with a driver diagnostic while the ask itself still arrives, rather than passing schema and failing at the 32 KiB canonical ceiling with a run left waiting on a card no one recorded; the OAuth launch URL is settled **by destination** rather than by a blanket prohibition that would have made both clients' logins unimplementable — one carrier, the `mcp.oauthLogin` reply, absent from every durable and broadcast surface, consumed at exactly one place per client — and the Spec-023 acceptance criterion is narrowed from "no configuration value" to no **withheld** value, so the redacted read-back the same amendment requires for the edit workflow is admitted; and the T3.26 → Plan-012 Phase 1 edge that would have closed a cycle is dissolved by **correcting the ownership** rather than gating around it — the driver reports what the provider declared, and Plan-012 T2.8, the plan's only `driver_ask.*` emitter, is the member's sole writer. **Round-3 fold.** Six further findings, and the two P1s at the centre of them are the same defect twice: a fact the corpus had already established, asserted somewhere the establishment ruled out. **(1)** The declared speed state was carried on `ProviderSessionHandle` and `DriverResumeResult` — spawn returns both — while `Spec-005 §The output-speed axis`'s detection-source ruling, the section that makes this axis unprobeable at all, states that the declaring handshake is emitted only as part of a **turn-bearing exchange**. A session's creation resolves before any turn can begin, and a resume is a fresh spawn, so neither carrier could ever have been populated: the member would have been structurally always-absent, a field minted ahead of its producer on the NS-84 ground. It is re-homed as **binding-held state observed on the first turn-bearing exchange** — no synthetic turn spent, no establishment call blocked — and the projection becomes **absent-until-observed**, its absence acquiring a third cause (live, declaring, not yet observed) that is the one every freshly spawned binding passes through and that no reader may render as the mode being off. **(2)** The enumeration read was addressed by agent and answered with a flat array, but V1 admits concurrent runs with no one-active-run-per-agent gate, so one agent can hold several live bindings, each with its own held enumeration. Re-addressing by `runId` was rejected — it reverses the round-2 decision for the one caller that has an agent and not a run, and `runtime_bindings` is keyed by its own id with `run_id` on the row, so a run does not name a binding either — in favour of a **run-and-binding-discriminated reply**: one group per live binding, each naming its run and its `(driverName, providerAccountId)` and carrying its own cap, which stays total under concurrency and cannot hand a composer another leg's commands with the provenance stripped. `observedOutputSpeed` takes the same discipline as a stated **selection rule** — the agent's most recently established live binding, the only one whose spawn could have realized the requested value served beside it. ### NS-94: A Durable Encrypted Home For Machine-Authored Prose — `session_events.content_payload`

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-08-30 — the in-swap flip-and-restore shape: six documents `approved → review → approved` within this diff, each restored by its own targeted readiness-audit delta riding the same diff, the runbook [§Status Flip Rule](../operations/plan-implementation-readiness-audit-runbook.md#status-flip-rule) path the NS-83 / NS-84 / NS-86 / NS-93 cohort established)

- Summary: Assistant- and tool-generated prose had **no durable home in this corpus, encrypted or otherwise**. `assistant.message` and `assistant.thinking_update` carried `contentType?` / `contentLength?` and no body; the three live `tool.*` rows carried `toolName` / `toolCallId?` / `durationMs?` and no bodies; the only place that prose landed was the bounded-retention diagnostic tier, which [Spec-020](../specs/020-observability-and-failure-recovery.md) makes explicitly non-canonical and purges in `≤ 7` days. The gap was a **compile-time fact rather than a doc reading**, which is why it is settled now and not deferred: shipped `packages/contracts/src/event.ts` registers 25 `SessionEventSchema` payload variants, none of them assistant or tool, so both shipped driver normalizers resolve every one of these types `payload-variant-pending` and **forbid envelope construction** — and no variant could be registered, because the payload shapes named no member carrying the body and the corpus offered nowhere durable to put it. Two consequences followed. [ADR-029](../decisions/029-canonical-transcript-is-authoritative.md)'s ruling that the daemon's canonical transcript is authoritative for the content of a provider session stood over a log holding none of that content, a promise `Spec-005 §Canonical Transcript Export And Replay` already conceded when it scoped the transcript to what the Spec-006 taxonomy carries. And NS-92's `'turn_content_unavailable'`, minted for the **exceptional** unreadable turn, would in fact have fired on **every** assistant turn — a declared loss that is universal is not a report. **The settlement.** `session_events.content_payload` (BLOB, nullable) is a **sibling of `pii_payload`, not a widening of it**: the two columns partition one row's text by authorship, so erasing a person never requires erasing a session. It is sealed AES-256-GCM under a **session**-scoped content key — a random 32-byte DEK held wrapped in `session_content_keys`, the `participant_keys.encrypted_key_blob` custody shape reused rather than a new one invented (a master-key **derivation** was the round-1 design and was replaced at the PR #383 fold) — with AAD = `session_id || event_id` and wire format `iv || ciphertext || tag`. It is excluded from the canonical bytes and committed to by a payload-embedded `contentCiphertextDigest`, the existing Encrypt-Then-Digest-Then-Sign order re-run with **one** embedded member instead of two: there is deliberately **no owner-stamp sibling column**, because `session_id` is already a canonical signed member, so the sealing key's binding is signed already and a second column would restate a fact the bytes commit to — which is why this costs one column and not two, and why no `content_owner_stamp_unbound` check pairs with `pii_owner_stamp_unbound`. Two write-path rules are inherited rather than merely echoed: `pii-indirection.ts` stays the **sole** write path (both codecs in one module, so the order has one home), and the column is unconstructible for `audit_integrity` / `event_maintenance`, whose never-compacted / never-shredded invariant would otherwise leave a destroyable body no mechanism may ever destroy. **The bound is the honest part.** Unlike `pii_payload`, bounded in practice by human typing, this column admits machine-scale text — a tool result is routinely a file dump — so it is capped at `CONTENT_PAYLOAD_PLAINTEXT_MAX = 262144` bytes and an over-bound body is **truncated at a codepoint boundary, never refused and never dropped**, with `contentTruncated: true` and a pre-truncation `contentLength` recording it and no invisible sentinel written into the text. That truncation is a real transcript loss, so `DeclaredLossKind` gains its **sixth** member `'turn_content_truncated'` rather than borrowing one: `'context_truncated'` scopes itself to the memo budget evicting whole exchanges and never halves, and `'turn_content_unavailable'` would overstate a turn that is available as a prefix. **The disposition is deliberately not a crypto-shred, and says so.** [Spec-022](../specs/022-data-retention-and-gdpr.md) takes the full reciprocals the 2026-08-18 `interventions.pii_payload` amendment set as the pattern — a durable-tier map row, an export disposition, a place in the artifact-payload posture, and a retention statement — and places the column **outside** the participant-keyed fan-out: a machine-authored body is session work product co-owned by every member, so a per-participant sweep would blank other members' record of what the session's agents did. Under [BL-066](../archive/backlog-archive.md)'s exhaustiveness rule an unreachable path is recorded with its disposition rather than omitted, which is what the row does. It also declines to overclaim: with no per-row key there is no crypto-shred here and a NULL-out is not a secure overwrite, so the map says the ciphertext dies with its row — at compaction, at session purge, or with daemon master-key destruction — and does not say it is provably destroyed on demand. The participant's own erasure is untouched: `pii_payload` on the same rows still holds everything that participant wrote, under their own key, and Path 1 still destroys it. Two diagnostic-tier rows are re-described rather than re-scoped — `driver_raw_events` and `tool_traces` stop being the **only** home for provider and tool bodies and become a provider-native superset with a shorter TTL. **Ownership and dispatch.** Plan-006 owns the column on the `pii_participant_id` precedent (Plan-006-created via its own additive migration, not Plan-001 forward-declared — a digest inside canonical bytes is that plan's integrity protocol by definition), building it in a new **Phase 3B** supplement (T3.6, T3.7, T3.8) because Phase 3 merged 2026-08-04 and a merged phase is not amendable in place, under new invariants **I-006-3-05** … **I-006-3-08** and obligation **CP-006-15**. Plan-005 is the consumer and the reason the column exists, registering **CP-005-13** and one **task-scoped dispatch hold on T3.20** — and the hold's scope is the judgment: **T3.19 is deliberately not held**, its fold and export being correct over a body-less log, which is the state they were authored against, while T3.20 is held because its post-replay assertion is `Spec-005`'s only admissible evidence a replay worked and over content-free turns that assertion cannot separate a provider that accepted every frame from one that silently dropped them all. The migration ordinal is left unpinned (`0NNN-content-payload.ts`, the `received_from_node_id` idiom) because ordinals are claimed in merge order and `0012` is already claimed by an in-flight branch. **NS-92's four residuals, adjudicated rather than inherited silently.** (1) the Spec-005 step-1 (Fold) declaring clause and (2) the Plan-005 T3.19 emission leg and test remain **owed by the swap that registers the fold's emission**, which NS-92 itself named as their owner and which is in flight as PR #379 at this authoring; taking either here would land a new requirement on an open PR mid-review and flip Spec-005 to author a clause whose producer is being written elsewhere. What this node settles instead is the **condition** those clauses will name, because the condition is this node's own content: an unreadable `content_payload` is what `'turn_content_unavailable'` reports, and a `contentTruncated` row is what `'turn_content_truncated'` reports. (3) the daemon-side / driver-reported loss-list merge is unchanged and still owed by the same swap. **A third residual is minted here rather than left implicit, on the same owner:** `'turn_content_truncated'` is registered by this node but **emitted by nobody in it** — T3.6 writes the `contentTruncated` flag and T3.7 tests it, while the leg that reads that flag into `declaredLosses` is a fold-emission leg, exactly the class this node just declined to author. Left unsaid that would be a field minted ahead of its producer, which **NS-84** rejected on its own terms and which the discovery rule this same diff leaves standing in Spec-005 forbids. Said, it is a recorded disposition with a named owner: the swap that registers the fold's emission owes the `'turn_content_truncated'` leg beside residuals (1) and (2), and the vocabulary entry is registered ahead of it deliberately, because `api-payload-contracts.md`'s own rule is that a loss kind is an amendment and never a code-first free string — doc-side registration preceding its producer is the ordering that rule prescribes, not a violation of it. (4) the Spec-013 rendering residual is **narrowed rather than sharpened** — the member it concerns becomes rare where it was universal — so it is recorded and deliberately left out of the flip set. **Documents flipped and restored `approved` in this diff (five):** Spec-006, Plan-006, Spec-022, Plan-005, and — added at the round-1 fold for the never-backfilled exclusion — Spec-008. **Three recorded no-flips:** Plan-016 (the two `DeclaredLossKind` count mirrors), Plan-022 (the inventory rows), and Plan-008 (the exclusion is a prohibition, not a filter — no task changes, since a backfill chunk carries canonical bytes and this column is absent from them). **Spec-005 is deliberately untouched and takes nothing normative**, for the residual reason above. **Round-2 fold (2026-08-30, Codex PR #383 round 1 — eight findings, every one accepted and folded as normative contract).** Two were design defects rather than gaps. **(1) The sealing key could not survive erasure.** Deriving it from the daemon master key collided with [Spec-022](../specs/022-data-retention-and-gdpr.md)' rotate-on-shred, which mints a fresh master and destroys the old one whenever **any** participant exercises erasure: every existing body on the daemon would have become permanently unreadable, destroying co-owned session work product the erasure request has no claim on — the exact outcome the artifact-payload posture exists to prevent, reached by the key schedule instead of by the sweep. The key is now a **stored, re-wrappable per-session DEK** in `session_content_keys`, re-wrapped **inside rotation's existing `BEGIN EXCLUSIVE`** rather than in a pass of its own, because a separate pass would falsify that transaction's all-or-nothing guarantee. **(2) The column could never be written to.** T3.6's contracts work was two constants; the five body-bearing `SessionEventSchema` variants — `assistant.message`, `assistant.thinking_update`, `tool.invoked`, `tool.result`, `tool.error` — were owned by no task, so Phase 3B could have created and sealed a column no row ever used. They are now explicit T3.6 deliverables. The rest: **(3)** the byte-accounting statements must count this column (both of them, named — otherwise a content-bearing session reaches ~12.5 GiB before the count trigger fires, and the round-1 text's claim that the 500 MB trigger becomes binding was simply false); **(4)** a **sixteenth** verification mode `content_ciphertext_digest_unbound`, provenance-dispatched on `received_from_node_id` exactly as NS-58's fourteenth is, without which a ciphertext replaced after signing would leave the signature green and surface as ordinary transcript loss — a verifier `failureMode`, not a wire error code, so no error census moves; **(5)** a distinct **`HydratedSessionEvent`** read projection, since splicing a body into signed `payload` would either fail strict validation or mutate already-verified bytes; **(6)** the audit stub preserves `contentLength` / `contentTruncated` — a commitment to destroyed bytes verifies nothing, but _how much was destroyed_ is exactly what a stub is for; **(7)** the column is **node-local**, never relayed, joining `pii_payload` in Spec-008's never-backfilled set, with a peer's `'turn_content_unavailable'` recorded as a named residual whose closing swap owns the key-distribution leg — which the stored DEK makes possible and a derived key never could; and **(8)** the [Spec-022 §Data Export](../specs/022-data-retention-and-gdpr.md#data-export) claim is **narrowed rather than defended**: a participant mentioned only inside an encrypted machine body is not discoverable by the metadata selector, and the three alternatives are each worse than the limit (a durable participant→content index is a new PII path; a content-keyed selector returns other members' record; a decrypt-and-scan mints a DSAR mechanism with no producer). Findings (1), (4), (5) and (7) each **prevented a mechanism from being minted ahead of its producer**, the same discipline this node's own follow-up commit was paid to restore.

### NS-95: Per-Model Effort Vocabularies, The Re-Derived Non-Probeable Enumeration, And The Outbound-Answer Bound

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-08-30 — the in-swap flip-and-restore shape: [Spec-005](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md) and [Plan-005](../plans/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md) go `approved → review → approved` within this diff, restored by the targeted readiness-audit delta riding the same diff, the runbook [§Status Flip Rule](../operations/plan-implementation-readiness-audit-runbook.md#status-flip-rule) path the NS-83 / NS-84 / NS-86 / NS-93 cohort established)
- Type: `governance`
- Priority: `P1`
- Upstream: **NS-85** (provider-CLI version tolerance — the node that made capability a per-capability **declared detection mechanism** with an admissibility test, which is the machinery leg 2 re-derives against), **NS-93** (desktop-console parity — its round-3 fold specified the six detection entries for `context_compaction` / `provider_commands` / `output_speed` that take the probed count from two to four)
- References: [Spec-005 §Provider Parameter Vocabularies](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md) (leg 1's rewritten rule), [Spec-005 §Capability discovery](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md) (leg 2's re-derived enumeration and the AC14 dormancy corollary), [Spec-005 §Required Behavior](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md) (leg 3's outbound-answer bound), [Plan-005](../plans/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md) C-8 / T3.15 leg 3 / T3.24 / I-005-14, [api-payload-contracts.md](contracts/api-payload-contracts.md) `ProviderModel.effortLevels` (the third and last in-corpus carrier of the superseded lists)
- Summary: Three legs in one swap — two corrections of claims the corpus carried, and one new rule. **(1) Effort vocabularies are per-model, not per-provider.** `Spec-005 §Provider Parameter Vocabularies` asserted Claude `low | medium | high | max` and Codex `minimal | low | medium | high | xhigh` with no `max`, and Plan-005 C-8 and the `api-payload-contracts.md` `effortLevels` comment mirrored it. Both halves are false at this spec's own pins, measured first-party zero-turn on 2026-08-30 (**Binary probe**, **Verified**): Claude Code `2.1.251` publishes `low | medium | high | xhigh | max` on three of four models and **no effort surface at all** on `claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`, and codex-cli `0.150.1` publishes **three** distinct lists across eight models with **no `minimal` anywhere** — one of them, `gpt-5.6-luna`, carrying `max` without `ultra`. That row is why the correction is structural rather than a value refresh: no single provider-wide list is right for every model in the provider's own reply, so the normative rule becomes the one the driver seam already realizes — the vocabulary is whatever the model publishes on the provider's catalog read, carried verbatim on `ProviderModel.effortLevels`, **absent meaning the model exposes no effort selection**, with each driver's pinned declared catalog answering a composition that binds **no** live read rather than standing in for one that **failed** (serving a stale catalog under the appearance of a live one is the confusion the detection-source doctrine exists to prevent, so a bound read that fails propagates). **(2) The non-probeable enumeration is re-derived by counting.** `Spec-005 §Capability discovery` and Plan-005 T3.24 both named two entries — the `mcp` flag and the Codex rollback boundary. That was written when probing was expected to be the common case, and reality inverted. Counting the detection tables gives **thirty-four** entries over seventeen flags on two drivers, **four** `probed` and **thirty** `static`; the four probeable entries are all on the Codex leg (`steer`, `session_goals`, `context_compaction`, `provider_commands`) and the Claude leg declares **zero**, a measured finding rather than an omission — its one zero-turn channel refuses the outbound-raised subtypes _by name_, so a refusal there is evidence about the inbound dispatcher and not about the capability. Both sentences now enumerate the small probeable set and state the non-probeable one as its complement, naming the four failing-conjunct shapes (`mcp` on both drivers failing zero-turn **and** non-mutating; Claude `model_mutation` failing non-mutating alone; Claude `context_compaction` / `provider_commands` / `output_speed` failing zero-turn; the remaining twenty-four failing decisiveness). The spec additionally settles what AC14's negative control asserts on a leg that declares no probe — **declared and dormant**, re-arming the moment an entry there becomes `probed` — which was left vacuous by the shipped Claude table and is the kind of gap a count re-derivation is supposed to surface. **(3) An answer that will not fit the wire is refused, never truncated.** `Spec-005 §Required Behavior` gains the outbound-answer bound. The inbound line ceiling bounds what the transport will **accept** and said nothing about what it will **send**, so an answer composed from daemon-side content — a callback tool's output, an elicitation's structured content — had no ceiling at all, and an oversized write the provider's reader rejects leaves the ask permanently unanswered. Every driver answering provider-raised asks now applies an explicit outbound bound measured on the **encoded** frame the write step will send (never estimated, an estimate being a second disagreeing serializer); an answer over it is replaced by that ask's **own refusal shape** carrying a bounded **constant** reason — never a slice of what overflowed, which can overflow again and reintroduce by its own remedy the failure the bound exists to prevent; and every attempt that does not reach the provider (oversized, unencodable, or **write-rejected**) emits a driver diagnostic, retiring the swallowed write rejection whose justification was that the exit path reports it — that path records a dead process, not a named ask left unanswered, and a write can reject on a closed connection while the ask's caller is still waiting. The one residual is stated rather than papered over: where the provider's own request `id` is itself past the bound, the constant refusal will not fit either, nothing is sendable, and the **pair** of diagnostics is what says so — the ask is unanswerable, never _silently_ unanswered. Built by Plan-005 T3.15 leg 3 under the new **I-005-14** and realized in the in-flight Phase-3 wave-2b slice (in flight as PR #387 at authoring); this swap is the governing registration rather than a landed-fact record. **One residual is recorded rather than filed as a backlog item:** the [provider-wire reference](../reference/provider-wire/README.md) family does not carry the model-catalog read leg 1 rests on at that family's own current pins (`codex-cli 0.150.1`, Claude Code `2.1.251`): `claude.md` names `list_models` in its control-subtype census but records no result shape for it, and `codex.md` names no `model/*` client-request family at all, so neither file carries the per-model `effortLevels` vocabulary those reads return — folding them in is an ordinary regeneration entry owed to that family's next pass, and it changes nothing any governance document here states.
- Census: re-derived by direct count over the final files rather than carried. **No pinned axis moves.** No capability flag, driver operation, wire method, method string, event type, error code, Cedar action, table, or column is minted, so local SQLite stays **59**, Postgres stays **26**, plans stay **30**, specs stay **30**, accepted ADRs stay **28**, the Spec-006 event taxonomy stays **159** across 20 categories, the Spec-005 capability-flag matrix stays **seventeen**, the `ProviderDriver` operation surface stays **eighteen**, the client-facing `driver.*` namespace stays **nine**, and the driver error namespace stays **seven** (the bound's refusal travels as the ask's own refusal shape, which is a result and not an error envelope, so no code is registered). The counts that do move sit inside the Spec-005 / Plan-005 pair's own closed sets and are re-derived by counting the final files: `Spec-005 §Acceptance Criteria` twenty-four → **twenty-five** (AC25) and Plan-005's invariants thirteen → **fourteen** (I-005-14), with Plan-005's §Done Checklist and Phase 3 Acceptance Mapping mirrors moved in the same diff; Plan-005's cross-plan obligations stay **thirteen**, since no leg crosses a plan boundary. This §6 DAG moves 94 → **95** nodes, **93** `completed` and **2** `blocked` (NS-09, NS-10), beside the one `BL108` governance node.
- Exit Criteria: The `### NS-95` entry and its `NS95[…]:::completed` graph node present with the `NS85 --> NS95` and `NS93 --> NS95` edges drawn; `Spec-005 §Provider Parameter Vocabularies` carrying the per-model rule with both pinned catalogs transcribed and no provider-wide list; `Spec-005 §Capability discovery` carrying the thirty-four / four / thirty derivation, the four failing-conjunct shapes, and the AC14 dormancy corollary; `Spec-005 §Required Behavior` carrying the outbound-answer bound with its two closing properties, matched by two `Spec-005 §Pitfalls To Avoid` prohibitions and AC25; Plan-005 C-8 and T3.24 carrying the corrected claims, T3.15 leg 3 carrying the bound, `I-005-14` present and cited from that task's `Verifies invariant` line, and the §Done Checklist invariant line reading fourteen; the `api-payload-contracts.md` `effortLevels` comment carrying no provider-wide list; both documents' §Status cells reading `approved` with the flip and its restoration recorded in the Spec-005 amendment blockquote and in Plan-005's §Preconditions Re-open clauses and §Notes entry; and no census moved anywhere in the corpus.

### NS-96: The Codex Service-Tier Surface Behind `output_speed`

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-08-31 — the in-swap flip-and-restore shape: [Spec-005](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md) and [Plan-005](../plans/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md) go `approved → review → approved` within this diff, restored by the targeted readiness-audit delta riding the same diff, the runbook [§Status Flip Rule](../operations/plan-implementation-readiness-audit-runbook.md#status-flip-rule) path the NS-83 / NS-84 / NS-86 / NS-93 / NS-95 cohort established)
- Type: `governance`
- Priority: `P1`
- Upstream: **NS-93** (desktop-console parity — the node that minted the `output_speed` flag and the Codex `false` cell, and whose justification prose this node corrects), **NS-95** (the re-derived non-probeable enumeration — this node preserves its thirty-four / four / thirty derivation and its four failing-conjunct shapes unmoved, and leans on its measured zero-turn `model/list` read for the improved decisiveness reason)
- References: [Spec-005 §The output-speed axis](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md#the-output-speed-axis) (the adjudication and the re-arm trigger), [Spec-005 §Parity Capability Mechanism Grades](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md#parity-capability-mechanism-grades) (the three separated evidence grades), [Spec-005 §Required Behavior](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md#required-behavior) / [§Per-Driver Capability Matrix](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md#per-driver-capability-matrix) / [§Provider Parameter Vocabularies](../specs/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md#provider-parameter-vocabularies) (the other corrected carriers), [Plan-005](../plans/005-provider-driver-contract-and-capabilities.md) T3.26 leg (c) (the detection-rationale correction), [Codex wire reference §Output speed](../reference/provider-wire/codex.md#output-speed--a-method-level-negative-beside-a-service-tier-surface) (the evidence, folded in by PR #400, which flagged the divergence for adjudication here and adjudicated nothing itself)
- Summary: One leg, correcting the **ground** of a cell without moving the cell. NS-93 gave the Codex `output_speed` cell `false` and justified it with an absolute — that codex-cli "publishes no speed axis at all" — resolved from a census of the generated method root. **That absolute is false at the pin.** The `0.150.1` **default, non-experimental** generation carries `TurnStartParams.serviceTier` (emphatically not field-gated the way `permissions` is, so a default connection can set it) and a per-model tier catalog on `Model` — `serviceTiers: Array<ModelServiceTier>` beside a required-nullable `defaultServiceTier`, with the older `additionalSpeedTiers` carrying its own deprecation. The census was never wrong — 185 method strings across the four default roots still match no speed, fast, turbo, or accel member — it was **the wrong instrument**, and the corpus already says so in its own words: `Spec-005 §Capability discovery` holds that absence in a censused registry bounds availability from below and not above. The claim here is deliberately narrow. That rule governs how a **driver resolves a flag at runtime**, and the Codex driver resolves `static` from its table exactly as it must, so **no driver violated it**; what happened is that the spec's own justification prose did to a method census the thing the rule forbids a driver to do. **The cell stays `false`, on ground that survives the correction.** This contract's axis is conjunctive on a **statically declarable level vocabulary** and a **declared-state read**, and the pinned Codex surface supplies neither: `ModelServiceTier` is three free-form strings, so which tiers exist is runtime catalog data rather than schema; this corpus's pinned declared Codex catalog carries no per-model tier list; nothing on that wire reports a current tier back (`ThreadUsageBreakdownGroup.speed` is a usage-**attribution** grouping key and sets nothing); and the only speed-differentiated tier value established anywhere at the pin — `ModelServiceTier { id: "priority", name: "Fast", description: "1.5x speed, increased usage" }` — lives in **two upstream test fixtures read at the floor tag `rust-v0.141.0`**, graded **Upstream source, Derived** and deliberately not Verified. A `false` resting on a Derived fixture would be as wrong as one resting on a method census; this one rests on the two conjuncts. The three readings are therefore **graded separately rather than fused** on the parity row: the method-level negative stays **Verified** at the pin, the service-tier surface is **Generated schema, Verified** at the pin, and the tier value is **Upstream source, Derived** at the floor — the fusion of the first into a transport-wide negative being precisely the error corrected here. **The detection entry does not move, and its reason improves.** The Codex `output_speed` entry stays `static` with **decisiveness** as its failing conjunct — which is what keeps NS-95's enumeration exact, since that entry is one of the twenty-four — but the superseded reason (the driver's only zero-turn channel is the method enumeration, and this axis is a handshake-declared state rather than a method) is itself false now that `model/list` is measured zero-turn. The replacement is stronger on the same conjunct: a zero-turn channel bearing on this axis **does** exist and still cannot decide the flag, because reading a returned tier as an output-**speed** tier is a semantic judgment over free-form strings rather than a decidable read. **The re-arm trigger is named** rather than left as a vague later: a pinned declared catalog read carrying a speed-differentiated `ModelServiceTier` re-grades the cell by ordinary amendment, and that amendment owes two decisions this one deliberately does not pre-empt — whether `outputSpeedLevels` stays statically declared or becomes per-model catalog-carried like `effortLevels` (the static rule's stated justification is that reading costs a turn-bearing request, and that justification does not transfer to a leg whose catalog read is zero-turn), and which application boundary the axis resolves to there, since `serviceTier` is a **per-turn** override while the Claude mechanism this spec binds is spawn-bound and resolves to a `run` boundary. **Spec-016 and Plan-016 are not edited and do not flip** (the NS-91 `carries no mirror` precedent): their `output_speed` text is scoped to the driver that **declares** the flag and to the mutation's validation against the declared vocabulary, neither of which moves — no provider-wire rationale lives there. The sweep is completed in code as well as prose, and was widened once when a second pass found carriers the first had missed: the Codex detection-table `rationale` string, the Codex capability-flag / vocabulary / omission comments, the Codex and Claude capability-test comments, the shared vocabulary table's comment, the `DRIVER_CAPABILITY_FLAGS` `output_speed` comment in `packages/contracts`, and the Claude composition root's `observedOutputSpeedFor` doc comment all carried the superseded absolute and are corrected in the same diff, none of them a behavior change — the `rationale` field is consumed only by the totality guard's non-emptiness check. Two **non-governance** reference sections take a pointer-only repair for the opposite reason: `codex.md` §Output speed and `claude.md` §Output speed were already correct about the wire — PR #400 corrected them the same day it surfaced this finding — but each closed by calling the divergence an unresolved governing-spec question, which this diff answers, so each now names the adjudicating section. No wire fact and no evidence grade in either file moves. **One loop closes in passing:** NS-95 recorded as a residual that `codex.md` named no `model/*` client-request family; PR #400 folded both that family and this output-speed section into the reference file, which is where this finding surfaced.
- Census: re-derived by direct count over the final files rather than carried. **No pinned axis moves.** No capability flag, driver operation, wire method, method string, event type, error code, Cedar action, table, or column is minted, so local SQLite stays **59**, Postgres stays **26**, plans stay **30**, specs stay **30**, accepted ADRs stay **28**, the Spec-006 event taxonomy stays **159** across 20 categories, the Spec-005 capability-flag matrix stays **seventeen**, the `ProviderDriver` operation surface stays **eighteen**, the client-facing `driver.*` namespace stays **nine**, and the driver error namespace stays **seven**. The counts that a correction of this shape most threatens are re-derived and **hold**: the detection table stays **thirty-four** entries over seventeen flags on two drivers, **four** `probed` and **thirty** `static`, in the same four failing-conjunct shapes, with the Codex `output_speed` entry still among NS-95's **twenty-four** decisiveness failures; `Spec-005 §Acceptance Criteria` stays **twenty-five**; and Plan-005's invariants stay **fourteen** with its cross-plan obligations at **thirteen**, so the preflight Gate-4 invariant-reference census pin does not move either. This §6 DAG moves 95 → **96** nodes, **94** `completed` and **2** `blocked` (NS-09, NS-10), beside the one `BL108` governance node.
- Exit Criteria: The `### NS-96` entry and its `NS96[…]:::completed` graph node present with the `NS93 --> NS96` and `NS95 --> NS96` edges drawn; `Spec-005 §The output-speed axis` carrying the service-tier surface, the two conjuncts the `false` now rests on, the improved decisiveness reason, and the named re-arm trigger with both decisions it owes; `Spec-005 §Parity Capability Mechanism Grades` carrying three separately-graded readings with the fixture at the floor tag and not at the pin; `Spec-005 §Required Behavior`, `§Per-Driver Capability Matrix`, and `§Fallback Behavior` carrying no transport-wide speed-silence claim; `Spec-005 §Provider Parameter Vocabularies` scoping the static rule's justification to the provider it was measured on; Plan-005 T3.26 leg (c) carrying the corrected rationale with `static` and the decisiveness conjunct unmoved; a repo-wide grep for the superseded phrasings (`publishes no speed axis`, `publishes no accelerated`, `no speed or fast`) returning only two admissible classes — the dated provenance records that carry them (the NS-93 Spec-005 amendment blockquote, the NS-93 §6 node above, the NS-93 CLAUDE.md narrative clause, and the 2026-08-29 Spec-005 References probe entry) and the quotations of the superseded claim inside this correction itself; both documents' §Status cells reading `approved` with the flip and its restoration recorded in the Spec-005 amendment blockquote and in Plan-005's §Preconditions Re-open clauses and §Notes entry; and no census moved anywhere in the corpus.
