### NS-98: The Child-Run Incompleteness Marker, The Reasoning-Surface Principal, And Timeline Page Framing

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-09-01 — the in-swap flip-and-restore shape: [Spec-013](../specs/013-live-timeline-visibility-and-reasoning-surfaces.md) and [Plan-013](../plans/013-live-timeline-visibility-and-reasoning-surfaces.md) go `approved → review → approved` within this diff, restored by the targeted readiness-audit delta riding the same diff, the runbook [§Status Flip Rule](../operations/plan-implementation-readiness-audit-runbook.md) shape NS-93 / NS-95 / NS-96 took. [Spec-007](../specs/007-local-ipc-and-daemon-control.md) and [Plan-007](../plans/007-local-ipc-and-daemon-control.md) go the same `approved → review → approved` route in the same diff, restored by their own targeted readiness-audit delta riding it — owed to the fourth and sixth legs (the request-`id` bound, which is new wire behavior on that plan's framer, and the daemon-resolved principal, which mints an invariant, an obligation, and a phase), under the Status Flip Rule's new-invariant / new-CP / new-Phase and behavior-change rows. The two remaining Plan-007 touches keep a **recorded no-flip** on the NS-93 mirror precedent — the `MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES` declaration move and the barrier extraction — because its `register()` substrate and its framer are unchanged by them, the constant keeping its value, both enforcement sites, its exported name, and every importer, and the extracted module keeping `session.subscribe`'s behavior and its logged diagnostics byte-identical. The node number skips **NS-97**, which is claimed by the in-flight console-design amendment on a separate branch; numbering by count alone would have collided.)
- Type: `governance`
- Priority: `P1`
- Upstream: **NS-20** (the Tier-8 plan-readiness audit that recorded all three residuals — the marker and the principal as unshaped, and the Plan-007 dependency edge as undeclared in both directions — and explicitly did not clear any of them; this node is their named settling vehicle. NS-20's Plan-021 and Plan-023 edges stay open and are untouched here).
- References: [Spec-013 §Fallback Behavior](../specs/013-live-timeline-visibility-and-reasoning-surfaces.md#fallback-behavior) (the marked-incomplete rule the marker implements, now naming the closed cause set), [Spec-008 §Peer History Backfill On Join (V1)](../specs/008-control-plane-relay-and-session-join.md#peer-history-backfill-on-join-v1) (the `pending_backfill` coverage-state term this marker borrows rather than paraphrases), [api-payload-contracts.md §Authenticated Principal And Authorization Model](contracts/api-payload-contracts.md#authenticated-principal-and-authorization-model) (the class rule that settles the principal, and the enumeration this node repairs), [Plan-013 §Preconditions](../plans/013-live-timeline-visibility-and-reasoning-surfaces.md#preconditions) and [Plan-013 §Notes](../plans/013-live-timeline-visibility-and-reasoning-surfaces.md#notes) (the residual sites, each annotated with this vehicle), [Spec-007 §Wire Format](../specs/007-local-ipc-and-daemon-control.md#wire-format) (the 1 MB message-size limit every timeline page is now bounded against), [Plan-007 §Cross-Plan Obligations](../plans/007-local-ipc-and-daemon-control.md) (CP-007-16 — the ledger row for the registry, the streaming primitive, the frame limit's declaration move, the request-`id` bound, and the barrier extraction; and CP-007-17 — the daemon-resolved principal owed to Plan-013 Phase 3 and to every policy-aware namespace after it), [Spec-007 §Wire Format](../specs/007-local-ipc-and-daemon-control.md#wire-format) again for the `id` bound it now states, and [api-payload-contracts.md §JSON-RPC Request `id` Bound (Tier 1 Ratified)](contracts/api-payload-contracts.md) (the contract-doc registration of that bound, beside the method-name and `protocolVersion` registries it joins).
- Summary: Two legs, both settling residuals the corpus had carried unowned since NS-20. **(1) The marker.** `Spec-013 §Fallback Behavior` has required since it was written that a failed child-run detail fetch leave the summary row "visible and marked incomplete rather than disappearing", and **no member ever carried the mark** — the only signal was a low event count, which is indistinguishable from a child run that genuinely did little. It ships as a **required** two-arm `completeness` member on `ChildRunSummary`: `complete` carries nothing else, `incomplete` requires a `cause` and an `observedAt`, both arms strict, so a complete row cannot carry a cause and an incomplete one cannot omit it. Required rather than optional because an absent marker would be a third state meaning "probably fine", which is the inference the spec's rule forbids. The cause set is **closed at three** — what the daemon can actually distinguish — and **every member is a term the corpus already owns**: `detail_fetch_failed` is the spec sentence's own wording, `pending_backfill` is Spec-008's coverage-state term at the narrower scope of one child run's rows (the same condition, so reuse is accuracy rather than overloading; Spec-008 joins Spec-013's Depends On for it), and `compacted` is already shipped on this plan's own reasoning-surface availability arm. Three near-misses were checked and rejected with reasons rather than silently passed over: `session.history_backfill_unavailable` (a response-level code Spec-008 rules out **by name** for exactly this use — "the joiner's coverage state is `pending_backfill`, never this code"), `NodeState`'s `offline` (the _input_ to `pending_backfill`, not a synonym), and `RepoMountHealth`'s `unreachable` (mount-scoped, and its own module carries an explicit warning against overloading that word across axes). `observedAt` is required because two of the three causes are transient and one terminal, so a consumer cannot decide whether to retry without knowing how stale the reading is; and the row's event count on that arm is stated a **lower bound**. **(2) The principal.** Settled as the decision that `ReasoningSurfaceReadRequest` carries **none**: the caller is resolved from the transport under the class rule, whose opening sentence scopes every endpoint in that document to the authenticated caller and whose informational-body-fields bullet makes any participant-naming body field metadata Cedar does not read. The request stays `{ runId }` and its schema is strict, so a supplied principal is **refused rather than stripped** — a stripped member would let a caller believe it had scoped the read to someone. It is deliberately **not** registered as an instance of that section's numbered admitting-write list: instances (1)-(5) each name where a resolved principal is _retained_ on a durable carrier, and a read that admits nothing and writes no row has nothing to retain, so registering it there would widen a retention rule into a resolution rule and break the enumeration's own carrier taxonomy. The registration lands on the informational-body-fields bullet instead, zero-net-line. **Two pre-existing defects in that enumeration were repaired in passing** (doc-only, zero-risk, the Housekeeping Exception): its lead-in read "the four bullets above" where six stand, and `agents.pending_switch.admittingPrincipalId` had claimed to be held under this rule at its own §Plan-016 block since it was minted while never appearing in the enumeration — registered here as instance **(5)**, with the carrier classifier re-derived to admit a durable-JSON-slot member beside the three columns and the payload member. **(3) Page framing.** Codex round 3 on the Phase-1 PR surfaced the third residual and it is the sharpest of the three: `Spec-013 §Interfaces And Contracts` required bounded windows and cursor continuation of `TimelineRead` and required **neither** of `ReasoningSurfaceRead` nor `ChildRunExpand`, so both answered with a whole set. The substrate's message body is bounded absolutely (`Spec-007 §Wire Format`, 1 MB) and an oversized **response** cannot carry its own error — the shipped send path destroys the socket rather than answering — so an unpageable reply is a **dropped session** rather than a recoverable failure, and it is reachable from contract-valid data alone. Three rules close it across all three reads together rather than as three patches. **Continuation everywhere**: `afterCursor` in, `hasMore` out, `nextCursor` required on the continuing arm and optional on the terminal one — the asymmetry deliberate, so a caller handing a completed read's cursor to `timeline.subscribe` has one wherever the daemon does; the reasoning surface takes the split inside its `available` state only, the other three states having no entries to continue. **A bound on the encoded size**, checked once per reply beside the row ceiling. A cheap character-sum proxy was considered and **rejected as unable to deliver the guarantee it would claim**: `TimelineRow` mirrors the canonical envelope's unbounded `payload` record, so a summary-length sum bounds nothing; and even setting payload aside the worst case is **six** bytes per string unit rather than four, because the free-form string rule admits control characters and `JSON.stringify` escapes each to six ASCII bytes — a four-byte assumption would under-reserve by half on exactly the input that breaks it. The reply is measured exactly instead, with a page-fill helper giving producers a count the validator accepts by construction. **Page integrity**: nondecreasing sequence, expansion entries bound to the response's own `runId`, and no self-parenting child-run summary — schema refusals rather than renderer conventions, so a projection bug surfaces at the contract boundary. The frame constant gets **one declared home**, `packages/contracts/src/jsonrpc.ts`, with `local-ipc-gateway.ts` re-exporting it under its own name: a page builder outside the substrate now has to size a reply against the frame it will become, and a second literal would drift from the framer silently, the drift surfacing as closed connections rather than as a red test. That declaration move, plus the registry and streaming-primitive consumption, registers as **CP-007-16**, which also closes the Plan-007 half of NS-20's undeclared-edge residual. **Three further legs ride the same node**, each closing a way the rules above could still have been defeated, and two of them are what flip Spec-007 and Plan-007. **(4) The echoed request `id` becomes an enforced bound rather than an allowance.** The page reserve subtracted 256 bytes for the id the reply must echo and nothing enforced that number — `JsonRpcId` is a bare TypeScript union with no schema anywhere in the corpus — so a 900 KB id inside a 950 KB request produced a reply no page budget could save, and a caller could drop its own session with a request the substrate accepted. It is bounded at the **request** boundary rather than subtracted from the reply, because JSON-RPC makes the id the one response member no response schema chooses: `JSON_RPC_ID_MAX_BYTES` is declared beside the frame cap and the gateway refuses an over-bound id as `-32600` before dispatch, measured on the **JSON-encoded** form so escaping is covered and one rule reads identically across the string, number, and null forms. Enforcement is **two-sited and both sites are load-bearing** — the envelope's id gate refuses the request, and the id-extraction helper the `jsonrpc` and `method` gates build their error frames through (which answer _before_ the id gate) drops to Null, without which the one frame guaranteed to be small would be the one carrying the oversized echo. Stated as Plan-007's new **I-007-22**, with `Spec-007 §Wire Format` and two appended-last acceptance criteria carrying it. **(5) The subscribe-init ordering barrier becomes shared substrate.** `timeline.subscribe`'s binder had none, so a projection emitting synchronously during setup wrote notification frames ahead of the `{ subscriptionId }` acknowledgement — a violation of I-007-10 whose failure mode is **silent**, the SDK dropping frames for a subscription id it has not yet learned. The mechanism `session.subscribe` carried inline is extracted to `subscription-ack-barrier.ts` on its second use per the repo's hoist-on-second-use rule and both binders call it; the timeline binder hands its projection a **gated facade** rather than the raw producer, so a Phase-2 projection cannot bypass the barrier by holding the handle it was given, and `complete()` is gated alongside `next()` so a synchronously-completing projection cannot write its terminal state ahead of the ack either. **(6) The reasoning read gets a principal to evaluate.** Leg (2) settles that the request carries no principal member — correct, and it left the handler with nothing at all: `HandlerContext` exposes only `transportId`, and no task on any plan populated an identity. Rather than let a policy-aware read ship fail-open, the carrier is minted on its natural owner — Plan-007's substrate, the only component holding the transport's authenticated identity — as **I-007-21**, **CP-007-17**, and the explicit-label supplement **Phase 2B** (Plan-007 Phase 2 merged 2026-04-29, so it is not amendable in place; the NS-94 / NS-97 precedent). Plan-013 T3.2 is held by a born-unchecked, task-scoped box until that phase merges — deliberately not a phase-level entry, which would hold T3.1 / T3.3 / T3.4 for a dependency none of them has — and the class rule's local-daemon bullet in [api-payload-contracts.md](contracts/api-payload-contracts.md) gains the carrier sentence naming where a local handler reads that identity and what it must do while the provider is unwired. **(7) A reply is scoped to the request that asked for it.** Everything above constrains the SHAPE of a reply, and every one of those rules is a response-schema rule — and a response schema never sees the request. What survives all of them is an answer that is well-formed and about the WRONG SUBJECT: a read for session A returning a page of valid rows from session B, an expansion of run A answering self-consistently about run B, a live subscription forwarding another session's rows under the subscription id its client trusts. Each parses, each correlates to the caller's own request id, and no consumer can tell any of them from a correct answer. The rule is enforced at the daemon binder, the one place the parsed request is still in hand: the query binder wraps its handler and refuses before the registry sees the value, reusing the substrate's own `invalid_result` code — the identical condition one step further out than the registry can see — so the refusal lands as `-32603` with the offending coordinates in `data.fields.issues` and **no error code is minted**; the subscription binder gates each emission below the ack barrier, taking the cancel-log-stop posture a schema-invalid emission takes, which is the only posture available there because the acknowledgement it would ride behind has already settled and a notification frame carries no error channel. Both checks defer to the response schema when the shape they read is absent, so a defect that is also malformed is reported once with its real reason. Minted as **I-013-13**. **(8) Run-scopedness stops being decided by category alone.** Category was only ever decisive for `run_lifecycle`; the corpus registers run identity as OPTIONAL on every `artifact_publication` type, on five `usage_telemetry` types, and on `user.message`, so the same type is run-scoped on one row and session-scoped on the next and no type-level rule is correct for both. The `general` arm now refuses on three tests — the closed category, a census of the `Spec-006` types whose registered payload names a run unconditionally, and the row's own payload naming one under `runId` or the intervention family's `targetRunId` — with the census **derived from Plan-006's per-category arrays** rather than transcribed and its size pinned by a test, so a taxonomy growth that should change what the timeline refuses fails loudly. The `run` arm additionally refuses a payload whose echoed origin keys disagree with the row's own triple. Both land by extending I-013-1 and I-013-3 rather than by minting invariants, because both are the rule those invariants already carry reaching a place it had not. Legs (7) and (8) touch no Plan-007 surface — the refusal reuses a registered substrate code, adds no substrate file, and the handler-barrel export line is the seam five plans already append to — so **Spec-007 and Plan-007 are not edited and take no flip for them**. **(9) The paging contract is closed at both ends it had left open.** Leg (3) said what a page reporting more must carry and never what it must carry _at least_, so `hasMore: true` with a cursor and **zero** entries was contract-valid on all three reads — a promise of more that advances nothing while reading like progress, re-asked from the same cursor forever, with no member of the reply saying anything is wrong. The continuing arms now require at least one entry, and that forces the decision the byte budget had deferred. The page-fill helper returned a bare **zero** where the first candidate alone exceeded the budget, documented as a real outcome the caller was to treat as a failed read; with the empty continuing page refused, a zero has no representable answer left, and every caller had to remember the special case while one that forgot would ship the loop. The helper **floors at one** instead: the budget bounds **aggregation** and never bounds a page below a single entry, so the over-budget row is paged alone and the reply is refused **for its size** at the response boundary, naming the member and its measured bytes on a small error frame the substrate can deliver. Nothing oversized reaches the wire and the budget is unchanged — what moved is _where_ the undeliverable row is reported: structurally, on every producer, instead of in whatever each caller did with a zero. The reasoning surface's own non-empty floor is narrowed on the same leg, because it was stated as an absolute and is true only of a **first** read: an empty `available` page collapses onto `unavailable` while asserting the opposite when it is the first thing a caller sees, and is the only honest answer when the caller's own cursor had already reached the end, since `unavailable`, `compacted`, and `policy_redacted` each state something false about it. The floor therefore splits along the line leg (7) drew — the schema keeps the half it can see (the continuing arm, the one that can loop) and the daemon binder keeps the half that needs the request — which makes leg (7)'s check set no longer purely about a reply's _subject_, recorded on I-013-13 and in the binder's own header rather than left to be inferred. **(10) Two repairs ride the same fold.** The payload-attribution rule of leg (8) compared only `runId`, so an intervention row projected with outer `runId` A and `payload.targetRunId` B parsed and was then filtered, ranked, and superseded under A while its detail named B — the exact two-identity split that rule exists to foreclose, reached through the one spelling it did not read; both spellings are now compared, from the same exported key list the general arm's third leg reads so the two guards cannot drift, and on **every** arm carrying an outer `runId`, the compacted-stub arm included, which had carried no agreement check at all. And leg (7)'s correlation check, which runs one step before the response schema and is therefore handed unvalidated values, guarded the container (`Array.isArray`) and not the elements — so a page holding `null` threw a bare `TypeError` out of the dispatch promise, replacing the structured `invalid_result` envelope with an unmapped internal failure carrying no issue paths, which is the one outcome that check exists to prevent. It now tests every element it dereferences and defers **entirely** on a page with any unreadable one, a malformed entry being the response schema's finding and this check reporting it first only to report it worse. **(11) A page may not exceed the window the caller asked for.** `TimelineReadRequest.limit` is optional and a response schema never sees the request, so `entries` was bounded only at the global row ceiling: a read for ten rows answering with two hundred and fifty-six parsed, and a client sizing a viewport, a budget, or a render pass from its own request was handed a larger window with nothing on the reply saying the request had not been honoured. The effective ceiling is resolved per request — the caller's `limit` where it named one, the same global constant where it did not, which stays the default and the schema bound — and enforced at the binder beside the other correlation checks, the only layer holding both numbers; `ChildRunExpandRequest` declares no `limit`, so its ceiling is that constant, stated on the same binder so one rule covers both paged reads rather than two surfaces drifting apart the day either grows one. Legs (9), (10), and (11) land by extending I-013-3, I-013-11, and I-013-13 rather than by minting an invariant, and touch no Plan-007 surface, so **Spec-007 and Plan-007 are again not edited and take no flip**.
- Census: re-derived by direct count over the final files rather than carried. **No pinned axis moves.** No event type, wire method, method string, error code, Cedar action, table, or column is minted, so local SQLite stays **59**, Postgres stays **26**, plans stay **30**, specs stay **30**, accepted ADRs stay **28**, and the Spec-006 event taxonomy stays **159** across 20 categories. The counts that do move sit inside closed sets this diff owns: Plan-013's invariants nine → **thirteen** (I-013-10, I-013-11, I-013-12, I-013-13), its Phase-1 tasks four → **five** (T1.5) and its cross-plan obligations five → **seven** (CP-007-16, CP-007-17), `Spec-013 §Acceptance Criteria` eight → **nine**, Plan-007's invariants twenty → **twenty-two** (I-007-21, I-007-22), its `### CP-007-NN` sections fifteen → **seventeen** (CP-007-16, CP-007-17), and its phases gaining the **Phase 2B** explicit-label supplement, `Spec-007 §Acceptance Criteria` seven → **nine** by two appended-last criteria, and the §Authenticated Principal admitting-write enumeration four → **five** (a repair of an under-count, not a new application — the principal carrier this node adds is deliberately **not** a sixth entry, since it is resolution and not durable retention, and lands on the local-daemon-endpoints bullet instead). - Summary: `Spec-023 §Open Questions` has carried since 2026-04 whether any Electron WebAuthn module covers Windows and Linux, and `Plan-023 §Scope` recorded the consequence as an **accepted scope degradation** — "V1 does not claim cross-platform native platform-authenticator flows." **The question resolves negatively and the degradation is withdrawn rather than accepted.** No cross-platform Electron WebAuthn module exists: `@electron-webauthn/native` is deprecated on the registry in favour of `electron-webauthn`, whose own published description is "Cross-platform loader for native WebAuthn support **on macOS**" and whose sole implementation dependency declares `"os": ["darwin"]` — a packaging shim, not coverage. **Neither non-macOS leg needs one.** Windows exposes the public Win32 `webauthn.dll` API to any process holding an `HWND`, documented with no entitlement, package-identity, or browser restriction and with two independent non-browser consumers in the wild; Linux's only authenticator class is the roaming FIDO2 key that Yubico `libfido2` already drives, taken from the distribution package rather than bundled. The round-1 fold corrected the rationale this amendment first gave: no `libfido2` package ships udev rules and no supported Debian or Ubuntu release ships `70-u2f.rules` at all, so device access comes from the host's `systemd` / `udev` (≥ 244) descriptor autodetection, which the packaged `.deb` / `.rpm` declares — and that `uaccess` grant is a **seat ACL**, reaching no headless or non-seat session. **V1 therefore ships all three legs, native wherever the OS has a native surface**, with the macOS leg an **own-built** universal Swift N-API addon over `ASAuthorizationPlatformPublicKeyCredentialProvider` — Vault12 `electron-webauthn-mac` recorded as the reference implementation and rejected on two measured disqualifiers: it generates the WebAuthn challenge internally, so no assertion it produces is server-verifiable (defeating both passkey sign-in and the step-up re-authentication the Security Architecture requires), and its prebuilt binary is arm64-only and non-fat with no arch guard, so a `darwin-x64` install succeeds and fails at `require`. The Device Authorization Grant loopback is **restored to what `Spec-023 §Fallback Behavior` always made it** — the degradation for a host whose probe finds no usable authenticator or no PRF, on any of the three platforms — and stops being "the Windows / Linux path". **Detection is a per-host probe at ceremony time, never `process.platform`**, which selects a binding module and settles nothing else (new invariant **I-023-15**). **Codex round 1 folded fourteen threads into the same swap**, minting **I-023-16** (the preload bridge took renderer-supplied ceremony options and returned derived key material; it now takes no argument and main resolves server-issued options against the build-pinned RP), **T-023r-4-7** (the password-derived KEK custody leg `ADR-010 §Consequences` had already decided for no-PRF hosts), and a **fourth silent-failure guard** (hmac-secret output differs by user-verification mode, so an unpinned UV is a non-deterministic key derivation) — and correcting two of this amendment's own round-0 claims: the macOS probe named Web IDL members absent from the main process, and the Linux `uaccess` rules were attributed to the `libfido2` package when no supported release ships them, access coming from `systemd`/`udev` ≥ 244 instead. **Four claims this corpus carried are corrected against first-party measurement** on Electron 44.1.1 / Chromium 152.0.7977.65: (1) "Electron does not provide native platform-authenticator WebAuthn prompts on macOS, Windows, or Linux" is false for macOS since electron/electron #51255, backported by #51411 and present on the `44-x-y` branch V1 targets; (2) the renderer path is closed by **Chromium's origin allowlist, not by CSP and not by the secure-context test** — from the `sidekicks-renderer://` scheme registered `standard: true, secure: true` the renderer reports `isSecureContext === true` with `PublicKeyCredential` defined and still takes `SecurityError` from `navigator.credentials.create()`, so scheme privilege cannot open it; (3) the §Main Process Responsibilities bullet routed through "Electron's WebAuthn bindings", an API that does not exist for this path; and (4) the acceptance criterion demanded a **platform** authenticator on Linux, which no Linux desktop surface provides. **Plan-023 grows** the two binding modules and their tasks (**T-023r-4-5** Windows, **T-023r-4-6** Linux), a rewritten **T-023r-4-3** on the own-built macOS addon, the `apps/desktop/native/webauthn-darwin/` subtree with its §2 ownership row above — which also widens **I-023-8**'s renderer import-ban enumeration, since that trusted tree is a sibling of `src/` and neither the `src/main/` nor the `src/preload/` prefix reached it — two E2E spec files with two more re-scoped, and the `koffi` FFI pin (exact, floor `3.1.6`, MIT — per-platform prebuilt `optionalDependencies`, so nothing compiles at install and **no `onlyBuiltDependencies` entry is warranted**, with `asarUnpack` naming `**/node_modules/@koromix/**` explicitly because the binary lives in a sibling package, and out-structs copied with `koffi.decode()` because `koffi.view()` throws under Electron). **Three residuals are named rather than accepted wholesale**: the macOS end-to-end PRF verification stays [BL-108](../backlog.md)-gated on signing, entitlements, and an RP-hosted `apple-app-site-association` file (there is no localhost exemption on native macOS); no hosted CI runner can produce a PRF byte on any platform, so end-to-end PRF is a recorded manual matrix and CI verifies load, layout, prototype resolution, and the credential-free capability reads only; and the Windows Hello PRF build floor is graded **`Source`, not Primary** — it originates in a vendor blog, is corroborated only by a third-party issue thread, and the KB release notes for that exact build mention neither WebAuthn nor PRF — so **no gate encodes that build number**, the leg reading `WebAuthNGetApiVersionNumber()` and probing instead. The Linux leg carries one named re-evaluation trigger: `linux-credentials/credentialsd` landing with a TPM backend would give Linux a platform authenticator for the first time, and is an ordinary focused edit rather than a V1 gate. **Codex round 2 folded five more threads into the same swap**, two of which correct round 1 rather than the branch's round-0 text. **[ADR-016](../decisions/016-electron-desktop-shell.md)'s deciding set is re-derived by listing**, because round 1's ground for holding its Status — that WebKitGTK carries no engine-level WebAuthn — stops being a ground once every ceremony is shell-native and a Rust or Go host can bind the same three OS surfaces: the WebAuthn constraint is **struck** from the deciding set, §Synthesis's "the one constraint that cannot be engineered around" is corrected (this amendment is the engineering-around), and the §Decision Log entry enumerates what still decides with each item's evidence — the single Chromium renderer the console's single-number budgets and `@xterm/xterm` WebGL tier are measured against, the `browser` pane's in-process `WebContentsView` plus `webContents.debugger` CDP channel on all three platforms, `utilityProcess` over a Node main hosting the `better-sqlite3`-bearing daemon and its PTY-sidecar supervision, and the reversal cost of shipped Tier-1 code already bound to `app` / `BrowserWindow` / `contextBridge` — and then **states the Status outcome that list yields** rather than assuming it: the remaining set still decides, so `accepted` holds, and had it emptied the row would have moved the ADR to `proposed`. The sweep reaches §Thesis point 1, the §Consequences positive bullet, Option A's steel man, Options B and C point 1 (the WebAuthn gap **withdrawn** as a rejection reason), Assumption 1, and Revisit Trigger 1. **The macOS probe becomes advisory and gates nothing**: `canEvaluatePolicy(.deviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometrics)` is documented false with no Touch ID hardware, with no enrolled biometric, and system-wide after repeated failures, and a platform passkey ceremony still completes in all three states, so the platform provider is attempted on every host and the probe reads `.deviceOwnerAuthentication` as a diagnostic — a **direct** first-party availability answer may gate its own arm (Windows' UVPAA does), a proxy may gate nothing. **T-023r-4-7 gains the surface that makes it reachable**: main has no text-entry affordance and Electron's dialogs carry none, so the KEK leg opens a **secret-entry window** on the I-023-12 pattern through the same private `constructLockedWindow`, with its own preload exposing exactly one write-only operation that delivers the passphrase once and resolves `void`; it is not a `SidekicksBridge` namespace and not an auxiliary window, so that set stays at two. And two claims are corrected: `Spec-023 §Main Process Responsibilities` still returned the authenticator assertion through the bridge, contradicting I-023-16, and now resolves the typed `WebAuthnCeremonyOutcome` with main submitting the assertion over its own authenticated control-plane channel; and the Linux transport set said USB / NFC / BLE when `libfido2` has **no BLE backend under any flag**, so the row states HID plus NFC exactly and a BLE-only key takes the fallback path. No count and no census moves at round 2. **Codex round 3 closed the documentation cap with five more threads.** **Guard 4 is enforced on the response rather than the request**: a WebAuthn `userVerification` preference does not bind an authenticator — `discouraged` does not forbid verification and `preferred` does not establish it — so every leg now reads bit 2 (`0x04`) of the flags byte in the returned authenticator data (`WEBAUTHN_ASSERTION.pbAuthenticatorData`, `fido_assert_authdata_ptr`, `ASAuthorizationPublicKeyCredentialAssertion.rawAuthenticatorData`), compares it with the mode recorded at registration, and derives nothing on a mismatch, with each leg carrying a mismatched-bit fixture; the rule is deliberately not "require UV everywhere", which would refuse every non-UV key. **A binding that will not load became a third detection rule** — a negative capability result recorded as a diagnostic and routed to the fallback, never an unhandled rejection and never reported as a failed ceremony, since a host that never had a binding did not fail a ceremony — with a resolution-failure fixture per leg. **The macOS addon gained a build**, which no task owned: `swift build` per architecture joined by `lipo -create` into one universal `.node`, an `apps/desktop/package.json` script the desktop build depends on, a macOS CI step, and the `electron-builder.yml` output path, at the **Xcode 26.4** floor (Swift 6.3, macOS 26.4 SDK, itself requiring macOS 26.2+) set by the SDK because the security-key `prf` property is a 26.4 symbol, with the deployment target still macOS 12.0. **Implementation Step 9 was rewritten** off `WebAuthnPrfUnsupportedError` and refresh-token-only reauthentication onto the typed `fallback-required` arm followed by the DAG and then the T-023r-4-7 custody leg, which is what the round-1 fold had already made true everywhere except in that executable sequence. And **CP-022-3 got its producer back**: retiring `webAuthn.deriveKeyMaterial` left Plan-022's approved reciprocal naming a deleted method, so **CP-023-9** registers the main-owned `PrfKeyDerivationService` port — reachable from no bridge namespace, injected rather than imported, consumed by Plan-022's Tier-8 branch over the trusted shell-to-daemon channel — and Plan-022's CP-022-3 row, Tier-2 ladder pointer, and Tier-5 `Consumes:` line are re-pointed to it, Plan-022 taking an in-swap **flip-and-restore** because a cross-plan-obligation row changing its named producer is a contract-row change rather than mirror prose. This node gives the DAG a mechanical owner and admits the tool that owns it. **In Spec-023:** `§Console Libraries` gains a nineteenth axis, **structure enforcement** — ADOPT `knip` (a cross-reference to the Tests row that already adopts it for dead exports, scoped and gated here rather than re-admitted) and ADOPT-with-constraints `dependency-cruiser`, both scoped to `apps/desktop`, both CI gates on the tier-1 desktop job, run as two tasks with `--continue` because the claims are disjoint (reachability from an entry point versus whether an import may exist) and one red leg must not hide the other's findings; AVOID `jscpd` and AVOID `eslint-plugin-boundaries`, each with its measured reason. `§Console Test Tiers` gains one normative paragraph naming the DAG low to high — `core → tokens → routing → primitives → store / persistence → bridge → palette → frame → view families` — and stating that an upward edge is a CI failure, as are a cycle, an orphan module, a renderer-to-main import or its reverse, and an import from `src/shared/` into anything but the contracts package. `§References` gains **D.11**, the per-tool evidence, surfaced forward from a deleted research artifact. **Two AVOID reasons were corrected against primary sources rather than carried from the proposal that raised them.** `jscpd`'s is not merely that it is noisy: its documented `minLines` / `minTokens` minimums (5 and 50) are the size floor of a reported duplication, and the duplicates this tree actually carries are one to four lines — so it would miss the defect class while firing on the house style's near-identical block comments and deliberately parallel data tables; its publication record additionally carries a 557-day gap with zero releases in calendar 2025. `eslint-plugin-boundaries`' is **not** that its bundled `eslint-import-resolver-node` is active and cannot map `.js` to `.ts` — under flat config, which this repo uses, that guide states no resolver is active automatically at all, and an import no configured resolver resolves is classified `"external"`, so the plugin would fail **open** and silently on this tree's every relative import; making it correct would mean adding `eslint-import-resolver-typescript` for the alias map its own TypeScript-support guide requires, pulling the `eslint-plugin-import` resolver family into a lint stack deliberately kept core-ESLint-only. **In Plan-023:** **I-023-14 is widened in place** — the budgets and test tiers it already gates are joined by the two structure gates, so a console PR now also proves reachability and layering — and §Target Areas Build / Config registers the four files that carry them (`knip.json`, `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`, and the `AGENTS.md` / `CLAUDE.md` pair holding the package's structure standard). **No invariant is minted**, deliberately: an existing invariant already says "these gates run in CI", and a second one would split one obligation across two ids. **What the gates are, concretely.** `structure:dead-code` runs knip from the workspace root — a package-scoped run sees neither the pnpm catalog nor the root tooling manifest and reports both as findings — with `--treat-config-hints-as-errors`, so a pattern matching nothing fails the gate rather than rotting; its only admissible `ignore` entry names the task that will import the symbol. `structure:layering` cruises `src`, `build`, and `scripts` in one pass from the package root with `tsPreCompilationDeps`, so a type-only upward import is still a violation, and with an explicit extension list rather than `--ts-config`, because dependency-cruiser resolves a tsconfig's `extends` against the process directory and this tree declares no path aliases, so the flag would buy a cwd constraint and nothing else. `console-not-plan-subtree` forbids only the plan-owned subtrees whose owners **mount into** the console through `registerConsoleSurface`; it deliberately does not ban the three shipped Tier-1 components `Plan-023 §Target Areas` has the console absorb by import, because a gate stricter than its own plan is a defect. **Both gates were proven by negative control before landing**, each planted violation failing the gate by name and removed: an upward `tokens → store` import raised `console-layering-tokens`, and a planted unreferenced export appeared in the knip report by name. **Extended 2026-09-02, in the same node's console-substrate follow-on:** `Plan-023 §Console growth slate` gains a twenty-fifth row — the typed session snapshot read for a store's base state and the participant's session directory read, over the daemon method union, owned by Spec-007 (the method union) and Spec-001 (the `session.read` payloads) and consumed by session-store initialisation, the all-sessions list, and the auxiliary context picker — mirrored in the console's own in-tree ledger, whose two operations the fixture bridge now serves and the live bridge still refuses, which is what first lets the store layer reach a base state in any build. A registry row, and neither an invariant, task, phase, cross-plan obligation, nor ADR, so no Status moves (a recorded no-flip) and no census does either.

The one count that moves sits inside the flipped pair's own closed set: `Spec-023 §Console Libraries` eighteen → **nineteen** axes; NS-97's exit criterion records eighteen as the count at its own landing and is left as the dated provenance it is. ### NS-101: Typed Composite Refusal Guard — The Four Structural Guards Get A Wire Member

- Status: `completed` (born-`completed` 2026-09-06 — the in-swap flip-and-restore shape: [Spec-004](../specs/004-queue-steer-pause-resume.md) and [Plan-004](../plans/004-queue-steer-pause-resume.md) go `approved → review → approved` within this diff, restored by the targeted readiness-audit delta riding the same diff, the runbook [§Status Flip Rule](../operations/plan-implementation-readiness-audit-runbook.md#status-flip-rule) row-4 path this pair has taken since NS-67)
- Type: `governance`
- Priority: `P2`
- Upstream: **NS-67** (the rewind-hardening amendment that minted the atomic edit-and-resend composite and its four structural refusal guards — the guards this node types), **NS-75** (the replacement-send wire-arm registration, whose own census sentence recorded that the four guards "settle as `rejected` results carrying `rejectionReason`" — the free-form settlement this node gives a typed sibling), **NS-73** (the desktop edit-affordance placement, which authored T4.8, this member's named reader)
- References: [Spec-004 §Required Behavior](../specs/004-queue-steer-pause-resume.md#required-behavior) (the four-structural-refusal-guards paragraph and its new `rejectionGuard` clause), [Spec-004 §Acceptance Criteria](../specs/004-queue-steer-pause-resume.md#acceptance-criteria) (the atomic edit-and-resend criterion, extended in place), [Plan-004 §Invariants](../plans/004-queue-steer-pause-resume.md#invariants) (I-004-21, widened in place), [API Payload Contracts §Plan-004 — Queue Steer Pause Resume](contracts/api-payload-contracts.md#plan-004--queue-steer-pause-resume) (the `RollbackCompositeRejectionGuard` union and the `rejected` arm), `packages/contracts/src/runControl.ts#RollbackCompositeRejectionGuardSchema` (the shipped mirror), [Local SQLite Schema §Queue and Intervention Tables (Plan-004)](schemas/local-sqlite-schema.md#queue-and-intervention-tables-plan-004) (the `interventions.rejection_guard` durable carrier), [CONTRIBUTING.md §How Code Lands: Work Classification](../../CONTRIBUTING.md#how-code-lands-work-classification) (lane 1 — the amendment and its contracts mirror)
- Summary: The composite's **four structural refusal guards** have been normative since NS-67 and reached the wire as nothing but prose. NS-75 registered the composite's arm and recorded, in its own census sentence, that the guards "settle as `rejected` results carrying `rejectionReason`" — and `rejectionReason` is typed `string` in the shipped contract with no closed union naming the guards anywhere in the corpus. **Round 3 corrected this node's own premise** (PR #449): rounds 1–2 called that member a "free-form human sentence", and it is not — [API Payload Contracts §Plan-004](contracts/api-payload-contracts.md#plan-004--queue-steer-pause-resume) defines it as a "machine-readable cause on a `rejected` OUTCOME", the shipped `0015` DDL and `local-sqlite-schema.md` both call the column a "machine-readable rejected cause", and the shipped console renders it verbatim in a refusal `code` slot its own contract makes "never prose, never localized, never reworded between the producer and the screen" (`apps/desktop/src/renderer/src/console/core/refusal.ts#ConsoleRefusal`). The real gap is **openness, not prose**: [error-contracts.md §Intervention](contracts/error-contracts.md#intervention) deliberately registers no code for an intervention **outcome** ("`rejected` / `expired` / `degraded` are states, not error codes"; that namespace covers only request-level refusals producing no intervention row), so no contract anywhere enumerates the causes a rollback `rejected` may carry, and the wire type bounds length / whitespace / NUL at the trust boundary rather than fixing a value set. A client could therefore **show** the cause and never **switch** on it — a refusal family added later carries a new identifier every exhaustive read falls through, silently and at **no compile-time cost**. This node gives the refusal a typed sibling, and the correction **strengthens** rather than weakens the case: the justification now rests on a checkable type-system property instead of on prose fragility, and mints nothing new — no error row may be minted here in any case, since that registry rules outcomes out of the code space by design. **In Spec-004:** the four-structural-refusal-guards paragraph gains one clause registering the closed-union `rejectionGuard` on the composite's `rejected` response, its four literals — `'no-active-turn'` / `'no-pending-send'` / `'participant-authored-target'` / `'resumable-target'` — **derived from that paragraph's own guard names**, kebab-cased with the leading article dropped, so each names the condition its guard requires rather than restating the failure and a fifth guard amends the paragraph and the union together rather than passing as a free string; §Acceptance Criteria's atomic edit-and-resend criterion is extended **in place**, so the criteria set is narrowed rather than grown and no criterion is renumbered. **Two shape decisions, each stated rather than defaulted.** The member is **arm-scoped**, declared on the rollback `rejected` arm and not on the shared `InterventionResponseBase`: only a `rollback` request can be a composite and only a `rejected` composite settles on one of these guards, so a strict parse REFUSES the member on a steer / interrupt / cancel rejection and on every non-`rejected` state, instead of a base-level optional that would parse a guard on an arm that can never raise one. Within that arm it is **schema-optional and producer-obligated** on the NS-75 `resendDisposition` precedent, and for the same reason: no member of a `rejected` response identifies its request as composite (`replacementSend` is request-side and the response does not echo it), so requiredness is **not expressible** at the strict-parse boundary and is stated as the daemon's obligation rather than claimed of the schema. **In Plan-004:** T1.3 declares the union on the arm, **T3.17 is its sole producer** and carries the obligation — a refusal raised by one of the four always populates it, and every other refusal family the same handler reaches leaves it absent, so presence reads as "a composite guard refused" and never as "some rollback refused" — a claim its negative control makes checkable by being **total** over that set rather than sampling it (round 3): the **eight** `requested → rejected` families a rollback reaches, re-derived by counting [Queue And Intervention Model §Intervention State Transition Table](../domain/queue-and-intervention-model.md#intervention-state-transition-table)'s condition cell against T3.12's own enumeration — capability, authorization, target-position domain, compaction-boundary, incompatible target run state, the Spec-010 restore precondition, uncompacted-rewind-span, and execution-root `busy` — with that domain table's condition cell corrected in the same diff, having omitted the uncompacted-rewind-span family both Spec-004 and T3.12 carry — and **T4.8 is its named reader**, rendering the per-guard remedy off the literal and degrading, where the literal is absent, to `rejectionReason` alone rather than defaulting to a remedy that would attach the wrong advice to a refusal the composite did not raise. The member is therefore not minted ahead of a reader. **The round-2 fold gives the literal a durable home, and reverses a claim round 1 made without checking it.** Round 1 wrote that no column was needed because the guard was "derivable from the persisted cause on replay" — false, and false for the reason the whole node exists: `interventions.rejection_reason` holds an unenumerated cause vocabulary, so deriving the literal from it is exactly the match against an unpublished value set this member abolishes. And the derivation is not optional to get right, because a `rejected` intervention carries no `result` on the wire, so an idempotent replay of the same `clientIdempotencyKey` reconstructs its whole response from the durable row — which is exactly why `rejectionReason` was given a column of its own at campaign B9. The typed sibling therefore takes one too: `interventions` gains the additive nullable **`rejection_guard`**, written by T3.17 in the same write that settles `state = 'rejected'` and read back by T3.12's replay reconstruction, so a replay returns a `rejectionGuard` **equal to the recorded one** across a daemon restart — never omitted, and never re-derived by re-evaluating the guards against a run that has since moved on. Two shape consequences are stated rather than assumed. The `CHECK` is **column-attached rather than a table constraint**: `ALTER TABLE … ADD COLUMN` accepts a column-attached `CHECK` whose expression reads sibling columns (measured on SQLite 3.51.0, with a planted guard-on-a-`steer`-row, a guard-on-a-non-`rejected`-state, and an unknown-literal row each refusing), so the closed vocabulary **and** the `type = 'rollback' AND state = 'rejected'` binding — the at-rest mirror of the wire's arm-scoping — land together in one appended column and the shipped table stays off the 12-step rebuild; a `CHECK` in the table-constraint position has no `ALTER` form at all and would have forced one. And `interventions` **has shipped** (T1.4, PR #402, 2026-09-01), so the column lands by T3.17's own **next-ordinal** migration rather than by an edit of `0015` — the ordinal left unpinned here and resolved at that task's PR, the Plan-006 `content_payload` placeholder idiom — and T1.4's standing "no shipped migration exists to alter" basis is annotated as expired rather than left to mislead the next extender. No Spec-022 reciprocal is owed: the value is a daemon-minted member of a closed four-literal vocabulary, carries no participant content, and identifies no participant. **No invariant is minted**, deliberately: **I-004-21 is widened in place** on the NS-100 precedent, since an existing invariant already governs the composite and a second id would split one obligation across two. `rejectionReason` is unchanged on every path and stays the machine-readable cause. **Round 3 additionally gives the column its runner registration** (a P1 the Files list had left implicit): `migration-runner.ts` imports every migration explicitly and dispatches each from its own `hasMigrationApplied`-guarded `.immediate()` block — deliberately not a registry loop, because that module's header pins the `.immediate()` seam against the `worker_threads` concurrent-boot race — so T3.17's Files row now carries the same-commit runner EXTEND the dep-map §2 `migrations/` row already makes a registered class, its `migration-shape.test.ts` per-ordinal block on the `0017` precedent, and the `[1..17]` version-walk extension that is what an orphan migration file actually fails. The contracts mirror lands in the same PR — the union, its Zod parser, and the arm member in `runControl.ts`, with the accept case over all four literals, an unknown-literal refusal, and the arm-scoping refusal (a guard on a `steer` rejection, and on a non-`rejected` rollback state) as its negative controls.
- Census: re-derived by direct count over the final files rather than carried. **No pinned axis moves.** No intervention type, wire method, event type, **error code**, Cedar action, or table is minted — these guards settle as `rejected` **results** and never as `JsonRpcError` envelopes, and the six `InterventionState` values and the rollback disposition union are both untouched. **One column is minted** at the round-2 fold — the additive nullable `interventions.rejection_guard`, the replay carrier — and a column is not a table, so no table census moves: counted directly over the final files, local SQLite stays **59** `CREATE TABLE` statements, Postgres stays **28**, plans stay **30**, specs stay **30**, accepted ADRs stay **28**, and the Spec-006 event taxonomy stays **159** across 20 categories. The column consumes no migration ordinal **in this diff** — unlike the NS-77 / NS-84 unshipped-`CREATE` cases it joins a table that has already shipped, so the ordinal is owed by T3.17's own migration at that task's PR rather than absorbed into an unshipped statement here. Inside the flipped pair's own closed sets nothing moves either: `Spec-004 §Acceptance Criteria` stays **ten** criteria (the composite criterion is extended in place), Plan-004's invariants stay **twenty-five** (I-004-21 widened, not re-minted, so the preflight Gate-4 invariant-reference census pin does not move), its cross-plan obligations stay **sixteen**, and its task set is unchanged (T1.3, T3.17, and T4.8 are amended, none added). The one thing that grows is the wire vocabulary itself: `RollbackCompositeRejectionGuard`, a new closed four-member union on an already-registered arm, which no corpus census counts.

## 7. Maintenance

When adding a new plan:

1. Check the Dependency Graph (Section 3) for any shared tables or package paths with existing plans.
2. Add the plan to the Table Ownership Map (Section 1) if it creates or extends a shared table.
3. Add the plan to the Package Path Ownership Map (Section 2) if it creates or extends a shared directory.
4. Add the plan to the Build Order (Section 5) in the earliest tier where all its dependencies are satisfied.
5. Update the plan's header with a `Dependencies` row listing all inter-plan dependencies.

### Forward-Declared Table Migration Ownership

Schema-first plans (e.g., Plan-022 forward-declaring `participant_keys` and `session_events.pii_payload` onto Plan-001's `0001-initial.ts`) retain authoring ownership of post-V1 migrations against the forward-declared surface. The §1 Contested rows encode this split: Plan-001 appears as "Owning Plan (CREATE)" because it ships the Tier 1 initial DDL, and Plan-022 appears as "Extending Plan(s) (ALTER/USE)" because it originated the schema and therefore owns all subsequent `ALTER TABLE` work. Plan-001 must not author post-V1 migrations against `participant_keys` or `session_events.pii_payload`; that responsibility stays with Plan-022.
